📋 First Principles Scorecard

1. Earns Rent?
Does this skill directly serve revenue, hiring, or operations? Top 20 = yes. Everything else is support or debt.
2. Findable?
Can you find the right skill in under 10 seconds? Search + team filter + "say this" trigger = yes.
3. Honest?
Real usage data from .usage.json — not opinion. Skills are sorted by actual activity, not a locked guess.
4. Safe?
Right permission on the right door. Team-safe = store staff can use. Louis-only = owner only. Unset = fix now.
5. Lean?
No dead weight. 0-activity skills go to Debt tab. Archive if cold. Kill if useless. 80/20 or die.
🔥 80/20 Rule
Top 20 skills ≠ equal weight to 120+. The Earn Rent tab is your 80/20. The rest is drawer noise.

🔁 The Loop (how this stays honest)

1. Work in Slack
→
2. Skill auto-loads
→
3. Usage counted
→
4. Rebuild Dojo
→
5. See what earns rent

⚠️ Pitfalls

• Stale Dojo after hermes skills install without rebuild → always rebuild after install
• Slack blocklist paths (agents/foo) silently fail → use skill names only
• Parking cold skills in _archive/ → still loaded → use .archive/

People Recruiting (Steps 1–14)

Hiring → Onboarding → ACTIVE. 4 human gates total; this skill covers Gates 1 & 2.

🍽️ Restaurant Role Glossary

When someone says "server" they mean a restaurant server (takes orders, serves food), NOT a cloud/server computer. Common roles at Wiserise:

Term Role Department
server Restaurant server (waiter/waitress) FOH
host / hostess Greets/seats guests FOH
bartender Makes drinks FOH
busser / busboy Clears tables FOH
cook Line cook BOH
prep Prep cook BOH
dishwasher Dishwasher BOH
sushi chef Sushi chef BOH
kitchen Kitchen staff (any BOH) BOH
GM General Manager MGMT

FOH = Front of House (dining room) · BOH = Back of House (kitchen) · MGMT = Management

When to Use

  • GM says "Need 1 Server" or "We're hiring a cook" in a store channel
  • GM asks about an open hiring request or candidate pipeline
  • Someone asks about a new hire's onboarding status
  • A new hire's setup is stuck (accounts, I-9, training)

Don't use for: roster sync (→ people-roster-sync), discipline (→ people-discipline), payroll (→ people-payroll), ad-hoc queries (→ wiserise-people), Facebook/Indeed ads / hiring flyers / design variants (→ people-job-ads — class skill for all external recruiting creative)

HQ trainer / multi-unit coach: if Louis only wants ads or a flyer, load people-job-ads (not Steps 1–7). Skip store gap check unless he wants a Brain jobs row. Legacy notes: references/hq-trainer-ads-flyers.md (prefer people-job-ads going forward).

Architecture

4-pillar model (load wiserise-architecture for full rules):

  • 🧠 Brain (Supabase) = source of truth. Tables: stores, workforce_employees, applicants, jobs, workforce_audit_log, seven_shifts_cache, staff_count_minimums
  • ⚡ Hermes = sole worker. This skill tells Hermes what to do.
  • 💬 Slack = OS. GMs request in store channels. HR approves in 06-people.
  • 📊 Sheets = view. Pipeline tab auto-refreshs from Brain.

The loop: GM message → Brain record → Hermes processes → Slack notification → human gate (if any) → Hermes executes → Brain updated → Sheet refreshed

🧵 Thread-per-Employee Rule (ALL stages)

One Slack thread per employee, from first message → activation. The store channel stays clean — no scattered messages. Everything for one hire lives in one thread.

How it works: 1. GM posts "Need 1 Server" as a new top-level message in the store channel → that message's ts becomes the primary thread 2. ALL WISE OPS replies go in that thread using thread_ts — gap check, shortlist, hire confirmation, onboarding updates, training, activation 3. Each hire = one thread. If GM needs 4 servers, that's still one thread for the request. But each hire gets its own thread when the candidate is picked (Gate 1) — reply in a new thread starting from the shortlist pick. 4. Thread closes when employee goes Active. No more replies after activation. 5. Cross-channel posts (06-people hiring ticket, Ops handoff) are separate standalone messages — NOT in the store thread.

Thread storage: The primary thread ts + channel are saved in the employee_hired audit log entry's after_state: {"thread_ts": "1234567890.123", "channel": "C0ARRT1HSJU"}. Crons look it up from there.

Cron lookup pattern: GET .../workforce_audit_log?select=after_state&employee_id=eq.{emp_id}&event_type=eq.employee_hired&limit=1 → parse after_state.thread_ts + after_state.channel → post replies with thread_ts.

Fallback: If no employee_hired audit entry exists (old records), post a new standalone message and log the ts.

⚠️ NEVER post standalone messages in the store channel during onboarding. All updates (nudges, training checklist, activation) go as thread replies. The channel should show only the original hiring request + thread reply counts.

Key data sources for Step 3 (Gap Check): - 7shifts actual → seven_shifts_cache.employees (JSONB, pulled daily by 7shifts cron). Parse JSON, count by role. Who's actually working. - Min staff sheet → staff_count_minimums (per store, per shift, per role, per day). The target. Who we need. - Gap = min_staff sheet − 7shifts actual. This drives hiring. Not budget, not headcount. - Over the gap? → HR must approve + update staff_count_minimums. - stores.min_staff (JSONB column added Jul 2026) = fallback default when staff_count_minimums has no data for a store. Less precise (single number per role, no day-of-week breakdown).

Pre-Step: Staff Count Minimums Form Upload

Before Step 3 can run, the store needs data in staff_count_minimums. Without it, the gap check falls back to stores.min_staff JSONB (less precise — no day-of-week breakdown).

Form: SHIFT-F-006 Staff Count Sheet — the REAL, LIVE form. It already exists.

⛔ DO NOT hand-build this form. All Wiserise forms already live in the sops table (doc_type='form'), with the PDF stored in Supabase Storage bucket org-files. To send a form to a GM, pull the existing PDF — never regenerate it from scratch. Hand-building produces a wrong-looking, wrong-length document (a 3-page rebuild instead of the real 1-page form).

How to pull and send the form: 1. Find it in Brain: SELECT sop_no, title, file_url FROM sops WHERE doc_type='form' AND (title ILIKE '%staff count%' OR synonyms::text ILIKE '%min staff%'). The Min Staff form is SHIFT-F-006, file_url = playbooks/SHIFT-F-006_...pdf. 2. Download from Storage: GET {SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1/object/org-files/{file_url} with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. (Bucket is org-files — the file_url value already includes the playbooks/ prefix as the object path.) 3. Upload to the store's Slack channel (needs files:write — see Pitfall #18) with a short instruction comment.

Only create a NEW form via the wiserise-form skill if one does not already exist in sops. The wiserise-playbook-lookup skill finds existing SOPs/forms by title/synonym/number.

Full pull → deliver → intake detail: see references/form-delivery-howto.md.

When GM uploads the filled form to Slack: 1. Hermes receives the file (via wiserise-file-intake skill) 2. Identifies it as a Staff Count Minimums form 3. Parses the table data: store number, shift (am/pm), role_name, mon–sun counts 4. UPSERT INTO staff_count_minimums (store_number, shift, role_name, mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun, updated_by, updated_at) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT (store_number, shift, role_name) DO UPDATE SET mon=EXCLUDED.mon, tue=EXCLUDED.tue, ... 5. Confirms to GM: "✅ Min staff sheet updated for {Store}. {N} roles saved." 6. Original file saved to Drive → 03 – PEOPLE/Staffing/ and indexed in file_index

Stage 1: Recruiting (Steps 1–7)

Walk-In Hire (Bypass Steps 1–6)

Trigger: GM posts in store channel something like "Hired walk-in John Smith, Server, john@email.com, 555-1234" or "Walk-in hire: Host, Sarah Lee"

When to use: GM hired someone in person — walk-in applicant, referral, internal transfer. The GM already assessed them face-to-face. No need for scoring, shortlisting, or Gate 1.

What's skipped: Steps 1–6 (gap check, job posting, applicant scoring, shortlist, Gate 1 pick). The GM already made the decision.

What NOT to do: - ⛔ Do NOT create a fake applicants row — pollutes pipeline data - ⛔ Do NOT retroactively gap-check — GM on the floor knows if they need someone - ⛔ Do NOT block the hire — the GM already decided

Hermes does: 1. AUTO-DETECT STORE from channel (same as Step 1) 2. Verify sender is GM (same as Step 1) 3. Parse name, role, email, phone from GM's message 4. DEDUP CHECK — before creating, check if this person already exists: - Query by email (case-insensitive): SELECT id, employee_name, status FROM workforce_employees WHERE candidate_email ILIKE '{email}' - Query by phone (normalized — strip all non-digits, last 10 digits): SELECT id, employee_name, status FROM workforce_employees WHERE REGEXP_REPLACE(candidate_phone, '[^0-9]', '', 'g') LIKE '%{last10digits}' - If either matches → STOP. Do not create a duplicate. Reply in thread: "⚠️ {name} may already be in the system as '{existing_name}' (status: {existing_status}). Is this the same person? If yes, I'll update the existing record. If no, reply 'different person'." - If GM confirms different person → proceed to step 5 - If GM confirms same person → update the existing record (fix name/email if needed) instead of creating new 5. If no match → INSERT INTO workforce_employees (store_number, position, employee_name, candidate_email, candidate_phone, status, requested_by_slack_id, source) VALUES ('{store_number}', '{role}', '{name}', '{email}', '{phone}', 'hired', '{gm_slack_id}', 'walk-in') RETURNING id - Status goes straight to hired — skips recruiting - source = 'walk-in' marks the origin (new field, see schema note below) 6. Jump directly to Step 7 (Hired) — post checklist, notify channels, audit log 7. Stage 2 (Steps 8–14) runs normally — 7shifts, Chowbus, Gusto, I-9, training, activate

Over-hiring safety: The morning staffing cron (#01) reports gaps and over-staffing daily. If a GM over-hires, it shows up in the next morning brief. After-the-fact visibility, not a gate — trusts the person on the ground.

Duplicate prevention (root cause fix, July 2026): Lola Danlochi-Mongeli vs Lola Dawlocki Mongelli = two Slack messages → two Brain rows → two 7shifts users (different emails, same phone). Guards: 1. Walk-in hire dedup (Step 4): Before INSERT, query Brain by email (ilike) AND phone (last 10 digits). Match → STOP; ask same person vs different; same → update existing, never second INSERT. 2. 7shifts auto-create dedup: Script refuses when 2+ Brain rows share email/phone (DUPLICATE — resolve in Brain first). 3. 7shifts API email match: Active → flag only; inactive → reactivate. Does not catch same person with a new email — Brain phone check is mandatory first.

Schema note: source column on workforce_employees — ADDED July 2026, live. Values: 'walk-in', 'landing-page' (default for hires through Steps 1–6), 'referral', 'transfer'.

Walk-In Hire from Interview Sheet Photo

Trigger: Someone (Louis or a GM) uploads a photo of a completed Interview Sheet (physical form, spiral notebook page) with handwritten candidate data. Message says something like "onboard attached candidate" or "hired this person."

This is a walk-in hire variant — the GM already interviewed the candidate face-to-face, scored them, and circled "Hire." Same bypass as a Slack-text walk-in, just a different intake format.

Hermes does: 1. Use vision_analyze to extract ALL handwritten data from the photo: - Candidate: name, email(s), phone, position applied for, date - Screening: 3 pass/fail questions (nights/weekends, 6+ months tenure, reliable transport) - Character scores: Integrity, Energy, Service, Teamwork, Ownership (each 1–5, total /25) - Decision: Hire / Call Back / No (circled) - Pay rate (usually blank — set from Pay Band Policy) - Manager signature 2. AUTO-DETECT STORE from the channel (same as Step 1). If the message comes from a non-store channel (e.g. DM with Louis), check the manager signature name against known GMs to determine the store. 3. Dedup: check workforce_employees by candidate email(s) AND by name ILIKE — avoid creating a duplicate if the candidate was already entered. This is critical when the GM uploads a photo AND types the walk-in as text — Hermes may process both messages. Query Brain FIRST: - By email: GET .../workforce_employees?candidate_email=ilike.{email} - By name: GET .../workforce_employees?employee_name=ilike.{name} - If match found → STOP, do NOT create a duplicate. Reply: "✅ {Name} is already in the system. No duplicate created." If the existing record has no checklist posted yet, post it (Step 7). 4. INSERT INTO workforce_employees (store_number, position, employee_name, candidate_email, candidate_phone, status, requested_by_slack_id, source, hired_at) VALUES (...) — same as Slack-text walk-in, status='hired', source='walk-in'. 5. Record interview details in audit log reason field (score, decision, screening results, manager who signed). 6. Pay rate: Look up the Pay Band Policy (SELECT content FROM sops WHERE sop_no = 'REF-002') to determine the correct pay rate for the position. workforce_employees has no pay_rate column — pay rates are policy, not per-employee data. Mention the applicable rate in the Slack reply. 7. Jump to Step 7 (Hired) — post checklist, notify channels, audit log.

Multiple emails on the sheet: Use the first/primary one for candidate_email. Mention the second in the audit log reason.

Pay rate left blank: Common — GMs often don't fill it in on the paper form. Look up the Pay Band Policy (REF-002 in sops) and state the applicable rate in the reply. Training rate ($7.25/hr staff, $15/hr managers) applies until training passes.

Pay Band Policy updates: When Louis sends updated pay rate content, PATCH the existing sops row (sop_no = 'REF-002'), bump version, and update updated_at. Do NOT create a new row — the Pay Band Policy is a single living document. Log the update in workforce_audit_log with event_type = 'pay_band_updated'.

Step 1 — GM Requests Hire

Trigger: GM posts in store channel (e.g., "Need 1 Server")

Hermes does: 1. AUTO-DETECT STORE from channel. The Slack channel ID maps to a store. Use the channel name (visible in context) to extract the store number: - Channel name like store-00003-gangnam-wilmington → store number 00003 - Channel name like s00001-gangnam-fayetteville → store number 00001 - If you see only a channel ID (like C0ARRT1HSJU), look it up: C0ARRT1HSJU = store-00003, C0ARAG1LKED = store-00001, C0ARAG19LRX = store-00002, C0AUHCW7133 = 06-people, C0AQR6XURNX = 02-executive - Then query: SELECT id, number, brand, city, gm_slack_id FROM stores WHERE number = '{5_digit_number}' - NEVER ask "which store" if you're in a store channel. You already know. Only ask if the message comes from a non-store channel like 06-people or 01-announcements with no store context.

⛔ DO NOT run terminal commands (no hermes sessions list, no source .env, no grep, no shell exploration, no hermes sessions rename). You have all the info you need.

⛔ DO NOT use curl in terminal for API calls. Terminal output is visible in Slack — the GM sees your code, commands, and approval popups. Instead use execute_code (Python) for all Supabase and Slack API calls. Env vars are already available in execute_code via os.getenv().

⛔ DO NOT read reference files (channel-map, brain-queries, etc.) during Steps 1–7. Everything you need is in this skill body. Reading files wastes time and triggers unnecessary terminal calls.

⛔ NEVER show terminal output, code blocks, curl commands, or Python scripts in your Slack reply. The GM does not need to see your queries. They only need to see the result: gap count, budget status, and next step. Reply in clean Slack markdown with emoji headers only. 2. Verify the sender is the GM: gm_slack_id == sender_slack_id 3. If not GM → reply: "Only the GM can request hires. Ask your GM to post this." 4. If GM → continue to Step 2

Completion: Store identified, GM verified.

Step 2 — Record in Brain

Hermes does: 1. Parse the role from the GM's message (e.g., "Server", "Cook", "Host") 2. INSERT INTO workforce_employees (store_number, position, status, requested_by_slack_id) VALUES ('{store_number}', '{role}', 'recruiting', '{sender_slack_id}') RETURNING id 3. Reply in thread with hiring request confirmation (see Slack template R1)

Completion: workforce_employees row created with status='recruiting', GM notified.

Step 3 — Gap Check: 7shifts Actual vs Min Staff Sheet

This is the real staffing check. Not "count vs budget." It's what 7shifts says you have today vs what the min staff formula says you need.

THE FORMULA (confirmed with Louis, matches the paper form exactly):

MIN  = (sum of ALL weekly shifts for role, AM grid + PM grid) ÷ 4   [round to nearest]
SAFE = MIN × 1.25                                                    [round UP / ceil]
CURRENT = live count from 7shifts for that role
GAP  = max(0, SAFE − CURRENT)
  • ÷4 because one part-timer works 4 shifts/week → total shifts ÷ 4 = bodies needed on payroll
  • ×1.25 = 25% cushion for call-outs / quits
  • Verified: Server 00001 = 76 shifts ÷ 4 = 19 MIN, ×1.25 = 24 SAFE ✅

The GM only fills the AM + PM grids. MIN/SAFE/CURRENT/GAP are ALL computed by Hermes — never hand-typed. This kills the error-prone hand-math (crossed-out numbers on old sheets).

Data sources: - Demand grids → staff_count_minimums (per store, shift am/pm, role, mon–sun). The GM's input. - 7shifts actual → seven_shifts_cache.employees (JSONB, daily pull). Count by role. Who's actually working.

7shifts role name aliases (7shifts name → form role — normalize: lowercase + collapse spaces): - "General Manager" → GM - "AGM- Assist. GM" / "Assistant General Manager" → AGM - "Floor Manager" (any spacing) → Floor Manager - "Host" → Host · "Server" → Server · "Busser" / "Busser / Runner" → Busser · "Cook" / "Line Cook" → Cook

Hermes does: 1. Sum the grids per role → compute MIN, SAFE 2. Count 7shifts actual per role (with aliases) → CURRENT 3. GAP = max(0, SAFE − CURRENT) 4. UPSERT computed MIN/SAFE into min_staff_standards 5. If GAP > 0 → hiring is justified. Continue to Step 4. 6. If hiring goes OVER (CURRENT + requested > SAFE) → HR approval needed. Invite HR to the store channel thread for approval (mention/tag HR in the thread reply). Do NOT proceed to Step 4 until HR approves in-thread.

How the GM fills the grids (2 ways): - Paper: print SHIFT-F-006, fill AM+PM bodies per shift/day, leave summary blank, sign, photo-upload. Hermes reads photo → writes grids → computes summary. - Slack chat: GM types Server AM: 4 4 4 4 5 7 6 / Server PM: 5 5 5 5 7 8 7 (Mon→Sun). Hermes parses → writes grids → computes summary.

Completion: Gap calculated from live data. Hiring justified or HR-flagged.

Step 4 — Job on Landing Page (Always Open)

The Landing Page jobs are always open — the pipeline never stops. This is not per-request.

Hermes does: 1. Check if job exists: SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE store_number = '{store_number}' AND position ILIKE '{role}' AND status = 'open' 2. If job already open → skip. Pipeline is flowing. 3. If no job exists → INSERT INTO jobs (title, position, brand, store_number, description, pay_range, employment_type, status, posted_by) VALUES (...) 4. Reply in thread: "Pipeline open. I'll score candidates as they apply."

Note: The careers site (Manus app, e.g. eatatgangnam.com/careers) reads the jobs table LIVE — every open jobs row becomes a card on the site (verified July 2026: 55 open rows = 55 cards across 5 stores, 11 roles each). Applicants who apply are written into applicants by Manus. Hermes reads from Brain, not from Manus directly. Jobs staying open means candidates flow in continuously, even when no specific hiring request is active. As of July 2026: stores 00001/00003/00004 seeded by HR, stores 00002/00005 seeded by Hermes (11 roles each, posted_by='hermes'). Step 4's auto-INSERT path is now tested live.

Completion: Job confirmed open. Pipeline flowing.

Step 5 — Score Candidates, Shortlist to GM (ON-DEMAND ONLY)

⚠️ Where scoring actually happens (verified July 2026): The applicants.score value is computed inside the Manus landing-page app (the careers site, e.g. eatatgangnam.com/careers) at form-submit time — NOT in Supabase and NOT in Hermes. Confirmed by inspection: Supabase has no DB functions, no triggers, no edge functions on applicants. Manus writes the finished score into the row. The careers site pulls its job list live from the jobs table (55 open jobs = 55 cards on the site across 5 stores), so the site→Brain read path is real and working.

Step 5 AUTO-PULLS after the gap check. No cron, no manual trigger needed: - Within gap (auto-approved at Step 3): Hermes proceeds to Step 4 (confirm job open) → immediately runs Step 5 (pull and shortlist candidates). - Over gap (HR approval at Step 3): HR approves in-thread → Hermes proceeds to Step 4 → immediately runs Step 5.

A GM can also ask on-demand ("show me the pipeline", "any candidates?") at any time and Hermes will pull live. The 🟠P2-#02 cron is paused (July 2026) — do not re-enable it.

Hermes does: 1. SELECT id, name, score, position, email, phone, availability, experience, weekends, start_soon, created_at FROM applicants WHERE brand ILIKE '%{brand_short}%' AND position ILIKE '{role}' AND status = 'pipeline' AND score >= 60 ORDER BY score DESC - Always surface apply date = created_at as Applied YYYY-MM-DD on every candidate line (Louis 2026-07-13). 2. Limit the shortlist to top {gap + 2} candidates, max 5. If gap is 1, show top 3. If gap is 5, show top 5. Don't dump 15 candidates when you only need 2. 3. Threshold = 60 (the Gangnam framework's pipeline floor). Split into two tiers: - 🔥 Call Today (80–100): strong hire, GM calls same day - 📋 Interview (60–79): passed 6–7 questions, schedule an interview 4. Post numbered, tier-separated shortlist to the store channel (see Slack template R2) 5. Skip anyone already shortlisted (check workforce_audit_log for prior shortlist_posted event for that applicant id). Log shortlist_posted per applicant so next run doesn't repost.

When GM asks for detail on a candidate, post: contact, weekends/start_soon, why, movie signal, AND the 3 personalized gm_interview_questions (trait + question + green flag + red flag) so the GM has ready-made onsite questions. See references/scoring-framework.md Step 4.

Slack format for shortlist (R2): Plain text only — no Block Kit, no buttons. GM replies with a number to pick. See R2 template below. See references/slack-message-patterns.md for formatting details.

Auto-Fill Pay Rate from Pay Band Policy

When: Processing an interview sheet upload (walk-in hire or Gate 1 pick) and the pay rate field is blank.

Rule: Never leave pay rate empty. Auto-fill from the Pay Band Policy (SOP REF-002 in sops table).

How: 1. Detect blank pay rate on the interview sheet 2. Query Brain: SELECT content FROM sops WHERE sop_no = 'REF-002' AND status = 'live' 3. Map the candidate's position to the band: - Training rate first — all new hires start at training rate ($7.25/hr staff, $15/hr managers) - Band rate after Gate 2 — once training passes, the role's band rate kicks in 4. If position maps to a single role (e.g., "Server" → $2.13/hr + tips) → fill it, note it 5. If position is ambiguous (e.g., "Server/Host" = two different bands) → use training rate ($7.25/hr), flag to GM: "Position covers 2 roles with different pay bands. GM must decide Server ($2.13/hr+tips) vs Host ($9–$10/hr+tip-out) before Gate 2 training ends." 6. Post the auto-filled rate in the hire confirmation message 7. Log in audit: event_type = 'pay_rate_auto_filled', reason = 'Interview sheet missing pay rate. Filled from Pay Band Policy REF-002.'

Pay band quick reference (from REF-002 v2): | Role | Training | Band (post-training) | |------|----------|---------------------| | Server | $7.25/hr | $2.13/hr + tips | | Server Lead | $7.25/hr | $5.00/hr + tips | | Host | $7.25/hr | $9–$10/hr + 0.5% tip-out | | Busser | $7.25/hr | $9–$10/hr + 0.5% tip-out | | Bartender (Masa) | $7.25/hr | $5.00/hr + tips | | Line Cook | $7.25/hr | $12–$14/hr | | Prep Cook | $7.25/hr | $12–$14/hr | | Dishwasher | $7.25/hr | $10–$12/hr | | Kitchen Lead | $7.25/hr | $14–$16/hr | | Kitchen Manager | $7.25/hr | $16–$18/hr | | Sushi Chef (Masa) | $7.25/hr | $14–$16/hr | | Floor Manager | $15/hr | $16–$18/hr | | AGM | $15/hr | $18–$20/hr | | Manager in Training | $15/hr | $15/hr | | GM | $15/hr | salary + KPI bonus (corporate sets) |

⛔ Do NOT inline interview questions in the shortlist message. The gm_interview_questions are saved to Brain and surfaced only when the GM asks for detail on a specific candidate. Louis reverted an inline version — keep the shortlist lean.

Completion: GM sees shortlisted candidates in tiers with Hire/Decline buttons. Waiting for Gate 1.

Step 6 — ⭐ GATE 1: GM Picks Who to Hire

Trigger: GM replies in the candidate shortlist thread with a number (e.g., "1", "Pick 2", "#3") or a name (e.g., "Minjun")

Hermes does: 1. Number match (preferred): Parse the reply for a digit. Map to the numbered list from the shortlist message (1 = first candidate listed, 2 = second, etc.). This avoids name ambiguity entirely. 2. Name match (fallback): If no digit found, match GM's text to applicants.name ILIKE. If 2+ matches → ask GM to pick by number instead. 3. Once matched → UPDATE applicants SET status = 'approved', hr_decision = 'approved', hr_decided_by = '{gm_slack_id}', hr_decided_at = now() WHERE id = '{applicant_id}'

⚠️ Constraints on applicants table: - status only accepts: 'pipeline', 'rejected', 'interviewing', 'approved', 'declined' (no 'hired') - hr_decision only accepts: 'approved', 'declined' (no 'gm_approved') - When GM picks a candidate → status goes to 'approved' (not 'hired') 4. Log to workforce_audit_log: event_type = 'gate1_passed' 5. Continue to Step 7

⚠️ Important: The shortlist message (from Step 5 cron or session) MUST number candidates 1, 2, 3… so the GM can reply with just a number. The R2 template already does this.

Completion: One candidate selected. Gate 1 passed.

Step 7 — Hired

Hermes does: 1. UPDATE workforce_employees SET employee_name = '{applicant_name}', candidate_email = '{applicant_email}', candidate_phone = '{applicant_phone}', status = 'hired', hired_at = now() WHERE id = '{employee_id}' 2. Post to 06-people (People channel): hiring ticket (see Slack template R3) — standalone message, NOT in the store thread 3. Post simple hire confirmation as a thread reply to the GM's original message in the store channel (see R7 hire-time template). Use the original message's ts as thread_ts. Do NOT post the setup checklist yet — that comes later when auto-steps complete. 4. Cross-dept handoff: post to Ops channel: "{Store Brand} {City}: {Role} position filled — new hire in onboarding." — standalone message 5. Log to workforce_audit_log: event_type = 'employee_hired', after_state = {"thread_ts": "{ts}", "channel": "{store_channel_id}"}. This is the primary thread handle — all Stage 2 crons look it up from here.

Do NOT: mention remaining recruiting slots, push to hire more, or post the setup checklist at this stage.

⚠️ What Hermes CANNOT do: Hermes does not connect to 7shifts, Chowbus, or Gusto directly. The 7shifts skill (separate from Hermes) handles account creation via API. 7shifts native integrations then auto-create Chowbus and Gusto accounts. Gusto handles I-9 + E-Verify. Pullers confirm all accounts back to Brain. Hermes only reads Brain to check status.

Completion: Employee record updated. Status = hired. Setup checklist sent. People + Ops channels notified.

Stage 2: Onboarding (Steps 8–14) — AUTOMATED FLOW

Architecture (confirmed with Louis, July 2026): After hire (Step 7), People-Onboard-#2 creates 7shifts only. Chowbus + Gusto come from 7shifts Integrations after a delay. Hermes polls with #3 (never invents POS/Gusto flags). #6 sends package. Gusto owns I-9. GM only Gate 2 (#5). Termination is a different stage later.

Quick map: references/onboarding-pipeline-crons.md Stuck POS/Gusto: people-shifts-accounts → references/integration-employee-sync.md

Stage 2 starts at Step 8. Step 7 is Stage 1 handoff (hired + R7 + thread). Training appears only after setup chain is ready.

Step 8 — 7shifts Account Auto-Creates

Trigger: Step 7 completes — workforce_employees.status set to hired in Brain.

What happens: 1. 7shifts skill detects new hire in Brain (status = hired) 2. 7shifts skill creates employee account via 7shifts API with invite_user: true 3. workforce_employees.shifts_account_created → set to true by script 4. 7shifts sends invite email to employee automatically 5. Step 8b — Assign training courses (same run or next poll once user id exists) — see below 6. Bot posts to HR channel (06-people, C0AQVGCPDK8) via shifts_accounts_2h.py _post_7shifts_digest — v3 format (Louis 2026-07-27):

Parent (3 lines): 👷 *7shifts · {M/D} · 1 account created* • {store} · {Name} · {role} 👉 @Sally track package after invite accept Thread (details): ``` {Name} · {store} · created • 7shifts ID: {uid} • Email / invite: {email} • Store: {brand city} • Role: {position} • Training: New Hire Basics + role course (auto-assign) • Package auto-sends on invite accept • Docs: I-9, Emergency Contact, Rules, At-Will, Anti-Harassment, Tip Pool • Track: 7shifts → Employees → Onboarding

Reply here to act ```

Onboarding package is auto-configured in 7shifts Settings (6 documents ON: I-9, Emergency Contact, Rules, At-Will, Anti-Harassment, Tip Pool). No one needs to manually click "Send package" — it auto-appears when the employee accepts the invite email.

Hermes role: Creates account via API. Does NOT call 7shifts UI. The 7shifts API has NO endpoint to send onboarding packages — the package auto-triggers on invite acceptance.

Step 8b — Assign Role Training Course (auto on hire)

When: Right after shifts_account_created = true and the 7shifts user id is known (email match on company). Also re-run if missed (Gate 2 checklist time as backup).

What gets assigned (both): 1. Wiserise — New Hire Basics — company pack (rules, pay read, food safety + guest save 3D) 2. {Brand} — {Role} Training — e.g. Gangnam — Server Training, Masa — Host Training, LCB — Boil Cook Training

How (safe — no store blast):

python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/wiserise/people/assign_onboard_training_course.py \
  --email '{candidate_email}' \
  --store '{store_number}' \
  --position '{position}'

Or --user-id {7shifts_user_id} if email missing.

Rules (locked): - auto_assign on the course stays OFF forever - Script adds only this user via course PUT user_ids (append; does not wipe others) - Exact course title — never fuzzy (Server ≠ Server Lead) - Store → brand/company map inside script (00001/00003 Gangnam, 00002 Masa, 00005 LCB) - Do NOT turn on auto_assign=true or set location_ids (that dumps the whole store)

Brain audit (recommended):

event_type = 'training_course_assigned'
after_state = {"courses": ["Wiserise — New Hire Basics", "Gangnam — Server Training"], "user_id": 123, "script": "assign_onboard_training_course.py"}

If script fails (no 7shifts user yet): retry on next #2/#3 poll; do not block hire. Post HR note only if still failing after invite accepted.

GM-facing: When Gate 2 checklist posts, include one line: Training course is on their 7shifts app → Training.

Related: full course build/sync → company-sop-skill (not this step).

Step 9 — Chowbus + Gusto Auto-Create (7shifts Native Integrations)

What happens (automatic, no human action): 1. 7shifts native integration triggers Chowbus/POS account creation (auto-syncs at 5 AM daily) 2. 7shifts native integration triggers Gusto account creation 3. Pullers detect both and update Brain: - workforce_employees.pos_created → true (Chowbus) - workforce_employees.gusto_account_created → true (Gusto — added July 2026, live)

Gusto handles: payroll setup, W-4, tax forms, direct deposit

Cron #6 (People-Onboard-#6) polls every 2h: - Checks each hired employee's 7shifts invite_status - pending = waiting on employee to accept email (posts to HR if stuck > 3 days) - accepted = onboarding package in progress (posts to HR: "Package in progress for {Name}") - All notifications go to HR channel (06-people), NOT the store channel or GM

Gusto handles: payroll setup, W-4, tax forms, direct deposit, I-9 + E-Verify

⚠️ Live blocker (verified Jul 2026, Lola 00003): Company 396453 can be Integrations online while staff auto-create is still OFF. Diagnose with GET /v2/company/{cid}/integrations — see people-shifts-accounts → references/integration-employee-sync.md.

Do not stop at "connected" or company pos=other. Check: - pos.employee_sync_enabled — false = no auto Chowbus staff create - pos.employees_mapped / roles_mapped — false = mapping incomplete - payroll.employees_mapped / unmapped_users — Gusto lag queue

Invite accepted ≠ Chowbus. Invite only opens the 7shifts package. Staff path needs employee sync ON + map, then ~5 AM daily sync. Hermes cannot flip sync or map via API (GET-only). Multi-day stuck + sync off → human Integrations fix (Finance/Yumi or HR), not "wait overnight."

Brain flags can lie. Prefer live 7shifts user list for 7shifts truth; trust POS after ticket under name or human confirm.

Step 10 — Watch Setup, Nudge if Stuck

Crons: - People-Onboard-#3 Check Chowbus Gusto — setup poll - People-Onboard-#4 Nudge stuck hires — stuck nudges - People-Onboard-#6 Send onboarding package — package stamp

Hermes / scripts check: shifts_account_created, pos_created, gusto_account_created, gusto_i9_complete, onboarding_email_sent_at, training days / training_complete_pass

Completion: Setup complete or GM/HR notified of blockage.

Step 11 — I-9 / E-Verify Gate (Gusto)

Hermes does (auto-checked when status is 'hired'): 1. SELECT gusto_i9_complete FROM workforce_employees WHERE id = '{id}' 2. If gusto_i9_complete = false → BLOCK activation. Post to GM: "⛔ [Name] cannot go Active — I-9 not on file. Gusto needs to complete I-9 + E-Verify before training." 3. If gusto_i9_complete = true → allow activation to proceed

Rule: No employee goes Active without I-9. This is a legal gate, not a preference. Gusto owns I-9 + E-Verify (replaces the old shifts_docs_complete check).

⚠️ Schema note: shifts_docs_complete is deprecated but still exists in the table. Step 11 checks gusto_i9_complete (added July 2026, live) instead.

Step 12 — ⭐ GATE 2: Training Checklist (Auto-Decision from 5 Days)

Trigger: Hermes detects employee with all 4 onboarding conditions met except training. Training does NOT start until shifts_account_created = true — the Gate 2 cron query filters on shifts_account_created=eq.true&pos_created=eq.true&gusto_account_created=eq.true&gusto_i9_complete=eq.true before posting any training checklist. This is the dependency chain: 7shifts account → Chowbus + Gusto auto-create → I-9 via Gusto → THEN training checklist appears.

Hermes posts (via cron 🟠P2-#05, job d36c2277b124, every 2h): All training messages go in the employee's primary thread (look up thread_ts + channel from the employee_hired audit log entry's after_state). Do NOT post standalone messages.

One short plain text message (no Block Kit) — slack-message-structure v3 shape even in store thread:

👷 *Training · Gate 2 · {Name} · {store}*
Setup ✅ · days 0/5 · reply day N done [trainer] / pass / fail
👉 @{GM} mark days · @Sally if stuck 48h+

Optional second thread line if GM needs syntax: day 1 done [trainer] · day 3 fail · after 5: pass or fail (no auto-pass)

GM replies in thread with text. Hermes parses: - day 1 done Levi → training_day_1 = true, trainer = "Levi" (stored in audit log) - day 2 done Sarah → training_day_2 = true, trainer = "Sarah" - day 3 fail → training_day_3 = false, auto-fail - pass → training_complete_pass = true, approver = GM's Slack ID (stored in audit log) - fail → training_complete_pass = false, stays in onboarding

Tracking who trained and who approved: Stored in audit log after_state: - Per day: {"day": 1, "trainer": "Levi", "marked_by": "U0BB7LNP65C"} - Final: {"result": "passed", "trainers": {"1": "Levi", "2": "Sarah", ...}, "approved_by": "U0BB7LNP65C"}

No pass without explicit pass reply. No auto-passing. No answer = no pass = stays in onboarding.

GM interaction — reply with text in thread (no buttons): - GM replies "day 1 done Levi" → training_day_1 = true, trainer=Levi → Hermes confirms in thread + updates progress tracker (□ → ✅) - GM replies "day 3 fail" → training_day_3 = false → Hermes confirms in thread → auto-fail, stays in onboarding - Trainer name is required for each "done" day — tracked in audit log

Auto-decision (no pass without explicit pass reply): - All 5 days done + GM replies pass → training_complete_pass = true, approver = GM's Slack ID → auto-proceed to Step 13 (activate) - Any day failed → auto-fail, stays in onboarding - No reply = no pass = stays in onboarding. Never auto-pass. - Hermes checks after each reply: if all 5 days resolved, prompt GM for final pass or fail.

Trainer + approver tracked in audit log: - Per day: event_type=training_day_completed, after_state={"day": N, "trainer": "name", "marked_by": "gm_slack_id"} - Final: event_type=gate2_passed or gate2_failed, after_state={"trainers": {"1":"Levi","2":"Sarah",...}, "approved_by": "gm_slack_id"}

This is the ONLY human gate in Stage 2. GM marks 5 training days with trainer names, then explicitly approves with pass.

Completion: Training result recorded. Gate 2 resolved.

Step 13 — Active Gate (Auto)

Hermes does: 1. Check all conditions: - shifts_account_created = true (7shifts ✓) - pos_created = true (Chowbus ✓ via 7shifts integration) - gusto_account_created = true (Gusto ✓ via 7shifts integration) - gusto_i9_complete = true (I-9 + E-Verify ✓ via Gusto) - onboarding_email_sent_at set (package ✓ via People-Onboard-#6) - training_complete_pass = true (Training ✓ via Gate 2) 2. If all true → UPDATE workforce_employees SET status = 'active', active_at = now(), onboarding_complete = true, ws_onboarding_complete = true, updated_at = now() WHERE id = '{id}' 3. Post activation notice as a thread reply in the employee's primary thread 4. Cross-dept handoff: Post to Ops channel: "{Store}: [Name] active — add to schedule."

If any false → stay in onboarding. Tell GM what's missing.

Completion: Employee is ACTIVE. Ops notified.

Step 14 — Cross-Dept Handoff

Already handled in Step 7 and Step 13. Summary: - Step 7 → Ops channel: position filled, new hire in onboarding - Step 13 → Ops channel: employee active, add to schedule

Brain Queries Cheat Sheet

-- Store lookup from Slack channel
SELECT id, number, brand, city, gm_slack_id
FROM stores WHERE number = '{5_digit_number}';

-- 7shifts actual headcount by role (from daily cron pull)
-- Parse the employees JSONB array, count by role
SELECT employees FROM seven_shifts_cache
WHERE store_number = '{store_number}'
ORDER BY cache_date DESC LIMIT 1;
-- Then in code: json.loads(employees), Counter(e['role'] for e in emps)

-- Min staff sheet (per store, per shift, per role, per day)
SELECT role_name, shift, mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun
FROM staff_count_minimums
WHERE store_number = '{store_number}';

-- Fallback: stores.min_staff JSONB (no day-of-week, single number per role)
SELECT min_staff FROM stores WHERE number = '{store_number}';

-- Open jobs for a store
SELECT * FROM jobs
WHERE store_number = '{store_number}' AND status = 'open';

-- Shortlisted applicants for a role
SELECT id, name, score, position, email, phone, availability, experience
FROM applicants
WHERE brand ILIKE '%{brand_short}%'
AND position ILIKE '{role}'
AND status = 'pipeline' AND score >= 80
ORDER BY score DESC;

-- Gate 1: GM picks applicant
-- status must be 'approved' (not 'hired' — check constraint allows pipeline/rejected/interviewing/approved/declined)
-- hr_decision must be 'approved' or 'declined'
UPDATE applicants SET status = 'approved', hr_decision = 'approved',
    hr_decided_by = '{gm_slack_id}', hr_decided_at = now()
WHERE id = '{applicant_id}';

-- Onboarding status for a person (automated Stage 2)
SELECT employee_name, position, status,
       shifts_account_created, pos_created,
       gusto_account_created, gusto_i9_complete,
       training_complete_pass, training_result,
       onboarding_complete
FROM workforce_employees WHERE id = '{id}';

-- Activate employee (5 conditions — all auto except Gate 2)
UPDATE workforce_employees
SET status = 'active', active_at = now(),
    onboarding_complete = true, ws_onboarding_complete = true
WHERE id = '{id}'
AND shifts_account_created IS TRUE    -- 7shifts skill (auto)
AND pos_created IS TRUE                -- Chowbus via 7shifts integration (auto)
AND gusto_account_created IS TRUE      -- Gusto via 7shifts integration (auto)
AND gusto_i9_complete IS TRUE          -- I-9 + E-Verify via Gusto (auto)
AND training_complete_pass IS TRUE;    -- Gate 2 (GM only human action in Stage 2)

-- Audit log
INSERT INTO workforce_audit_log
  (agent_id, actor, event_type, store_number, employee_id, reason, before_state, after_state)
VALUES ('hermes', 'hermes', '{action}', '{store_number}', '{employee_id}', '{reason}', '{before}'::jsonb, '{after}'::jsonb);

Common Pitfalls

  1. Forgetting the store lookup. Always resolve channel → store first. Never assume which store from the message text alone.

  2. Skipping the GM check. Anyone can type "Need 1 Server" — verify the sender is the GM before creating a hiring record.

  3. Wrong table names. The real tables are workforce_employees (not workforce), applicants (not hiring_candidates), jobs (not hiring_requests). Using wrong names = query fails.

  4. Wrong join key. workforce_employees.store_number is TEXT like "00001" — it matches stores.number, NOT stores.id (UUID).

  5. Calling Landing Page directly. Hermes reads Brain, not Landing Page. The Puller feeds candidates into applicants. Hermes scores and notifies.

  6. Activating without I-9. The I-9 gate (gusto_i9_complete) is non-negotiable. Even if everything else is done, no I-9 = no Active. Legal requirement. Gusto handles I-9 + E-Verify — the old shifts_docs_complete field is deprecated.

  7. Not disambiguating names. If 2+ candidates or employees share a name, ask the human to pick by ID. Never guess.

  8. Nudging too aggressively. Day 0: silent (give them time). Day 1: Slack nudge. Day 2: Slack + text. Day 3+: tell GM. Don't spam.

  9. Forgetting cross-dept handoff. After hire (Step 7) and after activation (Step 13), post to Ops channel. Ops needs to know.

  10. Missing audit log. Every Hermes action → INSERT INTO workforce_audit_log. If you skip this, there's no trace-back.

  11. "Server" ambiguity. Without restaurant context in SOUL.md, the model will interpret "server" as a cloud/computer server. If the bot asks "do you mean cloud servers?", SOUL.md is missing or not loaded. Fix: ensure $HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md has the restaurant role glossary. The skill description already includes "server" as a trigger keyword, but the model also needs domain grounding from SOUL.md to disambiguate.

  12. Terminal output in Slack. Never show curl, python3, or shell commands in Slack replies. The GM only needs to see the result (budget status, job status). Use execute_code silently or make API calls without showing the implementation.

  13. Stage 2 crons (live naming Jul 2026): #2 Create 7shift logins · #3 Check Chowbus Gusto (poll only) · #4 Nudge stuck hires · #5 Mark training days · #6 Send onboarding package. Remaining gap: company 396453 POS Integrations (Wilmington) often still pos=other. See references/onboarding-pipeline-crons.md.

  14. Missing gm_slack_id — stores 00004 and 00005 still empty. As of July 2026: 00001=Steven Goode ✅, 00002=Taxx Galopo ✅, 00003=Levi ✅, 00004=❌ empty, 00005=❌ null. Step 1 GM verification fails for 00004/00005 until filled. To find GMs: list channel members via conversations.members, cross-reference with users.info to get real names, then ask Louis to confirm — never guess who is GM.

  15. The channel map in this skill is NOT verified ground truth — it drifted from live Slack. As of July 2026 the "Real channel map (from Supabase)" table above was WRONG for 4 of 5 stores when checked against the live workspace: Brain listed store 00002 as Masa (live Slack = s00002-gangnam-greenville), 00004 as Gangnam Greenville (live Slack = s00004-low-country-wilmington), 00005 was missing from Brain, and the workspace had duplicate junk channels (s001-gangnam-fay, s001-gangnam-fayetteville, store-gangnam-fayetteville, s003-gangnam-wil, s005-masa-greenville). Before a cron or batch job posts a store-specific message, list live channels via Slack conversations.list (auth with SLACK_BOT_TOKEN from ~/.hermes/.env) and reconcile with stores.slack_channel. On any conflict, STOP and ask the user which channel is real — posting the wrong store's message to the wrong GM is a real harm, worse than not posting. See wiserise-architecture pitfall #9.

  16. staff_count_minimums originates from a GM-filled form — never invent minimums, never hand-build the form. Step 3's gap check needs per-store staff_count_minimums data. It comes from the GM filling out the real SHIFT-F-006 Staff Count Sheet (which already exists in the sops table → org-files Storage bucket) and uploading it, OR from transcribing a real photographed/scanned form. ⛔ Do NOT regenerate the form locally — pull the existing PDF from Storage (see Pre-Step). Transcribe uploads two ways: shift-level rows → staff_count_minimums (store_number, shift am/pm, role_name, mon–sun), and the summary block → min_staff_standards (store_number, role, min_count, safe_count). If a store has no data, pull SHIFT-F-006 and send it to that store's GM. As of July 2026 only stores 00001 (transcribed from photo) and 00003 have real data.

  17. Posting to a store channel — the full Slack ladder. When a cron or session posts a store message (shortlist, morning brief, form request), do ALL of these in order, or the post silently fails:

    • a. Resolve the LIVE channel ID by store NUMBER via conversations.list (not the stale stores.slack_channel label — see #15).
    • b. Check the channel is not archived: conversations.info → reject if is_archived is true (posting returns error is_archived). Archived = dead store channel; if the store that needs the message has no live channel, STOP and report — do not force it elsewhere.
    • c. Ensure the bot is a member: conversations.info → if is_member is false, call conversations.join first (needs channels:join scope; private channels need a manual invite). chat.postMessage to a channel the bot hasn't joined fails unless chat:write.public covers it.
    • d. Post with chat.postMessage.

  18. Uploading a file to Slack — use files.getUploadURLExternal + upload + files.completeUploadExternal. The WISE BRAIN bot has files:write ✅ (added July 2026). The upload flow is 3 steps: (1) get upload URL via files.getUploadURLExternal, (2) POST the file to that URL, (3) call files.completeUploadExternal with the file_id + channel_id + initial_comment. Step 2 upload may return HTTP 401 but completeUploadExternal still succeeds — the 401 is a redirect auth quirk, not a real failure. Verify success via the completeUploadExternal response ok:true, not the intermediate upload HTTP code.

  19. Creating a new stores row needs org_id (NOT NULL). A bare INSERT fails with null value in column "org_id" violates not-null constraint. Copy org_id (and district_id/region_id if the store uses them) from an existing store row first, then include it in the INSERT.

  20. Cron model pinning — crons break when the active model changes. When you switch models mid-session (e.g. GLM → Claude → GLM), existing crons fail with RuntimeError: Skipped to prevent unintended spend: global inference config drifted since this job was created (model 'X' -> 'Y'), and this job is unpinned. Fix: pin every cron explicitly with cronjob action=update job_id=X model={"model":"z-ai/glm-5.2","provider":"nous"} (or whatever the current model is). Do this for ALL crons after a model switch, not just the one that errored — the others will fail on their next run.

  21. Cron delivery target — deliver=all fails in CLI/TUI sessions. Error: no delivery target resolved for deliver=all. CLI sessions have no gateway channel attached, so all has nowhere to deliver. Fix: set deliver=origin (delivers to the current chat) or pin to a specific platform channel. The cron's actual Slack posts (via chat.postMessage in the prompt) work regardless — this only affects the cron's own status summary delivery.

  22. Emoji rendering in Slack chat.postMessage. When posting messages with emoji (🔥, ✅, 📋, 🟢, 🔴) via the Slack API chat.postMessage with text= parameter, emojis may render as raw colon-syntax (:fire: instead of 🔥) depending on the client. To ensure proper rendering, either use the blocks= parameter with rich text sections, or verify the message renders correctly in the Slack client after posting. Don't assume emojis landed — check.

  23. Dedup applicants by email/phone before shortlisting. If the same person applies twice (same email OR phone), keep only the highest-scored one. Never shortlist the same person twice. Add this dedupe step in the Step 5 cron before posting the shortlist.

  24. Block Kit context blocks require elements array, not text. Slack returns invalid_blocks error if a context block has text but no elements. Use {"type":"context","elements":[{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"..."}]} or avoid context entirely — use section blocks instead. Confirmed live July 2026.

  25. No Block Kit buttons — use plain text + number reply for all gates. Louis approved plain text only (first principles: simpler = fewer things break, works now, no plugin/gateway dependency). All gates (Gate 1 pick, over-gap approval, Gate 2 training) use plain text messages. GM replies with text: number to pick candidate, approve/decline for over-gap, day 1 done/pass/fail for training. No Block Kit buttons anywhere in the People workflow.

  26. Shortlist format: lean, no inline interview questions, no movie; always include apply date. Louis asked to add interview Qs inline to the shortlist, then reverted. Then asked to remove the movie field from the shortlist too. Keep the shortlist to candidate details (name, score, Applied YYYY-MM-DD from created_at, email, phone, availability, experience, weekends, start_soon). No movie field. Interview questions stay in Brain (applicants.gm_interview_questions) and are surfaced only when the GM asks for detail on a specific candidate. Apply date is mandatory on every candidate line (Louis 2026-07-13).

  27. jobs table INSERT requires description (NOT NULL). A bare INSERT without description fails with null value in column "description" of relation "jobs" violates not-null constraint. Always include a meaningful description when creating a job row. The employment_type column also exists and defaults to Full-time.

  28. Slack file upload is 3 steps — don't check intermediate HTTP codes. The flow is: (1) files.getUploadURLExternal → returns upload_url + file_id, (2) POST file to upload_url → may return HTTP 401 (redirect auth quirk, NOT a real failure), (3) files.completeUploadExternal with file_id + channel_id + initial_comment → this is the call that matters. Verify success on step 3's ok:true, never on step 2's HTTP code. Confirmed live July 2026.

  29. supabase db query --linked requires supabase link first. If you get "Cannot find project ref. Have you run supabase link?", run supabase link --project-ref kwadpofhzjpmmahlrefj from home dir first. Then supabase db query --linked "ALTER TABLE..." works for DDL statements that PostgREST can't do (ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX, etc.). Use this for schema changes — the REST API only supports DML (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE).

  30. Gate 2 uses plain text replies — no buttons, no Block Kit. GM replies in thread: "day 1 done", "day 3 fail", etc. When all 5 days resolved, GM replies pass or fail. All Done + pass → auto-activate. Any fail → stays in onboarding. No buttons anywhere in the People workflow.

  31. Duplicate from dual intake (photo + text). When a GM uploads an interview sheet photo AND types "walk-in, onboard [name]" as text in the same channel within minutes, Hermes may process both messages. Without dedup, this creates TWO employee records for the same person — double 7shifts accounts, double checklist messages, confused onboarding. Fix: BOTH the photo path (Step 3) and the text walk-in path (Step 4) MUST check workforce_employees by email (ilike) AND by name (ilike) BEFORE inserting. If a match is found, skip the INSERT and reply that the person is already in the system. Name matching must be case-insensitive and handle partial matches ("Lola Mongelli" vs "Lola Dawlocki Mongelli") — use ilike with the full name from the new message.

  32. Exploring instead of executing. When a GM says "need 1 server" in Slack, the bot sometimes runs hermes sessions list, hermes sessions rename, reads reference files, and does shell exploration before doing any actual work. This wastes time and triggers security approval popups (curl | python3 blocks the flow). Fix: Steps 1–7 are pure Supabase REST API calls + Slack chat.postMessage. No terminal commands needed. No reference file reads needed. The skill body has everything. If the bot catches itself running hermes sessions, source .env, grep, or reading reference files during a hiring request — STOP and go straight to the Supabase query. The env vars are already in the gateway session context.

  33. Slack tool_progress: off required for Slack platform. By default, if display.tool_progress is set globally (e.g. to final), Slack shows all tool activity (Reading skill, Running code, terminal blocks) in the chat. This leaks code and internal activity to the GM. Fix: Set display.platforms.slack.tool_progress: off in config.yaml (keeps CLI progress visible). The global setting can stay final for CLI. Requires gateway restart to take effect. Verified July 2026 — without this, every tool call shows in Slack.

  34. Custom Slack buttons are dead on click. The Hermes Slack adapter (Socket Mode) only handles its own action IDs (hermes_approve_*, hermes_confirm_*). Custom action IDs like gm_hire_*, approve_overgap_*, train_day* have no handler — buttons render but clicking does nothing. Workaround: Post buttons as visual guides, but rely on TEXT replies from the GM ("1", "hire 1", "approve", "day 1 done", "pass"). The cron prompts (#04, #05) already parse text replies. To make real clicks work, a Slack plugin must register handlers via ctx.register_slack_action_handler() — see plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py lines 1188-1230. See references/slack-block-kit-patterns.md CRITICAL section.

  35. Do NOT fill both text and blocks in chat.postMessage. When posting Block Kit, Slack renders BOTH the text field AND the blocks field — causing a duplicate-looking message (card on top, plain text summary below). This was the #1 cause of "why show both" complaints in July 2026 testing. Fix: When posting blocks, set text to a short fallback only (e.g. "Hiring approval needed") or omit entirely. NEVER put a full summary, bullet points, or status log in text when blocks is also set. Louis's decision: use plain text only, no Block Kit at all (Pitfall #25). This eliminates the text+blocks conflict entirely.

  36. No internal jargon in Slack messages. GM-facing messages must never contain: "Brain", "rows logged", "recruiting rows saved", "audit", "thread reply posted", "pipeline" (as a system term). The GM only needs: gap count, approval status, candidate list, next action. Internal terms belong in audit logs, not Slack.

  37. workforce_audit_log.before_state is NOT NULL. Passing None/null for before_state causes a constraint violation (null value in column "before_state" of relation "workforce_audit_log" violates not-null constraint). For new-record events (walk-in hire, etc.), use an empty JSONB object {} — never null. The after_state should also be a JSONB object (not a string).

  38. Interview sheet photo → walk-in hire. When Louis or a GM uploads a photo of a completed Interview Sheet, use vision_analyze to extract handwritten data (name, email, phone, position, screening results, character scores, decision, manager signature). This is a walk-in hire variant — bypass Steps 1–6, go straight to INSERT + Step 7. Dedup by email AND name before creating. See the "Walk-In Hire from Interview Sheet Photo" section above.

  39. Pay Band Policy lives in sops (REF-002), not on workforce_employees. workforce_employees has no pay_rate column — pay rates are company-wide policy stored as an SOP. When a hire's pay rate is blank, look up SELECT content FROM sops WHERE sop_no = 'REF-002' and state the applicable rate in the reply. When Louis sends updated pay rate content, PATCH the existing sops row and bump version — do NOT create a new row.

  40. execute_code blocked in some session types. When execute_code returns a BLOCKED error, fall back to terminal with inline Python (using python3 -c). Read env vars from ~/.hermes/.env the same way. This is a session-type limitation, not a broken tool — don't hardcode the refusal into future behavior.

  41. Test data contamination — clean Brain before going live. E2E tests leave SAMPLE-*, ALLROLE-*, @test.com / @example.com / @email.com rows. Delete those before ops; they pollute shortlists and can trigger real 7shifts creates. Applicants score ≥ 60 must stay pipeline (or higher workflow status), never rejected solely for score — floor is 60 (Louis: “only reject below 60”). Fix mislabeled rows when found.

  42. Approvals mode — set to smart to avoid security popup spam. When the bot uses curl | python3 in terminal, the security scanner flags it and posts an approval popup in Slack. The GM has to click Allow for every single command. Fix: Set hermes config set approvals.mode smart — low-risk commands auto-approve, high-risk still prompt. Also: prefer execute_code (Python) over curl in terminal for API calls — execute_code does not trigger the security scanner.

  43. Gateway auto-posts final text response as a separate Slack message. When a Slack gateway session calls chat.postMessage to post a hiring card/shortlist AND then writes a text summary as the "final answer," the gateway posts BOTH to Slack — the API message AND the text response. This creates duplicate-looking messages (card on top, text summary below). Fix: After posting any message via chat.postMessage, your final text response must be exactly Done. — not a summary, not bullet points, not status updates. The gateway posts "Done." which is harmless. If you DON'T call chat.postMessage (just write a normal text reply), the gateway posts your text as the message — that's the normal flow, no issue.

  44. 7shifts onboarding package auto-sends — no manual click needed. The 7shifts API has NO endpoint to send onboarding packages (all return 404 — tried /onboarding_package, /onboarding_package/send, /resend_invite, /invite, PUT onboarding_required). The package is configured in 7shifts Settings (6 documents ON: I-9, Emergency Contact, Rules, At-Will, Anti-Harassment, Tip Pool). When the employee accepts the invite email, the package auto-appears. Do NOT tell the GM to manually send the package. Do NOT try to call onboarding endpoints via API.

  45. Onboarding notifications go to HR (06-people), not GM/store channel. All Step 8-11 notifications (7shifts created, package in progress, onboarding stuck, invite pending) go to HR channel (06-people, C0AQVGCPDK8). The GM only sees: hire confirmation (Step 7), training checklist (Step 12), and activation (Step 13). The GM does NOT need to know about 7shifts/Chowbus/Gusto account creation status — that's HR's job. Cron #4 (nudge) and cron #6 (package check) both post to 06-people.

  46. Training day tracking — trainer name required, no auto-pass. GM replies day 1 done Levi (not just day 1 done). Trainer name is stored in audit log per day. Final pass reply records the approving manager's Slack ID. No explicit pass = no pass = stays in onboarding. Never auto-pass. Each "done" day must include trainer name. The training checklist message must state this clearly: day 1 done [trainer name] and ⚠️ Training cannot pass without explicit pass reply.

  47. Setup checklist timing — NOT at hire time. The setup checklist (R7) should NOT be posted when the employee is hired (Step 7). It should only appear when all 4 auto-steps are complete (shifts_account_created, pos_created, gusto_account_created, gusto_i9_complete). At hire time, post only a simple "Hired ✅" confirmation. The checklist tells the GM what happened and what's next (training).

  48. Shortlist candidate limit — show top {gap + 2}, max 5. Don't dump the entire pipeline. If the gap is 1, show top 3. If gap is 5, show top 5. This keeps the shortlist focused and actionable.

  49. WISE OPS is the agent name for operations. Louis renamed the operations agent from "WISE BRAIN" to "WISE OPS." All SOPs, skill docs, and Slack messages should reference "WISE OPS" for operations work (onboarding, crons, store operations). "WISE BRAIN" refers to the Supabase database (the Brain), not the agent. The wise_ops profile runs all onboarding crons (#2-#6). The default profile runs executive/brain crons only.

  50. Dual profile setup — default + wise_ops. People onboarding crons (#2 7shifts create, #3 setup check, #4 nudge, #5 training, #6 package) all live on the wise_ops profile, not default. Default profile keeps executive/brain crons (health check, nightly review, token spend, 1Password sync, email inbox). When updating cron prompts or scripts, update the wise_ops profile's cron/jobs.json directly (cronjob tool can't edit cross-profile crons). Scripts must be copied to ~/.hermes/profiles/wise_ops/scripts/ as well as ~/.hermes/scripts/.

  51. 00003 Integrations "connected" ≠ staff auto-create (Lola case, Jul 2026). Company pos=other is unreliable. UI green checkmarks and integrations status=online only prove the link. For staff auto-hire check: employee_sync_enabled, employees_mapped, roles_mapped, Gusto unmapped_users via GET /company/{cid}/integrations. Lola stuck 70h+: Chowbus online + sales on but employee_sync_enabled=false; Gusto online with unmapped_users in the dozens. Do not say "auto after invite" or "wait one 5 AM" when employee sync is off — escalate Integrations UI (Finance/Yumi or HR). See people-shifts-accounts/references/integration-employee-sync.md.

  52. Onboarding package auto-sends — confirmed via 7shifts UI. The 7shifts Onboarding Settings page (app.7shifts.com/company/396453/employees/onboarding?tab=settings) shows 6 documents ON: I-9, Emergency Contact, Employee Rules & Policies, At-Will Employment, Anti-Harassment Policy, Tip Pool Agreement. 3 documents OFF: W-4, State tax, Payment method. The package auto-appears when the employee accepts the invite email — no manual "Send" click needed. The 7shifts API has no endpoint to send packages (all return 404).

  53. SOPs published — TEAM-013 Recruiting + TEAM-014 Onboarding. Both live in Brain (sops table, status=live) + Supabase Storage (org-files/playbooks/). HTML is a build artifact only — delete after publishing. PDF in Storage is the published version. SOPs say "WISE OPS" not "WISE BRAIN." Published via sop_html_builder.py + Chrome headless PDF + curl upload to Storage + REST insert to sops table (the supabase Python package is broken in the venv — use curl for Storage upload + REST insert instead of sop_publish.py).

  54. HQ trainer ≠ store hire workflow (Jul 2026). Company Trainer / multi-unit coach ads and flyers skip store gap check, Gate 1, and Landing Page unless Louis asks for a Brain jobs row. After "still too confused," ship only the short ad (no re-rate essay). Flyer: match attached style (default orange WE ARE HIRING bubble); 1-page PDF + letter-aspect PNG without black bars; pay always on creative; apply = resume + week-1 server plan. See references/hq-trainer-ads-flyers.md.

Corporate / HQ role ads & flyers (not store gap hire)

Trigger: Louis asks for Indeed/Facebook ads, hiring flyer, or recruit a Trainer / multi-unit coach / HQ people role — often with first-principles training for managers + staff.

Not Steps 1–7. No store channel gap check, no GM Gate 1, no auto Landing Page job unless he says post to Brain/careers.

First-principles rules (Louis Jul 2026)

  1. One system only — teach Layer 0 WISE OPS + manager L1–3 (Run / Lead / Keep money) + staff Day 1–5. No new framework / PowerPoint factory.
  2. Pay on every creative — Trainer not in REF-002; default $18–$22/hr DOE unless Louis locks another band/salary.
  3. Confusion ladder — if Louis is confused after a long pack → short copy-paste ad only (title · pay · job · 3 teach lines · need · apply). Do not re-explain theory.
  4. Flyer — match attached template; default orange WE ARE/HIRING! bubble; 1-page PDF + clean PNG via MEDIA:; Desktop copies. AVIF refs → sips to PNG before vision.

Apply line: Resume + 5 lines: how you train a new server in week 1.

Verification Checklist

  • [ ] Channel → store resolved before any action
  • [ ] GM identity verified (sender = store GM)
  • [ ] Budget check completed before opening job
  • [ ] I-9 gate checked before allowing Active status (Gusto gusto_i9_complete)
  • [ ] All 5 setup conditions true before activation (7shifts, Chowbus, Gusto, Gusto I-9, training)
  • [ ] Cross-dept handoff posted to Ops (Steps 7 and 13)
  • [ ] Audit log written for every Hermes action
  • [ ] Slack messages follow slack-message-structure v3 (WHAT/WHO/WHEN parent + 👉 @owner; details in thread; plain text only, no Block Kit)
  • [ ] No employee data sent to unauthorized channel or person
  • [ ] Human gates use plain text + number/text reply (no Block Kit buttons) — Gate 1: reply number, over-gap: reply approve/decline, Gate 2: reply day N done/pass/fail
  • [ ] Gate 2: auto-decision — all 5 days Done = pass, any Fail = fail. No separate Pass/Fail button.
  • [ ] HQ trainer / ad-flyer: skip store Steps 1–7 unless asked; short ad if Louis confused; pay on creative; 1-page PDF+PNG MEDIA
