Common Pitfalls

  1. Louis: conflict / FOH problem / “不知道该怎么处理” — first reply too long. He rejected full ladder + multi-SOP dumps (Jul 2026: 太多 → 白话/小孩都能懂). Default first reply (CN if he wrote CN): one bold line + exactly 3 steps — (1) write who/store/facts (2) private one talk / coaching (3) still bad → written warning. No form catalog, no TEAM-002/007/005/006 list, no express-lane essay until he asks 具体 / form / next step. Then: “把 谁+做了啥 发我 → 我写成一句话.” Only after facts → coach script or warning draft + doc numbers. Use clear-simple-bullets. 0b. Fake public posts after a fire / unprofessional exit (FB groups, Google, residents groups). Class: brand + people. P0 if sex crime / child / assault lie or major defamation. DRI = Owner (not the accused GM alone). First reply still 123: (1) document screenshots (2) private talk to GM covering false public posts + how-you-talk (3) lawyer/public statement only if Louis asks. Do not restate the assault claim in public drafts — use “false and defamatory posts.” Do not post the company reply into the attack/residents group first — official Page first; group only if Louis + lawyer OK. GM talk is private DM/call, never open store channel. Scripts + Version A Page post + Page vs group/Composio Facebook: references/public-retaliation-and-gm-talk.md. 0c. “Get all HR email / Slack / 7shifts as fact for staff complaint” (GM tone, multi staff, unprofessional). Do not answer from memory or the GM’s side story alone. Run references/staff-complaint-fact-pack.md. Parallel: Gmail hr@ + full get (empty body often = image attachments → download + vision) · Brain hr_cases · slack_chat_raw (col message_ts not ts) + live Slack only if bot has history · 7shifts announcements only (no DM API) · ladder = GM-style context only, not complaints about him. One named email ≠ “multiple staff.” Store Slack tiny / bot not in channel → 数据缺口, never “no Slack complaints.” Pay/bank HR mail ≠ tone case. Case resolved still report claims; don’t invent investigation outcome.
  2. Using Slack as the database. Slack is a conversation layer; verify live status in Supabase.
  3. Oversharing. Use the minimum employee information needed for the task.
  4. Treating a draft as approval. A draft, suggestion, or summary does not authorize a People decision.
  5. Alert spam. Report only an actionable issue. Correct silence is better than a wrong alert.
  6. Skipping the freshness check before payroll. Stale data → STOP. Never guess on money. 5b. Pretending payroll is live. Stage 7 is not built. Point to 7shifts + tip-out forms + Gusto; never fabricate a “wage sheet” workflow. 5c. Weekend “催工资” → spam finance. Default Monday. Final pay follows TEAM-006 + HR, not store cash. Only Louis/HR can approve off-cycle.
  7. Forgetting the discipline ladder. Warning needs Coaching. Hermes blocks skips via people_ladder_file.py. Never bypass unless express lane (theft/violence/safety) + Louis/HR. 6b. Photo intake without ladder write. Filing coaching photo to Drive/file_index only is incomplete. Always run people_ladder_file.py file --file-id … after index. 6c. Auto-terminating. Script may set terminated_at only after D3 human gate. Never set status=terminated from photo alone.
  8. Two entry points. All human input goes through Slack → Brain. Never enter data directly into Sheets.
  9. "Server" not recognized as restaurant role. If the bot responds to "I need 2 server" with a cloud computing question, SOUL.md is missing restaurant domain context. Fix $HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md.
  10. Channel map drifts. stores.slack_channel was wrong for 4/5 stores as of July 2026. Always verify against live Slack conversations.list before posting store-specific messages.
  11. Stores 00004–00005 have no GM Slack ID and no 7shifts cache. Morning brief and gap checks will produce no data for these stores until they're onboarded.
  12. v_roster.person_id ≠ workforce_employees.id. These are DIFFERENT UUIDs. Never cross-reference by ID between view and base table.
  13. Anon key returns 0 rows on RLS-protected tables. Use SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY for workforce_employees and stores.
  14. Cron model pinning. After a model switch, pin every cron explicitly or it will fail with a drift error.
  15. Employee on a coaching/discipline form not found in workforce_employees. When a GM uploads a coaching or discipline form, always search workforce_employees.employee_name (ilike) for the named employee. If not found, this is a compliance risk (possible off-system hire — no I-9, no 7shifts, no onboarding). Flag it to Louis immediately. Do not create the employee record without Louis's explicit approval. The workforce_employees name column is employee_name — NOT name or full_name.
  16. Employee resigns mid-coaching. If the form notes the employee quit during the coaching conversation, the form is still a valid document — file it as NEEDS_REVIEW (unsigned, incomplete). If the employee IS in the Brain, Louis must decide whether to update status to terminated with the incident as termination_reason. Do not auto-terminate.
  17. “Active account” multi-system dump confuses Louis. First answer = which system + last time + which store. 7shifts last_login ≠ Chowbus last ticket ≠ Brain status. Full dump only if he asks. See references/person-account-activity.md.
  18. Brain can say active while 7shifts is inactive (roster import then later deactivate). Re-check live 7shifts before saying “有 active 帐号”.

Verification Checklist

  • [ ] Supabase was checked before reporting live People status.
  • [ ] Original documents remain on Drive; no unsupported facts were invented.
  • [ ] The audience is authorized for the information shared.
  • [ ] No hiring, employment, pay, legal, or external action happened without approval.
  • [ ] The response gives one clear next human action when action is needed.
  • [ ] Freshness check passed before any payroll or money action.
  • [ ] 3-pillar model respected: Brain = truth, Hermes = worker, Slack = OS.

🏢 OPS 🔴 Louis Only v3.1
💬 Say this in Slack: session title / naming
Global session title format, naming convention, and sorting for all Hermes sessions.
Uses100
Patches18
Views100
Last Used2026-07-24
Pathagents/session-format

Session Title Format

Every session title MUST follow this format:

[Circle] Dept | Type: Description [Status]

Real examples:

🔴 People | Bug: hiring workflow crashed 🔥
🟠 IT | Feature: Wise Brain perms 🔥
🟠 People | SOP: GM role 🔥
🟡 IT | Research: Brain framework ✅
⚪ Finance | Research: Wilmington rent ✅
🟣 IT | Meta: session format rules ✅
🟠 People | Cron: gate 2 training · 07/12 20:24 ✅

Priority (first position — circle icon only)

Icon Level Meaning
🔴 Critical Infrastructure down, production broken, blockers
🟠 High Security, integrations, dependencies
🟡 Medium Knowledge, research, planning
⚪ Low Trivial, one-time, curiosity
🟣 Meta Housekeeping, admin

Type (1 word before description)

Bug, Feature, Research, SOP, Meta, Fix, Cron, Hire, Build, Report

Description

  • Max 5 words
  • High school language — no jargon, plain words
  • Short, punchy, tells you what the session is about
  • Optional uniqueness stamp · MM/DD HH:MM is allowed after the description (cron bulk renames) and does not count toward the 5 words

Status (last position — non-circle icons)

Icon Status Meaning
🔥 Active Working on it now
🧱 Blocked Waiting on something external
✅ Done Resolved, no action needed

Departments (Wiserise 7 + IT)

  • People — hiring, servers, onboarding, GM, 1-on-1, recruiting
  • Ops — store operations, facilities
  • Finance — lease, rent, payments
  • Admin — roadmaps, workspaces, approval, SOPs
  • IT — Slack, Hermes, Wise Brain, skills, tools, MCP, 1Password, agents, Brain
  • Growth — marketing, leads
  • Procurement — purchasing, vendors
  • Marketing — campaigns, content
  • Personal — personal tasks not work-related

When to Set / Update the Title

  1. FIRST ACTION after user's first message → set full title immediately before doing anything else
  2. During session → if topic changes significantly, update the title
  3. When session ends → flip status icon: ✅ (done) or 🧱 (blocked)

This is NOT optional. Set the title as your first action every session. If you forget, the user will say "title" — fix it immediately, no questions.

CLI (Hermes)

# List to get session_id (current often top row)
hermes sessions list --limit 500

# Rename — NOT `hermes session title` (invalid; fails)
hermes sessions rename <session_id> "🟠 People | Fix: FOH conflict help 🔥"

Pitfalls: - hermes session title "..." is not a command. Always hermes sessions rename <id> "<full title>". - Titles must be UNIQUE store-wide. Rename fails with Title '…' is already in use by session <id>. Never assign the same full string to many cron ticks. - Check exit code and stdout for Error / already in use (do not trust returncode alone). - Live title is SQLite sessions.title (not display_name). - default / WISE BRAIN: ~/.hermes/state.db - wise_ops / WISE OPS: ~/.hermes/profiles/wise_ops/state.db - wise_ops renames: HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes/profiles/wise_ops hermes sessions rename … (default CLI only hits the active profile).

Bulk rename (“rename all sessions”)

When Louis says rename all / fix titles / session format cleanup:

  1. Load this skill — do not invent a parallel scheme.
  2. Query each profile DB: id, title, source, started_at, ended_at + first user-message preview.
  3. Out-of-format = missing circle, missing Dept | Type:, legacy 🟠P2-#… cron labels, or empty title.
  4. Map to format. Cron → Cron:; hire requests → Hire:. Active work 🔥; old/cron ✅.
  5. Uniqueness: keep a used set. On collision, insert stamp before status from session id (YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS) or started_at: · MM/DD HH:MM. Example: 🟠 People | Cron: gate 2 training · 07/12 20:24 ✅.
  6. Apply hermes sessions rename per id; re-query until 0 non-strict titles remain.
  7. If user said “all”, cover default + wise_ops.

Design Rules

  1. Circles vs Shapes: Priority = circles (🔴🟠🟡⚪🟣). Status = shapes (🔥🧱✅). Never mix.
  2. Icon-only priority: Circle only. No P1/P2/P3/P4 text. Old 🟠P2-#04 … titles are wrong → rewrite to 🟠 People | Cron: ….
  3. 5-word limit: Forces clarity. Stamp is uniqueness-only, not description padding.
  4. Department, not project: Business function (IT, People, Finance), not vague names ("Wiserise OS", "Hermes").
  5. Unique titles always: bulk rename without stamps will silently leave most cron sessions unfixed.

Sort Sessions by Priority + Department + Status

# default profile
bash ~/.hermes/skills/productivity/session-format/scripts/session-sort.sh
# wise_ops
bash ~/.hermes/skills/productivity/session-format/scripts/session-sort.sh wise_ops

Sort order: 1. Priority: 🔴 → 🟠 → 🟡 → ⚪ → 🟣 (circle-only; script must not require 🔴P1) 2. Department: People → Ops → Finance → Admin → IT → Growth → Procurement → Marketing → Personal 3. Status: 🔥 Active → 🧱 Blocked → ✅ Done

wiserise-world-brain-router

Overview

Company traffic cop, not the whole company.

  • Understand the ask
  • Lock store / brand / time / actor
  • Check permission
  • Load the one specialist skill
  • Return one fixed WB Card (9 lines): 什么事 → 店 → 事实 → 严重 → DRI → IC → 下一步 → 缺什么 → 要人批

AI coordinates. Humans own judgment, relationships, and final results.

Pillars: Brain (Supabase) = truth · Hermes = only worker · Slack = OS.
Utilities (Sheets / Drive / Obsidian / NotebookLM) are views/files — never the source of live facts.

Naming (Louis 2026-07-15)

Full Short
World Brain WB
9-line reply WB Card
Policies WB- … (e.g. WB- GM 7SHIFT AND CHOWBUS PERMISSION = REF-011)

Activate: already live. Owner DM → mess or WB: …. Detail: references/wb-naming-and-activate.md

When to Use

  • Ask spans domains or skill is unclear
  • User says world brain / 总控 / 公司大脑 / route this
  • Need DRI / IC / coach assignment before action
  • Mixed: labor + people, sales + fraud, SOP + training
  • 做到哪里了 / continue World Brain / 复盘 / handoff
  • Top N issues for all staff / company people problems

Do not use for: pure single-skill phrases already in SOUL router (e.g. exact need 2 server → people-recruiting directly). If SOUL already matched one skill, load that skill — do not re-route.

Do not create tables, crons, or parallel skills from this file.

World Brain build status (Louis Jul 2026 — do not rebuild)

Phase Status
1 Framework + 9-line card ✅
2 router + store-health-review ✅
3 Practice cases (Levi / Masa) ✅
4 Clean people lists (budget ~20 stale; multi-GM titles) stuck — need Louis one-line
5 Labor-cost etc not built
6 Multi-agent fleet later

Continue triggers: ignore budget · budget 00001=N … · GM 00001=Steven 00002=Taxx 00003=Levi only · 复盘 · pause · yes lock

“做到哪里了” reply: done 1–3 · stuck at 4 · one-line triggers only. No essay.

Hard bans

  1. Never invent store numbers, sales, labor %, headcount, or names
  2. Missing fact → write UNKNOWN — NEEDS VERIFICATION (or 数据缺口)
  3. Never read owner-locked (O) data for non-owners (bank, full payroll decide, fire decide, secrets)
  4. Never treat Slack chat as final truth — clue only; write verified facts to Brain
  5. Never say “done” unless the specialist skill actually finished + Brain/Slack shows it
  6. Never fire, change pay, send bank money, or sign legal alone
  7. Never become a mega-skill that reimplements hiring/fraud/SOP
  8. Money / fire / formal discipline / formal schedule publish / formal SOP publish = human gate

Workflow (always)

1) Classify intent

One primary: | Intent | Meaning | |--------|---------| | query | show facts | | analyze | explain why | | recommend | suggest action | | execute | do something | | approve | human yes/no |

Done when: one primary intent chosen.

2) Resolve context

What a letter IS (first principles)

A letter's only job: tell a person something formal, in writing, that they sign to acknowledge.

It is not a form (forms have blank lines people fill in). It is not an SOP (SOPs are procedure steps). A letter is pre-filled content written TO someone — the role, the pay, the terms — and they sign at the bottom to accept.

Three document types in the Wiserise brand system

Type Skill Content Signature Number
SOP wiserise-sop Procedure steps for staff No sign-off SERIES-###
Form wiserise-form Blank fields people fill in Yes (handwritten) SERIES-F-###
Letter wiserise-letter (this skill) Pre-filled content TO a person Yes (acceptance) No number (per-recipient)

Letters are per-recipient, not reusable playbook documents. They don't get a sops table row or a series number. The HTML template is the reusable artifact; each instance is unique.

Architecture (3 Pillars + 4 Utilities)

Load wiserise-architecture for the full framework. Key rules for Letters:

Pillar/Utility Letter Role Rule

⚡ Hermes Sole worker — builds HTML, generates PDF This skill tells Hermes how.
💬 Slack Where Louis approves before sending Human gate: never send without explicit yes.
📁 Drive Original PDFs saved under 03 – PEOPLE/Letters/ Push from Hermes.

Full steps: references/offer-letter-e2e-workflow.md.

The look (Wiserise brand template — shared with SOP/Form)

  1. Header band — navy #152035, white wordmark "WISERISE / HOSPITALITY GROUP" on left, letter type label on right (e.g. "OFFER LETTER", "TERMINATION LETTER").
  2. Title — Unna Bold, navy, gold rule underneath. Subline: role · store · FT/PT.
  3. Letter meta — DATE / TO / FROM pre-filled (letters are not forms — no blank underlines for name/date).
  4. Sections — navy pill headers with content below. Two-column for THE ROLE + PAY & TERMS.
  5. Color-coded panels — green "what you do" / orange "what you don't". Max 3 bullets each.
  6. Acceptance box — gold-edged tinted box; plain high-school words (I-9, at-will).
  7. Signature block — SIGNATURE / PRINT NAME / DATE lines (only blanks on the page).
  8. Footer — "WISERISE HOSPITALITY GROUP · CONFIDENTIAL · FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY".

The 6 parts of an offer letter (first principles)

  1. Company identity — Wiserise brand header (navy + gold)
  2. Who + what — Candidate name, position, store, employment type (FT/PT)
  3. Pay — Split lines: Training pay ($7.25/hr staff, $15/hr managers) → After training band rate (REF-002). Never one long mash-up line.
  4. When — Start date + training / 90-day review
  5. Legal — Plain NC at-will: "either side can end it"
  6. Acceptance — Sign-by date + I-9 line + signature block

Tight content rules (v1.3 — Louis first-principles pass)

  • If a line does not answer who / job / pay / start / rules / sign → delete it.
  • Max 3 role bullets + max 3 do + max 3 don't.
  • High-school English. Short words. No jargon. Never leave internal codes undefined (e.g. say "must-fill open jobs", not bare "SAFE gaps").
  • Letter ≠ form (send mode): fill DATE + TO + sign-by. Only signature lines stay blank. Bracket/{{…}} tokens = not send-ready.
  • DocuSign / master template mode (Louis Jul 26, 2026): when he says template, DocuSign, or leave blank where DocuSign needs input → empty underlines (not {{PLACEHOLDER}}) on DATE · TO · Start · sign-by · SIGNATURE · PRINT NAME · Date Signed. Gold micro-hints OK under sign caps. FROM + locked body stay filled. See DocuSign blank rule below.
  • Weekly schedule OFF by default. Include only if schedule changes the hire decision (e.g. multi-store travel coach — keep it).
  • I-9 wording: "Job starts after I-9 / work papers check" (not "contingent upon employment verification").
  • At-will wording: "This is at-will work in North Carolina (either side can end it)."
  • Signature block = candidate only (SIGNATURE / PRINT NAME / DATE). Do not dual-line Owner + Candidate like old plain drafts.
  • Salaried / owner-set roles (GM, Regional People Coach): use salary Louis gives — not staff $7.25 training → band. REF-002 is for hourly seats only.
  • Pay shape: monthly salary + KPI (not bi-weekly as headline).
  • All money = mo AND yr. Every $ shows both. KPI column: Pay (mo / yr) like $258 / $3,100.
  • PAY & TERMS = short/clean ≤6 bullets (Louis: "more short concise and clean"):
  • Salary · 2. KPI pool · 3. Max · 4. Hours (start–end · ~hrs/wk) · 5. Travel · 6. Start. Do not stuff scorer/pay-cadence/miss into PAY — those live in the KPI note.
  • Daily start/end hours when asked: PAY Hours line and schedule HOURS column (default coach: 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM).
  • Travel (coach default): car rental + gas + hotel (receipts) — not IRS mileage-only unless Louis says mileage.
  • KPI block: gold note = rules only (proof · Owner scores yes/no each month · hit = next paycheck · miss $0 · no side sheets). Table # | KPI | What it means | Goal | Proof | Pay (mo / yr). Pool = % of yearly salary / N unless weighted.
  • Locked KPI wording: staffing = "Must-fill open jobs closed"; onboarding means = "Completed onboarding checklist + train done".
  • Main job line: Louis's exact short phrase (e.g. "Coach managers across 5 stores") in subline + role + KPI #1 means + scope do.
  • Clean/neat: balance two-col ROLE vs PAY; avoid fat PAY lists and repeated pay walls.

First-principles rate (when Louis says "rate this")

Score ~ /10 on: one job only · letter≠form · brand · who/job/pay/start/rules/sign · simple words · mo+yr pay · 1 page · scope max 3 · schedule earns space · send-ready (no brackets; KPI scorer + pay cadence set). Lead with overall score + weak fixes only.

Rebuild from an existing draft (Louis drops PDF / "try this")

When Louis attaches an old plain offer PDF (or says try this / redo this on a letter):

  1. pdftotext -layout the PDF. Capture role, pay, schedule, do/don't, names.
  2. Map into templates/offer_letter_template.html with v1.1 rules — do not keep plain unbranded layout.
  3. Chrome headless → 1-page PDF; verify pdfinfo | grep Pages, then pdftoppm + vision check.
  4. Show Louis PDF + PNG (MEDIA:). Leave date / last name / sign-by as [brackets] if unknown — ask once.
  5. Known-good salaried coach skeleton: references/sally-coach-offer-example.md.

E-Signature Integration (DocuSign)

When Louis wants offer letters sent for electronic signature through DocuSign instead of printed signature lines:

What the API CAN do (via Composio DocuSign toolkit):

  • LIST / GET templates — inspect what exists and read field definitions
  • CREATE envelope from template — DOCUSIGN_CREATE_ENVELOPE_FROM_TEMPLATE (map candidate → signer role, send for signature)
  • SEND / track / download — SEND_ENVELOPE, GET_ENVELOPE (status), RETRIEVE_ENVELOPE_DOCUMENTS (signed PDF)

What the API CANNOT do:

  • Cannot create a new template. Template creation (uploading a PDF, placing Signature/Date/Name tabs) is a DocuSign web UI task only. No Composio or DocuSign eSignature API action exists for this. This is a hard limitation — don't waste time searching for a "create template" tool.

PDF vs DocuSign (Louis Jul 26/27 2026 — FIRST CLASS)

Default delivery = branded PDF. DocuSign is not required for NC at-will offers. What matters: clear signed acceptance + I-9 before start + file in Drive 03 – PEOPLE/Letters/.

PDF only (default) DocuSign (optional)
Store staff (Server/Host/Cook/Dish…) Remote / multi-store (Coach)
In-person or easy photo/scan back Senior (GM/Coach) when Louis wants timestamp + chase
Don't block hire on e-sign setup Explicit “send DocuSign” / “create template”

Rule: default PDF; DocuSign when Louis/HR says remote or senior. Never block hiring on Composio DocuSign OAuth.

Template inventory: by role, not store×role (~12 masters for 5 stores). Catalog + live IDs: references/offer-letter-docusign-catalog.md.
Live coach template: Wiserise Offer Letter — Regional People Coach · id ab2765fd-29b6-4e2b-a642-2599d698b583 · role Candidate.

“open the link” after a DocuSign test: open Gmail DocuSign mail → Review / View Completed → Chrome tab + activate. Prefer completed envelope if both waiting + completed exist.

One-time setup (web UI — drive Louis's Chrome on CDP 9333 if available):

  1. Generate the DocuSign-blank branded PDF (coach pack: templates/sally-coach-offer-template.html / Desktop Wiserise_Offer_TEMPLATE_Regional_People_Coach_DocuSign.pdf; other roles: same blank rule on offer_letter_template.html)
  2. Log into DocuSign web UI → Templates → New → Upload the PDF
  3. Drag tabs onto blank underlines:
  4. Signature → SIGNATURE line
  5. Name → PRINT NAME (and/or TO if left blank)
  6. Date Signed → bottom DATE
  7. Optional Text → letter DATE / Start / sign-by if those underlines are blank
  8. Set signer role name to "Candidate"
  9. Category = Employment Contracts (required or Next is a no-op)
  10. Save as "Wiserise Offer Letter" (or role-specific name)
  11. Capture the template ID for future API sends

After setup — sending from Hermes (API path — only if Composio DocuSign is Active):

DOCUSIGN_CREATE_ENVELOPE_FROM_TEMPLATE
  template_id = "{from setup step 6}"
  template_roles = [{"roleName":"Candidate", "name":"{Name}", "email":"{email}"}]
  email_subject = "Offer Letter — {Role} — Wiserise Hospitality Group"
  status = "sent"

Composio DocuSign connection quirk (locked):

COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS(toolkits=["docusign"]) fails hard with no redirect URL: "Composio does not manage auth for toolkit docusign…" Do not retry-loop. DocuSign = bring-your-own OAuth (Integration Key + Secret).

Custom OAuth runbook (2026-07-27): references/docusign-composio-oauth.md
- Auth config: nested auth_config.type=use_custom_auth + authScheme=OAUTH2
- Link: POST /api/v3/connected_accounts/link → open redirect_url immediately
- Script: ~/.hermes/profiles/wise_ops/scripts/docusign_composio_connect.py
- Playwright OK for Apps-and-Keys after Louis types password
- Never treat login CSRF __RequestVerificationToken / random HTML inputs as client_secret
- OAuth "client id … not registered" → create/fix real IK on apps-d; stale env ID invalid

Default send until connected_accounts DocuSign=ACTIVE = Chrome CDP (:9333). Dropbox Sign ≠ DocuSign.

LIVE SEND — Chrome CDP (proven Jul 26 2026 · Sally Park)

Prerequisite (Louis 7-26 CRITICAL): Draft PDF already shown in this thread and Louis said send / approved / yes.
Same-breath create docusign and send to {name} with no prior draft MEDIA → run E2E Steps 0–2 only (draft + show + STOP). Do not jump here.

When gate is clear:

  1. Dedupe (Brain offer_sent / same name today) → ask resend if needed.
  2. PDF ready — filled one-off preferred (Wiserise_Offer_{Name}_*.pdf).
  3. CDP → https://apps.docusign.com/send/prepare until input[type=file] exists.
  4. Category → EmploymentContracts (native setter + change). Required or Next is silent no-op.
  5. Upload: DOM.setFileInputFiles with local path [str(pdf)] (path works on Louis Chrome).
  6. Expand [data-qa=add-recipients-slider] + add-message-slider.
  7. Native-set React fields: recipient-name, recipient-email, prepare-subject (Offer Letter — {Role} · Wiserise), prepare-message (short pay/start/I-9). Role = Needs to Sign.
  8. Click footer-add-fields-link → wait /add-fields.
  9. Auto-place is enough: if banner says Signature + Date Signed placed, do not fight drag-drop. Optional Name only if missing.
  10. Click footer-send-button. Success = URL /send/sent/{envelope_id} + body "Agreement sent".
  11. Brain workforce_audit_log event_type=offer_sent (envelope_id, email, pdf_path).
  12. Reply Louis: To · subject · PDF · envelope_id · Agreement sent · “reply offer signed {Name} when done”.

Templates & scripts

templates/offer_letter_template.html — HTML offer letter template for PDF output. Copy and modify for any role. Key features (v1.1): - Pre-filled DATE / TO / FROM (not blank form lines) - Two-column THE ROLE + PAY & TERMS; hourly = training → after training; salary = owner figure + review ceiling - Max 3 bullets role / do / don't - Weekly schedule commented out by default (keep for travel roles) - Plain acceptance + candidate signature only - Print CSS tuned for 1-page output

scripts/offer_letter_draft.py — Draft-only (never sends). Coach/generic HTML→1-page PDF on Desktop + prints Slack MEDIA lines. Always run before Louis gate unless HTML already built.

scripts/offer_letter_docx_builder.py — Word .docx builder (python-docx). Edit the ROLE_DATA, RESPONSIBILITIES, TERMS, SCOPE_DO, SCOPE_DONT sections near the top, run the script, output goes to ~/Desktop/Wiserise_Offer_Letter_{Role}.docx. All brand elements (navy band, gold accents, tinted tables, scope panels, signature block) are inline. Includes verify_docx() helper to check cell shading via XML parse.

references/offer-letter-e2e-workflow.md — Canonical send runbook v1.1: intake → draft → show ⭐ → dedupe → DocuSign/hr@ → Brain offer_sent → offer signed → Drive + offer_signed. Stuck ladder + copy-paste phrases.

references/one-page-pdf-fitting.md — condensed technique for getting content-rich HTML letters onto exactly 1 page. Read before building any HTML→PDF letter. Covers two-column layouts, break-inside:avoid grouping, print CSS margins, iterative tightening values table, and verification with pdftoppm + vision_analyze.

How to generate the PDF

"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" \
  --headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox \
  --print-to-pdf="{output_pdf_path}" \
  --print-to-pdf-no-header \
  "file://{html_path}"

No execute_code needed — use write_file for HTML, terminal for Chrome PDF generation.

One-page PDF fitting technique (NON-TRIVIAL — read before building)

Getting a content-rich letter to fit on exactly 1 page requires multiple CSS techniques. Documented here so you don't rediscover them:

1. Two-column layout for bullet-heavy sections

When two sections both have bullet lists (e.g. THE ROLE + PAY & TERMS), put them side-by-side in a CSS grid:

.two-col-content { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:0 24px; padding:0 34px; }

This halves the vertical space those sections consume.

2. Group section header + content, prevent page-break between them

If a section header sits at the bottom of page 1, its content gets pushed to page 2, leaving 30% white space. Wrap header + content in a div with break-inside:avoid:

<div class="scope-wrap" style="break-inside:avoid">
  <div class="section"><h2>...</h2></div>
  <div class="two-col">...</div>
</div>

3. Print media query with tight margins

The screen layout and print layout are different. Always include:

@media print {
  @page { size:Letter; margin:5mm }  /* 5mm, not 7mm — saves ~4mm top + bottom */
  body { background:#fff; padding:0 }
  .sheet { box-shadow:none; border-radius:0; max-width:none; overflow:visible }
  /* compact ALL spacing values for print */
  .band { padding:8px 34px }
  h1 { font-size:24px }
  .section { padding-top:6px }
  .section h2 { margin-bottom:4px }
  .content { font-size:11px }
  .col-block ol li { font-size:10px }
  .sign .slot .line { height:28px }
  footer { margin-top:6px; padding-top:4px; padding-bottom:0 }
  * { -webkit-print-color-adjust:exact; print-color-adjust:exact }
}

4. Iterative tightening

If content still spills to page 2, reduce these values incrementally: - Section padding-top (10px → 8px → 6px) - Content font-size (13px → 12px → 11px) - Table cell height (36px → 30px → 24px) - Signature line height (38px → 30px → 26px) - Col-block padding (14px → 12px → 10px → 8px) - Footer margin-top (26px → 18px → 12px → 8px)

5. Verify page count with pdfinfo + pdftoppm

Use pdfinfo first — it's the reliable page count. pdftoppm can generate extra blank PNGs that mislead:

pdfinfo "{pdf_path}" | grep Pages   # Pages: 1 = 1 page ✅
pdftoppm -png -r 200 "{pdf_path}" "{preview_prefix}"   # for visual inspection

Then use vision_analyze on the preview PNG to check layout quality.

6. Previewing .docx when Louis says "show me"

Build a parallel HTML version (same content, same template), Chrome to PDF, pdftoppm to PNG, share as MEDIA. Do NOT use textutil (drops shading) or Chrome on file://*.docx (hangs).

Map the candidate's position to the band: - Training rate first — all new hires start at training rate ($7.25/hr staff, $15/hr managers) - Band rate after Gate 2 — once training passes, the role's band rate kicks in - For salaried roles (GM, Regional Coach): use the salary Louis specifies, not REF-002

Common Pitfalls

  1. {{PLACEHOLDER}} tokens on offer PDF. Louis: leave blank where DocuSign inputs. Empty underlines + optional gold DS hints only. 0b. Filling Signature / Print Name / Date on the PDF. DocuSign owns those three lines — always empty on template and one-off PDFs. 0c. Blank underlines → 2-page PDF. Re-check pdfinfo; tighten meta/accept/sign heights before deliver. 0d. Treating "letter ≠ form" as ban on all blanks. Send-ready one-offs fill DATE/TO/start; DocuSign masters intentionally blank variable lines. Don't re-fill sign block "to look complete."

  2. Content spilling to page 2. Use the one-page fitting technique above. Two-column layouts + break-inside:avoid + tight print CSS. Verify with pdftoppm.

  3. Using form_html_builder for letters. Forms have blank fill-in fields. Letters have pre-filled content. Use the letter template, not the form builder.
  4. Inventing pay rates. Always pull from REF-002 or confirm with Louis. Never guess.
  5. Missing signature block. Every letter must have SIGNATURE / PRINT NAME / DATE (candidate only — not dual Owner+Candidate lines from old plain drafts).
  6. Sending without approval. Always show Louis the PDF before first deliver. No cold sends of unreviewed drafts. 5z. DocuSign / email send gate (Louis 2026-07-26 · CRITICAL). DRAFT → SHOW → YES → SEND. Same-breath “send to X” with no draft shown yet → still show first. Only skip re-show if this thread already has the approved draft MEDIA and he says send/approved. After send: Brain offer_sent. After sign: offer signed {Name} → Brain offer_signed + Drive. Dedupe before every send. 5b. Treating a dropped PDF as final. If Louis says "try this" / attaches an old offer, rebuild into brand v1.1 — do not only rate or lightly edit the plain file. 5l. Composio DocuSign manage-connections fails (no redirect). Don't loop. Use CDP live send (references/docusign-live-send-cdp.md). 5m. React recipient fields need native value setter on [data-qa=recipient-name|recipient-email|prepare-subject|prepare-message] + input/change. 5n. CDP upload with local path array on input[type=file]; confirm filename in page text.

5o. No Brain offer_sent / offer_signed. Envelope id only in Slack gets lost. Always audit log on send and on sign (E2E Steps 4 + 5b). 5p. Double-send. Step 3b dedupe: same name today or offer_sent last 7d → ask resend before CDP. 5q. GM draft without locked pay. Stop and ask Louis salary+KPI once. Hourly without live REF-002 = wrong pay. 5r. hr@ from louis@. HR sends = hr@ only · cc louis@ · real gmail id before claiming sent. 5s. Auto-place Signature + Date Signed is enough to Send on one-off envelopes. Don't block on Name drag unless missing/Louis asks. 5t. Send success signal = URL /send/sent/{envelope_id} + body "Agreement sent" (not merely clicking Send). 5u. Conflicting “send = yes” vs draft gate. Prefer E2E gate always. Only treat send as yes when this thread already showed the draft PDF. 5v. Forcing DocuSign for every hire. Louis: PDF is enough for most store roles. DocuSign optional for remote/senior only (PDF vs DocuSign above). 5w. Per-store offer templates (×5 Server, etc.). Wrong. One template per role; store is a blank/pre-fill. See references/offer-letter-docusign-catalog.md. 5x. _DocuSign PDF is 2 pages on envelope. Master must stay pdfinfo = 1 before upload; 2-page sends confuse candidates — fix HTML tighten, don't ship. 5c. Forcing hourly training→band on salaried coach/GM offers. Owner-set monthly salary (+ KPI if Louis adds it); REF-002 is for hourly seats. 5d. Year-only pay after Louis said dual. Show every $ as mo / yr (salary, pool, each KPI, max). 5e. KPI table without pay cadence / scorer. Not send-ready — ask or leave explicit [when paid] / [who scores] only if still drafting. 5f. Jargon in KPI goals ("SAFE") without plain English — candidate must understand without HQ slang. 5g. Repeating full pay math in both PAY and a long KPI banner — KPI note = rules only. 5h. Fat PAY & TERMS (8–10 bullets). Louis wants ≤6: salary · KPI · max · hours · travel · start. 5i. Hours without daily window after he asked start/complete — put start–end in PAY + schedule HOURS column. 5j. Mileage-only travel on coach offer after he said car rental + gas + hotel (receipts). 5k. Onboarding KPI means = only "I-9 + train" — use Completed onboarding checklist + train done. 6. Treating letters as SOPs. Letters don't get sops table rows or series numbers. They are per-recipient documents saved to Drive. 7. Missing at-will statement. Use plain NC wording: "This is at-will work in North Carolina (either side can end it)."

  1. textutil -convert html drops cell shading — do NOT use it to preview .docx letters. macOS textutil converts .docx to HTML but strips table cell background colors (navy header band, tinted position table, green/orange scope panels all vanish). The letter looks broken in the preview when the actual .docx is fine. To verify a .docx letter: (a) open it in Word/Pages, (b) parse word/document.xml with zipfile + ElementTree and check <w:shd> fill attributes (the verify_docx() function in the builder script does this), or (c) use LibreOffice soffice --headless --convert-to pdf then pdftoppm for a PNG preview. Never trust a textutil HTML conversion as a visual check.

  2. Chrome headless times out on file:// .docx URLs. Google Chrome --headless --print-to-pdf "file:///path/to/file.docx" hangs (60s+ timeout, no output). Chrome cannot render .docx directly. To get a PDF from a .docx, use LibreOffice (if installed) or convert to HTML via textutil first (accepting the shading loss), then Chrome the HTML — but for a true visual check, just open in Word/Pages.

  3. break-inside:avoid on .accept-wrap can push the entire acceptance block to page 2. If the acceptance + signature block is the last section and doesn't fit in the remaining page 1 space, break-inside:avoid forces the WHOLE block to page 2, leaving 15-20% white space at the bottom of page 1. Fix: remove break-inside:avoid from .accept-wrap (let it split across pages if needed), or reduce content above it so the block fits. pdfinfo will confirm the actual page count.

  4. pdftoppm can generate extra blank PNGs. If pdfinfo says 1 page but pdftoppm produces 2 PNGs, the 2nd PNG is a rendering artifact (91%+ white). Always verify page count with pdfinfo | grep Pages first, then use pdftoppm only for visual inspection of real pages.

  5. Previewing .docx when Louis says "show me". You can't open Word/Pages headlessly, textutil drops shading, and Chrome hangs on .docx. The working approach: build a parallel HTML version of the same letter (same content, same brand template), Chrome the HTML to PDF, pdftoppm to PNG, vision_analyze to verify, share the PNG as MEDIA:. The .docx remains the deliverable; the HTML/PNG is just the preview.

  6. DocuSign templates can ONLY be created in the web UI — not via API. Composio's DocuSign toolkit has list/send/download but NO "create template" action. When Louis asks for a DocuSign template, you must drive the browser (Templates → Create → Upload PDF → drag fields). Don't waste time searching for an API template-creation tool — it doesn't exist. See references/docusign-template-creation.md.

  7. macOS native file picker (NSOpenPanel) is AX-unreachable. When driving a browser to upload a file (e.g. DocuSign template creation), the "Open" dialog doesn't expose its buttons through the accessibility tree — get_window_state returns only the menu bar. Cmd+Shift+G → type path → Enter is unreliable. The reliable path: use CDP DOM.setFileInputFiles to inject the file directly into the <input type="file"> element — no native picker needed. See references/docusign-template-creation.md → "CDP file injection" for the proven Python script. If CDP is unavailable, ask Louis to manually pick the file.

14b. DocuSign template Category is REQUIRED — "Next" silently does nothing without it. On the Create Template page, the Category dropdown (marked *) must be set (e.g. "Employment Contracts") or the "Next: Add Fields" button fires zero feedback and stays put. Set via CDP Runtime.evaluate (React select needs native value setter + change event). See references/docusign-template-creation.md → "Category is REQUIRED".

14c. DocuSign field drag-drop is flaky — prefer auto-place on one-off send. On /add-fields, DocuSign often auto-places Signature + Date Signed ("Review all automatically placed…"). If auto-place landed, click Send. Synthetic HTML5 drag is unreliable. Only ask Louis to drag when auto-place missed required tabs (template setup still usually needs human drags once). 14d. One-off envelope ≠ template. "create docusign and send to Sally" = prepare envelope with her filled PDF, not necessarily save a reusable template first. Template master is optional for repeat roles.

  1. Composio DocuSign auto-connect fails. Need custom auth — references/docusign-composio-oauth.md. Blocks API until ACTIVE; CDP still OK.

  2. CSRF as secret (2026-07-27). __RequestVerificationToken (e.g. AdYyc6ny…) ≠ Integration Secret. Only Apps and Keys → Add Secret Key.

  3. Stale IK in env. DOCUSIGN_CLIENT_ID can still be "not registered" on prod OAuth — verify/create on apps-d + redirect URI.

  4. Playwright connect. Drive CDP for keys/OAuth; stop at password for Louis, then finish.

Wiserise File Intake

First Principle

A company file system has one job: keep the real file safe and make the current version easy to find. Everything else must support that job.

Four non-negotiable rules follow from this:

  1. One original — Google Drive holds the original file. Archive, never delete.
  2. One index — Supabase file_index tells Hermes what it is, who owns it, its status, and where it lives. Never read file metadata from Sheets or Obsidian.
  3. One current version — only one file version can be ACTIVE for the same document. New versions get v02, v03. Never overwrite signed files.
  4. No guessing — unclear, private, duplicate, unreadable, or incomplete files go to 99 Inbox — Needs Review. Louis decides.

First-principles split: Capture is mandatory and fast. Classification, approval, sharing, and downstream work are separate routing decisions. Do not block preservation because a classification detail is unknown.

Architecture

Pillar/Utility Intake Role Rule
🧠 Brain (Supabase) file_index table = one index of all files One ledger. Never read file metadata from Sheets or Obsidian.
⚡ Hermes Sole worker — reads file, classifies, stores, indexes No sub-agents. execute_code runs silently.
💬 Slack Where files arrive + where Hermes replies Staff uploads file → Hermes replies with status. Never show terminal.
📁 Drive Original file storage — the legal copy Push from Brain. Original is always safe here.
📊 Sheets View only — file index dashboard Refreshed from Brain, never entered directly.
🔬 NotebookLM Research only — ingests approved files Never replaces Drive or Brain.

The loop:

File arrives (💬 Slack / email)
→ Verify readable bytes + hash the file (⚡ Hermes)
→ Capture the original in Drive + create a minimal Brain record (📁 + 🧠)
→ Identify and assign confidence (⚡ Hermes)
→ Clear file → normal folder; unclear/high-risk → 99 Inbox — Needs Review
→ Reconcile Drive ID, Brain row, audit events, and Slack reply
→ Route downstream work to People, Legal, Finance, or Ops (⭐ human gate when needed)

The Only Four Intake Stages

1. Capture    — preserve the file safely + create a minimal Brain row
2. Identify   — classify with confidence, or route to review
3. Route      — clear files to the normal folder; unclear/high-risk to Needs Review
4. Reconcile  — confirm Drive ID, Brain row, audit events, Slack reply, and recover failures

Intake routes files to downstream workflows. It does not fully process discipline, legal review, approvals, or employee verification — those are separate skills (People, Finance, Legal).

1. Capture (mandatory, fast, unconditional)

Goal: the file is safe and findable within seconds. Classification is NOT required to capture.

  1. Verify that real bytes were cached and are readable (not an HTML login page).
  2. A Slack attachment notice is NOT proof of download. Verify the cached file's MIME type/size can be read.
  3. If download failed → reply with download-failed template, stop. Never search Desktop, Downloads, or screenshots to "find" the upload.
  4. If a teammate's upload was silently dropped (no reply at all) → likely not on the Slack allowlist (SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS in ~/.hermes/.env). See references/slack-upload-dropped-diagnosis.md.
  5. Compute the file hash (digital fingerprint).
  6. Check file_index for the same hash before uploading.
  7. Match found → stop. Link existing file_id, log duplicate_linked, send duplicate reply. No new copy.
  8. No match → continue.
  9. Upload the original to Drive — pick the best folder by filename/store hint; if unclear, upload to 99 Inbox — Needs Review/. See references/drive-structure.md for the folder map.
  10. Capture the Drive file ID and build drive_url (https://drive.google.com/file/d/{drive_file_id}/view).
  11. Allocate File ID: query Brain for max sequence for {DEPT}-{TYPE}-{YEAR} prefix → increment → insert. Retry on unique-constraint collision.
  12. Create a minimal file_index row: file_id, original_filename, normalized_filename, file_hash, drive_file_id, drive_url, source, sender, status = INBOX, review_status = pending.
  13. Create the first audit event: received.

Completion gate: file exists in Drive AND Brain row exists with hash + Drive link. If either fails → enter Recovery (Stage 4). Do NOT proceed to Identify.

2. Identify (classify with confidence, or route to review)

Read the file (filename, text, layout, dates, names, amounts) and assign:

Required decision DB value (use EXACTLY this) Human label
Department ops, finance, people, growth, marketing, technology, legal_admin, hq Ops, Finance, People, Growth, Marketing, Tech, Legal/Admin, HQ
Scope company, brand, store Company, Brand, Store
File type (free text — no constraint) Lease, contract, permit, insurance, invoice, employee file, SOP/form, inspection, LOI/site, other
Sensitivity team, internal, confidential, restricted Team, Internal, Confidential, Restricted
Status INBOX, NEEDS_REVIEW, DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, EXPIRED, ARCHIVED same
Review status pending, approved, rejected, not_required Pending, Approved, Rejected, Not Required
Extraction confidence high, medium, low High, Medium, Low

⚠️ Case matters. The DB enforces CHECK constraints. Using human-readable labels ("Legal/Admin", "Store", "Confidential") causes constraint violation (error 23514). See references/supabase-constraints.md.

Scope composite constraint: - company → brand_key NULL AND store_number NULL - brand → brand_key NOT NULL AND store_number NULL - store → store_number NOT NULL

Extra facts by file type (add to extracted_facts when relevant):

File type Extra facts
Lease store, landlord, start/end date, renewal notice, rent
Contract parties, dates, value if known, signature status
Permit / license store, agency, issue and expiration date
Insurance carrier, policy number, coverage dates
Invoice vendor, invoice number, amount, due date, payment status
Employee file employee ID, subtype, effective date
SOP / form audience, review date, approval date
Inspection store, agency, date, result, due date
LOI / site file market, address, stage, counterparty, dates

If any required decision is unclear → assign low confidence, route to Needs Review in Stage 3. Do NOT block capture — the file is already safe.

Update the Brain row with classification. Create audit event: classified.

3. Route (classify outcome → normal folder or Needs Review)

Finding Action
Exact duplicate (caught in Stage 1) Already linked. Send duplicate reply. Done.
Clear, low-risk, high confidence Set status = ACTIVE, review_status = not_required. File to normal Drive folder.
Unclear / missing facts / low confidence Set status = NEEDS_REVIEW. File stays in 99 Inbox — Needs Review/.
High-risk (lease, contract, insurance, employee, payroll, tax, permit) Captured + indexed as NEEDS_REVIEW. Human gate controls status/access/sharing — NOT preservation.
Signed file Captured as NEEDS_REVIEW. Never overwrite. New versions get v02, v03.

Never automatically share, delete, change access, mark final, sign, or replace high-risk files. Human review controls status, access, sharing, and downstream action — not basic preservation. Never block preservation because approval is pending.

Downstream routing (intake routes, doesn't fully process):

File type Routes to
Employee/coaching/discipline/termination People workflow → cross-ref workforce_employees + run people_ladder_file.py
Lease/contract/legal Legal review → Louis approves
Invoice/finance/banking Finance review → Yumi/Louis
Equipment/ops Ops workflow → ticket if needed

Create audit events: stored (if folder confirmed) → indexed (if not already).

4. Reconcile (confirm + recover)

Drive upload and Brain write are separate systems — failures have defined recovery states.

Reconcile checklist: 1. Drive file ID captured in file_index.drive_file_id and drive_url. 2. Brain row exists with correct hash and all required fields. 3. Duplicate check completed (hash before upload; post-upload link if found). 4. Audit events created: received → classified → stored → indexed. 5. Slack reply sent with correct template (see references/slack-reply-templates.md). 6. For people files: workforce_employees cross-reference done. 7. For discipline photos: people_ladder_file.py run (or ladder blocked reported).

Recovery states:

Failure State Recovery
Drive OK, Brain fails INDEX_PENDING Retry Brain insert with same hash + Drive ID. Check hash first.
Brain OK, Drive fails STORAGE_PENDING Retry Drive upload. If hash exists in Brain, link existing record.
Both fail CAPTURE_FAILED Re-download from source. If source gone, report to Louis.
Duplicate found post-upload duplicate_linked Link existing file_id. Delete redundant Drive copy only if original confirmed intact.

Recovery rules: - Every retry is duplicate-safe (check hash before insert). - Never create a second Brain row for the same hash. - Never overwrite an existing Drive file (new version = v02, v03). - After 2 failed retries → set NEEDS_REVIEW + report to Slack for Louis.

People-File Cross-Reference

When a file names a person (employee, coaching, discipline, termination), always search workforce_employees by employee_name (ilike, service role key — anon key returns 0 rows due to RLS).

  • Found → link workforce_employees.id to file_index.entity_name, note employee's current status.
  • Not found → flag in extracted_facts as employee_in_brain: false. This is a compliance risk (possible off-system hire). Set review_status: pending, escalate to Louis. Do NOT create an employee record yourself.

The name column is employee_name — NOT name, NOT full_name. When unsure of a table's columns, query ?select=*&limit=1 first.

Discipline Ladder Write (MANDATORY after coaching/warning/probation/termination photos)

After file_index is written for a discipline notice, also write one ladder row:

python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/people_ladder_file.py file --file-id {FILE-ID}
# express lane only (theft/violence/safety):
python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/people_ladder_file.py file --file-id {FILE-ID} --express

The script: reads file_index + extracted_facts → maps conversation type → level → enforces ladder order (Warning needs Coaching, etc.) unless --express → inserts ladder row (unique on file_id, safe to re-run) → updates employee's coaching_date / warning_date / probation_start (never auto-terminates).

Required extracted_facts keys: employee_name, position, manager, incident_date, conversation_type, policy_areas, observed_behavior, signatures, employee_in_brain, optional employee_commitment_questions, coaching_conversation_notes, form_signed_manager_date.

If ladder order is violated → ladder row NOT written → send ladder-blocked template.

Brain Writes

file_index insert (Supabase REST)

POST https://kwadpofhzjpmmahlrefj.supabase.co/rest/v1/file_index
Headers: apikey + Authorization (service role key), Prefer: return=representation

Required fields: file_id, original_filename, normalized_filename, file_hash, drive_file_id, department, file_type, scope, status, sensitivity, source, sender, version. Always include drive_url (NOT drive_link — causes PGRST204).

file_audit_log insert

Columns: file_index_id (FK → file_index.id), action, actor, details (jsonb).

⚠️ Action enum — only: received, classified, duplicate_linked, stored, indexed, reviewed, approved, rejected, shared, superseded, expired, archived. Create one event per lifecycle step, not a single "INTAKE" event.

File ID + sequence allocation

File ID: {DEPT}-{TYPE}-{YEAR}-{SEQUENCE}
Filename: YYYY-MM-DD__DEPT__SCOPE__TYPE__SHORT-NAME__v01.ext

Query Brain for max existing sequence for the prefix, increment, insert. If insert hits unique constraint (concurrent upload), re-query and retry. Never assume the next number.

Automation Gate

Automate only after ten real low-risk files pass all checks (correct Drive folder, correct index record, no duplicate, correct type/scope/status, audit event exists). Never automate deletion, access changes, signatures, final approvals, or high-risk file processing.

Done Checklist

  • [ ] File downloaded and readable (real bytes, not HTML login page)
  • [ ] Capture complete: original in Drive + minimal Brain row with hash + Drive URL
  • [ ] File identified (department, scope, type, sensitivity) OR routed to Needs Review
  • [ ] Duplicate check completed (hash before upload)
  • [ ] Drive file ID and drive_url written to Brain row
  • [ ] Audit events: received → classified → stored → indexed
  • [ ] Recovery state cleared (no INDEX_PENDING / STORAGE_PENDING)
  • [ ] Discipline photo → people_ladder_file.py run (or blocked reported)
  • [ ] High-risk file → captured as NEEDS_REVIEW + human gate
  • [ ] Slack reply sent with correct template
  • [ ] No terminal output shown in Slack
  • [ ] Brain is the one truth — no file metadata from Sheets/Obsidian

Common Pitfalls

Reference: references/supabase-constraints.md contains the full CHECK constraint definitions. Consult it if you hit error 23514.

  1. Blocking capture on classification. The file must be in Drive + Brain before classification. Never delay preservation because department or scope is unclear.
  2. Guessing when unsure. Route to Needs Review. Never file a guess. But always capture the file first — preservation does not require classification.
  3. Treating Drive + Brain as one atomic transaction. They are separate systems. If one fails, use recovery states (INDEX_PENDING, STORAGE_PENDING) and retry duplicate-safe.
  4. Treating a Slack attachment notice as proof of download. Always verify real bytes were cached and readable. Never search Desktop/Downloads for the upload.
  5. Showing terminal output in Slack. Never show curl, python3, pymupdf, or shell commands. Use execute_code silently.
  6. Overwriting signed files. Signed or approved files are immutable. New versions get a new filename (v02, v03).
  7. Auto-filing high-risk files. Lease, contract, insurance, employee, payroll, tax, permit files need human review before status changes — but they ARE captured and indexed as NEEDS_REVIEW immediately.
  8. Forgetting the duplicate check. Always check file hash before uploading. Uploading a duplicate creates confusion.
  9. Not replying in Slack. Always reply with the result — even if it's "I couldn't identify this."
  10. Creating new folders during intake. Use the existing Drive structure. See references/drive-structure.md.
  11. Deleting instead of archiving. Archive, never delete. Legal, finance, tax, payroll, People, signed, permit, and insurance files are never auto-deleted.
  12. Wrong DB enum case. department = legal_admin not "Legal/Admin". scope = store not "Store". sensitivity = confidential not "Confidential". review_status = pending not "PENDING". Causes CHECK violation (error 23514).
  13. Wrong audit action enum. Only: received, classified, duplicate_linked, stored, indexed, reviewed, approved, rejected, shared, superseded, expired, archived. No "INTAKE".
  14. Violating scope composite constraint. scope=store → store_number NOT NULL. scope=company → both brand_key + store_number NULL. scope=brand → brand_key NOT NULL + store_number NULL.
  15. Forgetting normalized_filename. It is NOT NULL. Always include it.
  16. Using drive_link instead of drive_url. The column is drive_url. Using drive_link causes PGRST204.
  17. Not cross-referencing people files. When a file names an employee, always search workforce_employees.employee_name (ilike, service role key). If not found → compliance risk (off-system hire) → escalate to Louis.
  18. Coaching photo filed but no ladder row. After discipline photos, run people_ladder_file.py file --file-id …. file_index alone is not the discipline record.
  19. File ID sequence collision. Always query max sequence for the prefix, increment, handle unique-constraint violation by re-query + retry.
  20. Leaving a file in recovery state without reporting. If INDEX_PENDING or STORAGE_PENDING persists after 2 retries → set NEEDS_REVIEW + report to Slack. Never silently leave a file half-captured.

Pathagents/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent

Hermes Agent is an open-source AI agent framework by Nous Research that runs in your terminal, a native desktop app, messaging platforms, and IDEs. It's in the same category as Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex (OpenAI), and OpenClaw — autonomous coding and task-execution agents that use tool calling to interact with your system. Hermes works with any LLM provider (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, xAI, local models, and 20+ others) and runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, and WSL.

What makes Hermes different:

  • Self-improving through skills — Hermes learns from experience by saving reusable procedures as skills. When it solves a complex problem, discovers a workflow, or gets corrected, it can persist that knowledge as a skill document that loads into future sessions. Skills accumulate over time, making the agent better at your specific tasks and environment.
  • Persistent memory across sessions — remembers who you are, your preferences, environment details, and lessons learned. Pluggable memory backends (built-in, Honcho, Mem0, and more) let you choose how memory works.
  • Multi-platform gateway — the same agent runs on Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, iMessage, Signal, Matrix, Teams, Email, and a dozen more platforms with full tool access, not just chat.
  • Many surfaces — the same agent core drives the CLI, the Ink TUI, a native Electron desktop app, a web dashboard, and an ACP server for IDEs (VS Code / Zed / JetBrains).
  • Provider-agnostic — swap models and providers mid-workflow without changing anything else. Credential pools rotate across multiple API keys automatically.
  • Profiles — run multiple independent Hermes instances with isolated configs, sessions, skills, and memory.
  • Extensible — plugins, MCP servers, custom tools, webhook triggers, cron scheduling, and the full Python ecosystem.

People use Hermes for software development, research, system administration, data analysis, content creation, home automation, and anything else that benefits from an AI agent with persistent context and full system access.

This skill helps you work with Hermes Agent effectively — setting it up, configuring features, spawning additional agent instances, troubleshooting issues, finding the right commands and settings, and understanding how the system works when you need to extend or contribute to it.

Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/

Scope & Verification

This skill is a concise operating guide, not the complete source of truth for every Hermes feature. If a Hermes feature, command, or setting is not mentioned here, do not treat that absence as evidence that it does not exist. Check the live repository and official docs before giving a negative answer.

Good verification targets:

  • CLI commands: hermes --help, hermes <command> --help, and hermes_cli/main.py
  • User documentation: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/
  • Source tree: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

Quick Start

# Install (shell installer — sets up uv, Python, the venv, and the launcher)
curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash

# Or via PyPI (ships the TUI bundle + shell launcher)
pip install hermes-agent       # or: uv pip install hermes-agent

# Interactive chat (default surface; set display.interface: tui to launch the Ink TUI instead)
hermes

# Single query
hermes chat -q "What is the capital of France?"

# Setup wizard  /  pick model+provider  /  health check
hermes setup
hermes model
hermes doctor

# Other surfaces
hermes desktop                 # launch the native desktop app (alias: hermes gui)
hermes dashboard               # web admin panel + embedded chat
hermes proxy                   # OpenAI-compatible local proxy backed by your OAuth provider

Project Context Files

Hermes injects project-level instructions into the system prompt by reading context files from the working directory. The discovery order is first match wins — only one project context source is loaded per session.

File (in priority order) Discovery Use when
.hermes.md / HERMES.md Walks parents up to the git root, stops at git root You want hierarchical project rules (root + per-package overrides)
AGENTS.md / agents.md Cwd only — subdirectory and parent copies are ignored You want portable agent instructions that work the same in Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, etc.
CLAUDE.md / claude.md Cwd only Same as AGENTS.md, Claude-flavored
.cursorrules / .cursor/rules/*.mdc Cwd only Migrating from Cursor

SOUL.md (in $HERMES_HOME) is independent and always loaded when present — it sets the agent's identity, not project rules.

Pick the right one

  • Use .hermes.md when you want Hermes-specific behavior that lives above the cwd (root + subtree), or when you want rules to inherit from a parent directory. The parent walk stops at the git root, so a home-level .hermes.md won't leak into every project (a git repo's root is the boundary).
  • Use AGENTS.md when the same project will also be worked on by other agents (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode). Those tools all have their own conventions for AGENTS.md, and the "cwd only" contract keeps the file portable.
  • Don't put project rules in ~/.hermes/AGENTS.md (or any other home-level location). When Hermes runs with that directory as cwd, the file loads — but only for that one directory. For cross-project context, use SOUL.md (in $HERMES_HOME, identity-only) or install a skill via hermes skills install.

Size and truncation

Each context file is capped at 20,000 characters. Files longer than that get head + tail truncated (the middle is dropped, with a [...truncated...] marker). For large project rules, prefer splitting into multiple skills over cramming one file.

Security

All context files pass through the threat-pattern scanner before reaching the system prompt. Patterns matching prompt injection or promptware are replaced with a [BLOCKED: ...] placeholder. This means an AGENTS.md containing obvious injection attempts won't reach the model — the scanner blocks the content, not the file, so the rest of the file still loads.

Disable for one session

hermes --ignore-rules skips auto-injection of all project context files (.hermes.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules) and SOUL.md identity, plus user config, plugins, and MCP servers. Use it to isolate whether a problem is your setup or Hermes itself.

Example: a small .hermes.md

# My Project

Hermes: when working in this repo, follow these rules.

## Build
- Always run `make test` before declaring a change done.
- Use `uv run` for Python, not `pip install`.

## Style
- Prefer `pathlib.Path` over `os.path`.
- No `print()` in production code — use the `logger`.

That file at /home/me/projects/myrepo/.hermes.md is auto-loaded when Hermes runs in any subdirectory of /home/me/projects/myrepo, but not when it runs in /home/me/other-project.

Security & Privacy Toggles

Common "why is Hermes doing X to my output / tool calls / commands?" toggles — and the exact commands to change them. Most of these need a fresh session (/reset in chat, or start a new hermes invocation) because they're read once at startup.

Secret redaction in tool output

Secret redaction is on by default — tool output (terminal stdout, read_file, web content, subagent summaries, etc.) is scanned for strings that look like API keys, tokens, and secrets before it enters the conversation context and logs. Leave it enabled for normal use:

hermes config set security.redact_secrets true       # keep enabled globally

Restart required. security.redact_secrets is snapshotted at import time — toggling it mid-session (e.g. via export HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS=false from a tool call) will NOT take effect for the running process. Tell the user to change it in config from a terminal, then start a new session. This is deliberate — it prevents an LLM from flipping the toggle on itself mid-task.

Disable only when you deliberately need raw credential-like strings for debugging or redactor development:

hermes config set security.redact_secrets false

PII redaction in gateway messages

Separate from secret redaction. When enabled, the gateway hashes user IDs and strips phone numbers from the session context before it reaches the model:

hermes config set privacy.redact_pii true    # enable
hermes config set privacy.redact_pii false   # disable (default)

Command approval prompts

By default (approvals.mode: manual), Hermes prompts the user before running shell commands flagged as destructive (rm -rf, git reset --hard, etc.). The modes are:

  • manual — always prompt (default)
  • smart — use an auxiliary LLM to auto-approve low-risk commands, prompt on high-risk
  • off — skip all approval prompts (equivalent to --yolo)
hermes config set approvals.mode smart       # recommended middle ground
hermes config set approvals.mode off         # bypass everything (not recommended)

Per-invocation bypass without changing config: - hermes --yolo … - export HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1

Note: YOLO / approvals.mode: off does NOT turn off secret redaction. They are independent.

Shell hooks allowlist

Some shell-hook integrations require explicit allowlisting before they fire. Managed via ~/.hermes/shell-hooks-allowlist.json — prompted interactively the first time a hook wants to run.

Disabling the web/browser/image-gen tools

To keep the model away from network or media tools entirely, open hermes tools and toggle per-platform. Takes effect on next session (/reset). See the Tools & Skills section above.

Voice & Transcription

STT (Voice → Text)

Voice messages from messaging platforms are auto-transcribed.

Provider priority (auto-detected): 1. Local faster-whisper — free, no API key: pip install faster-whisper 2. Groq Whisper — free tier: set GROQ_API_KEY 3. OpenAI Whisper — paid: set VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY 4. Mistral Voxtral — set MISTRAL_API_KEY

Config:

stt:
  enabled: true
  provider: local        # local, groq, openai, mistral
  local:
    model: base          # tiny, base, small, medium, large-v3

TTS (Text → Voice)

Provider Env var Free?
Edge TTS None Yes (default)
ElevenLabs ELEVENLABS_API_KEY Free tier
OpenAI VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY Paid
MiniMax MINIMAX_API_KEY Paid
Mistral (Voxtral) MISTRAL_API_KEY Paid
NeuTTS (local) None (pip install neutts[all] + espeak-ng) Free

Voice commands: /voice on (voice-to-voice), /voice tts (always voice), /voice off.

Spawning Additional Hermes Instances

Run additional Hermes processes as fully independent subprocesses — separate sessions, tools, and environments.

When to Use This vs delegate_task

delegate_task Spawning hermes process
Isolation Separate conversation, shared process Fully independent process
Duration Minutes (bounded by parent loop) Hours/days
Tool access Subset of parent's tools Full tool access
Interactive No Yes (PTY mode)
Use case Quick parallel subtasks Long autonomous missions

One-Shot Mode

terminal(command="hermes chat -q 'Research GRPO papers and write summary to ~/research/grpo.md'", timeout=300)

# Background for long tasks:
terminal(command="hermes chat -q 'Set up CI/CD for ~/myapp'", background=true)

Interactive PTY Mode (via tmux)

Hermes uses prompt_toolkit, which requires a real terminal. Use tmux for interactive spawning:

# Start
terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s agent1 -x 120 -y 40 'hermes'", timeout=10)

# Wait for startup, then send a message
terminal(command="sleep 8 && tmux send-keys -t agent1 'Build a FastAPI auth service' Enter", timeout=15)

# Read output
terminal(command="sleep 20 && tmux capture-pane -t agent1 -p", timeout=5)

# Send follow-up
terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t agent1 'Add rate limiting middleware' Enter", timeout=5)

# Exit
terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t agent1 '/exit' Enter && sleep 2 && tmux kill-session -t agent1", timeout=10)

Multi-Agent Coordination

# Agent A: backend
terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s backend -x 120 -y 40 'hermes -w'", timeout=10)
terminal(command="sleep 8 && tmux send-keys -t backend 'Build REST API for user management' Enter", timeout=15)

# Agent B: frontend
terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s frontend -x 120 -y 40 'hermes -w'", timeout=10)
terminal(command="sleep 8 && tmux send-keys -t frontend 'Build React dashboard for user management' Enter", timeout=15)

# Check progress, relay context between them
terminal(command="tmux capture-pane -t backend -p | tail -30", timeout=5)
terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t frontend 'Here is the API schema from the backend agent: ...' Enter", timeout=5)

Session Resume

# Resume most recent session
terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s resumed 'hermes --continue'", timeout=10)

# Resume specific session
terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s resumed 'hermes --resume 20260225_143052_a1b2c3'", timeout=10)

Tips

  • Prefer delegate_task for quick subtasks — less overhead than spawning a full process
  • Use -w (worktree mode) when spawning agents that edit code — prevents git conflicts
  • Set timeouts for one-shot mode — complex tasks can take 5-10 minutes
  • Use hermes chat -q for fire-and-forget — no PTY needed
  • Use tmux for interactive sessions — raw PTY mode has \r vs \n issues with prompt_toolkit
  • For scheduled tasks, use the cronjob tool instead of spawning — handles delivery and retry

Durable & Background Systems

Four systems run alongside the main conversation loop. Quick reference here; full developer notes live in AGENTS.md, user-facing docs under website/docs/user-guide/features/.

Delegation (delegate_task)

Spawn a subagent with an isolated context + terminal session.

  • Single: delegate_task(goal, context).
  • Batch: delegate_task(tasks=[{goal, ...}, ...]) runs children in parallel, capped by delegation.max_concurrent_children (default 3).
  • Background: delegate_task(background=true) returns a handle immediately and keeps the parent loop going; the child's result re-enters the conversation as a new turn when it finishes.
  • Roles: leaf (default; cannot re-delegate) vs orchestrator (can spawn its own workers, bounded by delegation.max_spawn_depth).
  • Not durable. A backgrounded child is still process-local — if the parent process exits, the child is lost. For work that must outlive the process, use cronjob or terminal(background=True, notify_on_complete=True).

Config: delegation.* in config.yaml.

Cron (scheduled jobs)

Durable scheduler — cron/jobs.py + cron/scheduler.py. Drive it via the cronjob tool, the hermes cron CLI (list, add, edit, pause, resume, run, remove), or the /cron slash command.

  • Schedules: duration ("30m", "2h"), "every" phrase ("every monday 9am"), 5-field cron ("0 9 * * *"), or ISO timestamp.
  • Per-job knobs: skills, model/provider override, script (pre-run data collection; no_agent=True makes the script the whole job), context_from (chain job A's output into job B), workdir (run in a specific dir with its AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md loaded), multi-platform delivery.
  • Invariants: 3-minute hard interrupt per run, .tick.lock file prevents duplicate ticks across processes, cron sessions pass skip_memory=True by default, and cron deliveries are framed with a header/footer instead of being mirrored into the target gateway session (keeps role alternation intact).

User docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron

Curator (skill lifecycle)

Background maintenance for agent-created skills. Tracks usage, marks idle skills stale, archives stale ones, keeps a pre-run tar.gz backup so nothing is lost.

  • CLI: hermes curator <verb> — status, run, pause, resume, pin, unpin, archive, restore, prune, backup, rollback.
  • Slash: /curator <subcommand> mirrors the CLI.
  • Scope: only touches skills with created_by: "agent" provenance. Bundled + hub-installed skills are off-limits. Never deletes — max destructive action is archive. Pinned skills are exempt from every auto-transition and every LLM review pass.
  • Cost: the deterministic inactivity/prune sweep runs for free. The aux-model "consolidate overlapping skills into umbrellas" pass is off by default — opt in with curator.consolidate: true or hermes curator run --consolidate. Routine background curation costs zero tokens.
  • Telemetry: sidecar at ~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json holds per-skill use_count, view_count, patch_count, last_activity_at, state, pinned.

Config: curator.* (enabled, interval_hours, min_idle_hours, stale_after_days, archive_after_days, backup.*). User docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/curator

Kanban (multi-agent work queue)

Durable SQLite board for multi-profile / multi-worker collaboration. Users drive it via hermes kanban <verb>; dispatcher-spawned workers see a focused kanban_* toolset gated by HERMES_KANBAN_TASK, and orchestrator profiles can opt into the broader kanban toolset. Normal sessions still have zero kanban_* schema footprint unless configured.

  • CLI verbs (common): init, create, list (alias ls), show, assign, link, unlink, comment, complete, block, unblock, archive, tail. Less common: watch, stats, runs, log, dispatch, daemon, gc.
  • Worker/orchestrator toolset: kanban_show, kanban_complete, kanban_block, kanban_heartbeat, kanban_comment, kanban_create, kanban_link; profiles that explicitly enable the kanban toolset outside a dispatcher-spawned task also get kanban_list and kanban_unblock for board routing.
  • Dispatcher runs inside the gateway by default (kanban.dispatch_in_gateway: true) — reclaims stale claims, promotes ready tasks, atomically claims, spawns assigned profiles. Auto-blocks a task after failure_limit consecutive spawn failures (default 2; configurable via kanban.failure_limit or per-task max_retries).
  • Isolation: board is the hard boundary (workers get HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD pinned in env); tenant is a soft namespace within a board for workspace-path + memory-key isolation.

User docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/kanban

Surfaces & Other Capabilities

Beyond the CLI and gateway, a few things worth knowing about:

  • Desktop app (hermes desktop / hermes gui) — native Electron app for macOS/Linux/Windows: streaming chat, session list, drag-and-drop + clipboard-paste files, Cmd+K palette, status-bar model picker, rebindable shortcuts, native notifications, live subagent watch-windows, VS Code Marketplace themes, and per-profile remote-gateway login (OAuth or username/password) so a thin local GUI can drive a heavy remote agent.
  • Web dashboard (hermes dashboard) — full admin panel: configure every messaging channel, the MCP catalog, webhooks/hooks, memory, and a complete profile builder (model + skills + MCPs) from the browser, plus an embedded hermes --tui chat. Secured behind an OAuth/token gate.
  • OpenAI-compatible proxy (hermes proxy) — exposes a http://localhost:port OpenAI API backed by whichever OAuth provider you're signed into (Claude Pro, ChatGPT Pro, SuperGrok). Point Codex CLI, Aider, Cline, Continue, or any script at it — no API key.
  • Automation Blueprints — pick a named automation and Hermes asks for what it needs (no cron syntax). One definition renders as a dashboard form, a slash command, an agent conversation, and a docs-catalog entry.
  • memory tool batch operations — pass an operations array of add/replace/remove edits applied atomically against the final character budget, so a single call can free space and add entries even when an add alone would overflow.
  • session_search — FTS5-backed, no aux-LLM, effectively free. One tool, three modes inferred from which args are set: discovery (query), scroll (session_id + around_message_id), browse (no args).
  • xAI Grok via SuperGrok OAuth — sign in with your xAI account (no API key); includes Cursor's grok-composer-2.5-fast coding model.

Windows-Specific Quirks

Hermes runs natively on Windows (PowerShell, cmd, Windows Terminal, git-bash mintty, VS Code integrated terminal). Most of it just works, but a handful of differences between Win32 and POSIX have bitten us — document new ones here as you hit them so the next person (or the next session) doesn't rediscover them from scratch.

Input / Keybindings

Alt+Enter doesn't insert a newline — Windows Terminal (and mintty) grab it for fullscreen before prompt_toolkit sees it. Use Ctrl+Enter instead (the CLI binds it to newline on Windows; raw Ctrl+J does the same, harmlessly). To inspect how your terminal reports a keystroke, run python scripts/keystroke_diagnostic.py from the repo root.

Config / Files

HTTP 400 "No models provided" on first run — config.yaml was saved with a UTF-8 BOM (Notepad does this). Re-save as UTF-8 without BOM; hermes config edit writes correctly.

execute_code / Sandbox

WinError 10106 from the sandbox child process — it can't create an AF_INET socket. Root cause is usually Hermes's env scrubber dropping SYSTEMROOT/WINDIR/COMSPEC (Python's socket needs SYSTEMROOT to find mswsock.dll), not a broken Winsock LSP. The _WINDOWS_ESSENTIAL_ENV_VARS allowlist in tools/code_execution_tool.py covers it; if you still hit it, echo os.environ inside an execute_code block to confirm SYSTEMROOT is set.

Testing on Windows

scripts/run_tests.sh is POSIX-only (expects .venv/bin/activate); the Hermes-installed venv/Scripts/ has no pip/pytest (stripped for size). Install pytest into a system Python and run directly with -n 0 (pyproject.toml's addopts already sets -n):

"/c/Program Files/Python311/python" -m pip install --user pytest pytest-xdist pyyaml
export PYTHONPATH="$(pwd)"
"/c/Program Files/Python311/python" -m pytest tests/foo/test_bar.py -v --tb=short -n 0

(POSIX-only tests need skip guards — see the cross-platform guard list in the Contributor section below.)

Path / Filesystem

Line endings. Git may warn LF will be replaced by CRLF. Cosmetic — the repo's .gitattributes normalizes. Don't let editors auto-convert committed POSIX-newline files to CRLF.

Forward slashes work almost everywhere. C:/Users/... is accepted by every Hermes tool and most Windows APIs. Prefer forward slashes in code and logs — avoids shell-escaping backslashes in bash.

Troubleshooting

Voice not working

  1. Check stt.enabled: true in config.yaml
  2. Verify provider: pip install faster-whisper or set API key
  3. In gateway: /restart. In CLI: exit and relaunch.

Tool not available

  1. hermes tools — check if toolset is enabled for your platform
  2. Some tools need env vars (check .env)
  3. /reset after enabling tools

Model/provider issues

  1. hermes doctor — check config and dependencies
  2. hermes auth — re-authenticate OAuth providers (or hermes auth add <provider>)
  3. Check .env has the right API key
  4. Copilot 403: gh auth login tokens do NOT work for Copilot API. You must use the Copilot-specific OAuth device code flow via hermes model → GitHub Copilot.

Changes not taking effect

  • Tools/skills: /reset starts a new session with updated toolset
  • Config changes: In gateway: /restart. In CLI: exit and relaunch.
  • Code changes: Restart the CLI or gateway process

Skills not showing

  1. hermes skills list — verify installed
  2. hermes skills config — check platform enablement
  3. Load explicitly: /skill name or hermes -s name

Gateway issues

Check logs first:

grep -i "failed to send\|error" ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log | tail -20

Common gateway problems: - Gateway dies on SSH logout: Enable linger: sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER - Gateway dies on WSL2 close: WSL2 requires systemd=true in /etc/wsl.conf for systemd services to work. Without it, gateway falls back to nohup (dies when session closes). - Gateway crash loop: Reset the failed state: systemctl --user reset-failed hermes-gateway

Platform-specific issues

  • Discord bot silent: Must enable Message Content Intent in Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents.
  • Slack bot only works in DMs: Must subscribe to message.channels event. Without it, the bot ignores public channels.
  • Windows-specific issues (Alt+Enter newline, WinError 10106, UTF-8 BOM config, test suite, line endings): see the dedicated Windows-Specific Quirks section above.

Auxiliary models not working

If auxiliary tasks (vision, compression, session_search) fail silently, the auto provider can't find a backend. Either set OPENROUTER_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY, or explicitly configure each auxiliary task's provider:

hermes config set auxiliary.vision.provider <your_provider>
hermes config set auxiliary.vision.model <model_name>
