Contributor Quick Reference

For occasional contributors and PR authors. Full developer docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/

Project Layout

hermes-agent/
├── run_agent.py          # AIAgent — core conversation loop
├── model_tools.py        # Tool discovery and dispatch
├── toolsets.py           # Toolset definitions
├── cli.py                # Interactive CLI (HermesCLI)
├── hermes_state.py       # SQLite session store
├── agent/                # Prompt builder, context compression, memory, model routing, credential pooling, skill dispatch
├── hermes_cli/           # CLI subcommands, config, setup, commands
│   ├── commands.py       # Slash command registry (CommandDef)
│   ├── config.py         # DEFAULT_CONFIG, env var definitions
│   └── main.py           # CLI entry point and argparse
├── tools/                # One file per tool
│   └── registry.py       # Central tool registry
├── gateway/              # Messaging gateway
│   └── platforms/        # Platform adapters (telegram, discord, etc.)
├── cron/                 # Job scheduler
├── tests/                # Extensive pytest suite (run via scripts/run_tests.sh)
└── website/              # Docusaurus docs site

Config: ~/.hermes/config.yaml (settings), ~/.hermes/.env (API keys) — both under $HERMES_HOME when it is set.

Adding a Tool

Two files. Auto-discovery imports any tools/*.py with a top-level registry.register() call, but a tool is only exposed to an agent once its name appears in a toolset.

1. Create tools/your_tool.py:

import json, os
from tools.registry import registry

def check_requirements() -> bool:
    return bool(os.getenv("EXAMPLE_API_KEY"))

def example_tool(param: str, task_id: str = None) -> str:
    return json.dumps({"success": True, "data": "..."})

registry.register(
    name="example_tool",
    toolset="example",
    schema={"name": "example_tool", "description": "...", "parameters": {...}},
    handler=lambda args, **kw: example_tool(
        param=args.get("param", ""), task_id=kw.get("task_id")),
    check_fn=check_requirements,
    requires_env=["EXAMPLE_API_KEY"],
)

2. Wire it into a toolset in toolsets.py — add the name to _HERMES_CORE_TOOLS (every platform) or to a specific toolset.

All handlers must return JSON strings. Use get_hermes_home() for paths, never hardcode ~/.hermes. For custom/local-only tools, write a plugin in ~/.hermes/plugins/ instead of editing core — see the developer docs.

Adding a Slash Command

  1. Add CommandDef to COMMAND_REGISTRY in hermes_cli/commands.py
  2. Add handler in cli.py → process_command()
  3. (Optional) Add gateway handler in gateway/run.py

All consumers (help text, autocomplete, Telegram menu, Slack mapping) derive from the central registry automatically.

Agent Loop (High Level)

run_conversation():
  1. Build system prompt
  2. Loop while iterations < max:
     a. Call LLM (OpenAI-format messages + tool schemas)
     b. If tool_calls → dispatch each via handle_function_call() → append results → continue
     c. If text response → return
  3. Context compression triggers automatically near token limit

Testing

Use the canonical runner — it enforces CI-parity (hermetic env, unset credentials, TZ=UTC, xdist workers, per-test subprocess isolation):

scripts/run_tests.sh                          # full suite
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/             # one directory
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_x.py    # one file
scripts/run_tests.sh -v --tb=long             # pass-through pytest flags
  • Tests auto-redirect HERMES_HOME to temp dirs — never touch real ~/.hermes/.
  • The script probes .venv, then venv, then the shared worktree venv.
  • Windows: the wrapper is POSIX-only; see the Windows-Specific Quirks section above for the direct-pytest workaround.

Cross-platform test guards: tests using POSIX-only syscalls need a skip marker. Common ones already in the codebase: - Symlink creation → @pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="Symlinks require elevated privileges on Windows") (see tests/cron/test_cron_script.py) - POSIX file modes (0o600, etc.) → @pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform.startswith("win"), reason="POSIX mode bits not enforced on Windows") (see tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_toctou_file_modes.py) - signal.SIGALRM → Unix-only (see tests/conftest.py::_enforce_test_timeout) - Live Winsock / Windows-specific regression tests → @pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform != "win32", reason="Windows-specific regression")

Monkeypatching sys.platform is not enough when the code under test also calls platform.system() / platform.release() / platform.mac_ver(). Those functions re-read the real OS independently, so a test that sets sys.platform = "linux" on a Windows runner will still see platform.system() == "Windows" and route through the Windows branch. Patch all three together:

monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "platform", "linux")
monkeypatch.setattr(platform, "system", lambda: "Linux")
monkeypatch.setattr(platform, "release", lambda: "6.8.0-generic")

See tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py::TestEnvironmentHints for a worked example.

System prompt's execution-environment block

Factual host/backend guidance (OS, $HOME, cwd, terminal backend, shell) is emitted by agent/prompt_builder.py::build_environment_hints(). The key invariant for prompt authors: with a remote terminal backend (docker, singularity, modal, daytona, ssh, managed_modal), host info is suppressed and every file tool runs inside the backend container — the prompt must never describe the host the agent can't touch.

Commit Conventions

type: concise subject line

Optional body.

Types: fix:, feat:, refactor:, docs:, chore:

Key Rules

  • Never break prompt caching — don't change context, tools, or system prompt mid-conversation
  • Message role alternation — never two assistant or two user messages in a row
  • Use get_hermes_home() from hermes_constants for all paths (profile-safe)
  • Config values go in config.yaml, secrets go in .env
  • New tools need a check_fn so they only appear when requirements are met

People Roster Sync

Goal: Keep the store team list true, clean, and visible — and publish CURRENT by role so hire math and scheduling can trust Brain.

What this skill does

  1. Show the roster (Brain v_roster) — role counts first, names second
  2. Publish CURRENT[role] — active floor people by canonical role + machine handoff JSON for people-min-safe-gap
  3. Flag data issues — dupes, bad names, missing/unknown positions, stuck hired
  4. Health alerts — unknown_role high · Brain ≪ 7shifts · live store missing 7shifts map · missed daily run
  5. Compare Brain vs 7shifts when asked or Brain looks thin
  6. Import missing actives 7shifts → Brain (human yes, or daily cron) — primary role lock (one bucket/person/store)
  7. Drift report (read-only) — Brain active missing from 7shifts; weekly short list → Louis/Yumi OK only

Does not: decide how many to hire · post jobs · build 7shifts board · auto-deactivate anyone

Truth model (locked)

Layer Role
7shifts active @ location Source of truth for who can work the floor
Brain v_roster / workforce Company read model GMs/Louis use
Write path 7shifts → Brain only for backfill (source=7shifts-sync)
Deactivate / terminate Never without Louis or Yumi explicit OK

Old staff missing email/training in Brain is not a deactivate reason.
If Brain collapses to teens/managers-only → Step 7 compare + import.

Legacy: stores.headcount_budget (~20) is stale. Do not use it for gap decisions or “over budget.” Hide it unless Louis asks for that field.

Restaurant context

  • server = waiter/waitress, not a computer
  • FOH = server, host, bartender, busser
  • BOH = cook, prep, dishwasher, sushi chef
  • Boss = GM, AGM, Floor Manager (Lead ≠ boss)
  • All reads: Supabase (WISE BRAIN), never Google Sheets as truth

Auto-detect store

CURRENT[role] contract (for min-safe-gap)

CURRENT[role] = count of people who count toward hire math for that role at one store.

Include

Exclude

  • terminated · recruiting · coaching (unless Louis says otherwise)

  • Double-count: if same person is active on 2 stores, count toward primary store only for company totals; on a single-store roster, count if listed active there and note multi-store

Multi-store person rules

  1. Same human on 2 stores → note in roster reply (“also on 0000X”)
  2. Company-wide unique headcount → dedupe by normalized name + email/phone

  4. Do not merge stores when user asked one store

  2. stores RLS on anon — don’t depend on it; never use headcount_budget for gaps

  4. Don’t auto-fix data in cron; human “clean it up” only
  5. Hired >14 days = stuck onboarding nudge, not auto-active
  6. URL-encode names with spaces in filters
  7. 7shifts pagination = cursor, not offset
  8. Filter location_id= only — not location_ids
  9. 7shifts active ≠ worked this week
  10. Big missing lists: table + count + few examples; full dump only if asked

  15. Shift Lead ≠ Floor/GM/AGM for boss CURRENT
  16. Never deactivate without Louis/Yumi

⚠️ CRITICAL — 7shifts API active=true filter is BROKEN (discovered 2026-07-25)

Root cause of the ghost crisis (164 ghosts terminated Jul 25):

The 7shifts v2 API GET /v2/company/{cid}/users?active=true&location_id={loc} does NOT filter by active status. It returns ALL users (active AND inactive). This was verified by comparing API response counts vs. actually checking each user's active field:

Store API "active=true" returned Truly active: true in payload Ghosts hiding
00001 127 40 87
00002 132 52 80
00003 99 45 54

What happened: The sync script trusted active=true and imported/matched ALL returned users. People who quit months ago stayed "active" in Brain because the script kept seeing them as "active" from 7shifts. Brain grew to 288 "active" while real 7shifts actives were only 137.

Fix applied (Jul 25): fetch_location_users() now double-filters: [u for u in users if u.get("active") is True] after the API call. Do NOT remove this line.

Prevention rules (first principles): 1. Never trust API query filters alone — always verify by checking the actual field value in the response payload 2. Sync = add-only — the script imports missing 7shifts actives into Brain, but does NOT auto-terminate Brain rows (drift is report-only) 3. Termination = human gate — Louis/Yumi must say "terminate" or "no longer with us" before any Brain status changes to terminated 4. Drift report = the safety net — --report-drift compares Brain active vs 7shifts truly active; if drift > 0, flag for review 5. Nightly cron keeps it clean — people_roster_sync_7shifts_cron.py runs daily 5am with the fix; new ghosts can't accumulate

POS Fraud Watch (Hermes-native)

WHY: Peek at last night’s sales. Say nothing if fine. One short note if something smells off. Remember repeat people.

First principles (10-year-old)

  1. Free food / money left wrong → look
  2. Clean night → silent
  3. Same person keeps failing rules → louder

No 10 crons. No button circus for v1. Math in script. Judgment only when Louis asks deep-dive.

Architecture loop

pos-chowbus-nightly saves sales → Brain chowbus_raw
pos-fraud-nightly reads order-level POS → writes fraud_history
  → stdout empty if GREEN → Slack silent
  → stdout alert if 🟡/🔴 → Slack #02-exec
Human replies approved/not fraud → pos_fraud_verdict.py → fraud_verdicts

When to use

  • Cron: every night after sales pull
  • Louis / Luna: “any fraud?” / “suspicious?” / “check voids” / 30天异常 / 具体问题单
  • Verdict: “approved” / “not fraud” / “real” / “escalate”
  • Server deep-dive: load this + pos-chowbus, scan that employee’s tickets

Don’t use for: labor hours (7shifts), payroll, hiring.

Script

# Nightly watchdog (silent if clean)
python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/pos_fraud_nightly.py

# Manual
python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/pos_fraud_nightly.py --date 2026-07-11
python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/pos_fraud_nightly.py --store 00003 --report
python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/pos_fraud_nightly.py --dry-run --report

# Human verdict (required when Louis decides)
python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/pos_fraud_verdict.py \
  --date 2026-07-11 --store 00003 \
  --verdict dismissed --by louis \
  --note "birthday under 4 — coach only"

Source of truth: scripts/ in this skill → copy to ~/.hermes/scripts/.

5 checks

# Check RED YELLOW
1 Voids >2% gross or 3+ voids by one server >1% or 2+ voids
2 Refunds >1% >0.5%
3 Mystery discounts >5% unexplained >3% unexplained
4 Cash share >40% >30%
5 Gift card free (no pay) any —

Named / known discounts are not mystery: Birthday, Military, UNCW, Employee, Deposit,
ECU 10%, DoorDash / Grubhub / Uber, Healthcare night, $10 voucher,
Manager's meal / manager allowance, loyalty, food complaint, google review.
Still mystery (flag): bare Custom Discount and anything with no known keyword.
Birthday free needs 4+ guests (eatatgangnam.com) → under-4 = 🟡 policy, not auto-theft.

Owner wait rule (Louis + Luna — locked 2026-07-14)

Bug: Luna said「可以 / 全部详情」→ multi-day Chowbus pull with zero Slack text → looked ignored.

Do every Louis/Luna ticket deep-dive:

Multi-day review (30d / N days)

fraud_history may only hold recent cron nights. For “check 30 days each store”:

  1. Query Brain fraud_history date=gte.<start> — column is date not business_date.
  2. If missing cells (store×day), backfill: loop days × stores → analyze_store + upsert_history. ~0.15s sleep; 4 stores × 30d ≈ 2–3 min.
  3. Summarize: GREEN/YELLOW/RED per store · flag-type counts · RED nights · people with bday_bad / multi-void.
  4. First reply: worst store first + next-step hooks (expand / tickets / birthday ask).
  5. After PROMO list change: copy skill scripts/pos_fraud_nightly.py → ~/.hermes/scripts/.

Recipe: references/multi-day-and-tickets.md.

Ticket extract (“具体问题单”)

On flagged days for one store, fetch_sales_details and list #order, not only night %.

Bucket Rule Present
Refunds Paid + refund cents > 0 #order · who · $refund
Voids status Voided #order · who (gross often $0)
Birthday under-4 birthday promo + guests < 4 #order · who · guests · $off
Real mystery name has Custom or fails PROMO_OK #order · who · name · $
Not theft (first reply) DoorDash/Grubhub/ECU/Healthcare/voucher/manager meal One line: platform/ECU — not theft

Priority: big refunds → whole-check Custom → birthday under-4 repeats → void piles.

Refund field: (o.get("refund") or {}).get("amount_in_cents") on Paid rows (not payment.detail alone).

Refund row shapes (Masa Jul 2026):

Shape POS signals Priority
Reopen / real ticket refund gross > 0, line_items present, reopen_amount_in_cents ≈ refund High — ask why whole bill refunded
Pure refund record gross $0, line_items null, card amount negative, often has refund_id Medium — original meal may be another day/ticket
Tip full refund tip cents ≈ −refund (or tip == −bill) High — flag tip clawback / mis-refund
Custom whole-check free Custom Discount amt ≈ gross, pay $0 (not a refund) High — reason required

Theft judgment (one employee, one flag)

Use first principles + 7-day pattern. Never answer “maybe” without both.

  1. Ticket fit — guests_total vs line items (e.g. 2 adult + 1 kid = 3 real seats)
  2. Money path — card vs cash, tip size, void/refund after pay (cash + void after pay = theft-shaped)
  3. Discount shape — one free adult birthday vs whole table free / mystery %
  4. 7-day same employee — fetch_sales_details for that store; filter employee; list birthday/discount rows with guests + order #
Pattern Say
1 under-4 birthday in 7d, family-shaped ticket, card + tip, no void Policy coach, not theft

Chowbus POS (Open API)

Hermes talks to Chowbus directly via Open API OAuth keys. Nightly cron writes daily snapshots to Supabase chowbus_raw. Other skills/crons read Brain — they do not re-implement OAuth.

Profile note: Full client/scripts historically live under default profile ~/.hermes/scripts/chowbus_*.py and shared skill bank. This wise_ops copy is the capability + reply source of truth after Anson HQ thread 2026-07-16 (loyalty/marketing + how data flows). Keep in sync when puller changes.

What the Open API can pull

Endpoint Path Use
Sales details GET /api/v1/sales/details Full order-level sales (primary)
Orders GET /api/v1/orders Richer times; metadata.third_party_member_id
Menus GET /api/v1/menus Menu tree (page + page_size required)
Stores GET /api/v1/stores One restaurant for header ID

Cannot pull: labor / clock / payroll hours / staff last-login / employee directory / loyalty members, points, guest CRM. Labor → 7shifts.

How data gets here (HQ short answer)

When Anson/Louis asks “how are you getting info from Chowbus?” — simple bullets, no secrets:

  1. Chowbus Open API (official read path)
  2. OAuth group keys → temporary token
  3. Per-call restaurant ID header
  4. Pull sales/details + orders for mapped stores
  5. Nightly → Brain chowbus_raw; on demand → live client
  6. Not store-screen login for normal sales; not 00005 until keys exist

Do not paste client_secret, full .env, or dual-bot architecture into Slack.

Marketing & loyalty (can / can’t)

Trigger: loyalty program, marketing list, member export, points, separate loyalty platform, “purchases for loyalty.”

HQ reply style (Anson 2026-07-16): bulletin points only — Can / Can’t. Easy and simple. No architecture lecture unless asked.

✅ Can - Pull tickets/sales (items, spend, discounts, voids, refunds, store, time) - Power spend-based external loyalty if guest ID comes from elsewhere - Summarize sales by store/day for promo measurement - See named discounts on tickets - Nightly sales archive for 00001–00004

❌ Can’t - Export Chowbus loyalty members (name/phone/email) - Pull points balances or earn/redeem history - See guest identity on most tickets (no phone/email on Open API) - Run/edit Chowbus loyalty or send SMS/email/push via this API - Cover 00005 (unmapped) - Assume native loyalty CRM already flows into Brain

Orders metadata.third_party_member_id = external hook; empty full day 00001–00004.
Sales deferred_sales.loyalty_amount_in_cents + annual_membership_fee_amount_in_cents = money slots; often $0.

Wiserise Playbook Lookup

Searches the Supabase sops table for an existing SOP, form, or policy. Returns the answer the person needs — content + PDF link — in clean Slack markdown.

Architecture (3 Pillars + 4 Utilities)

Load wiserise-architecture for the full framework. Key rules for Playbook Lookup:

Pillar/Utility Lookup Role Rule
🧠 Brain (Supabase) Source of truth — sops table has all 321 docs One query. Never read from Obsidian/Drive/Sheets as source.
⚡ Hermes Sole worker — queries Brain, formats answer, sends to Slack No sub-agents. Query silently via terminal/python if needed.
💬 Slack Where the person asked — reply here with the answer Clean markdown only. No terminal output.
📊 Sheets Not used —
📓 Obsidian Not used as source Brain has the content. Obsidian is a push destination, not a read source.
📁 Drive PDF link comes from Brain's file_url field The link may point to org-files storage bucket. Brain holds the reference.
🔬 NotebookLM Not used —

The loop for lookup:

Person asks "what's the SOP for X?" (💬 Slack)
→ Hermes extracts the search term
→ Hermes queries Brain: SELECT from sops WHERE title/synonyms/content matches (🧠 Brain)
→ If money/rate/% and file_url set → download PDF + extract text; prefer PDF numbers
→ Hermes formats the result (⚡ Hermes)
→ Hermes posts the answer + PDF link to Slack (💬 Slack)
→ Done. No human gate needed — this is a read-only query (except money conflicts → @Louis).

Default path: Brain has content, synonyms, and PDF link — one query. Exception (Exec only): user says "not this version" on a handbook/training book → resolve designed PDF on Drive and update Brain (see Version resolution + references/version-resolution.md). Do not use Drive as a silent second truth for store-channel manager lookups.

PDF vs content — money / rates / % (Kai / store 00001 2026-07-27)

sops.content can diverge from the designed PDF at file_url. Brain text was edited without regenerating the PDF (or the reverse).

HARD for pay, tip-out %, tax, labor targets, band rates, or any number a GM will run tonight:

  1. If file_url exists → sign + download + extract PDF text (pypdf / pymupdf) before stating the rate in Slack.
  2. Quote / summarize from the PDF when it conflicts with content.
  3. If related live docs disagree with each other (e.g. PAY-002 PDF vs GNG-068 vs REF-002 vs roadmap) → do not pick a winner. Show the conflict, say which source says what, @Louis for money/policy lock. Never invent “true” %.
  4. If the manager says “the PDF shows X” after you cited Brain text → re-extract the PDF, own the mistake, correct the thread. Do not argue from content alone.
  5. Lookup stays read-only on OPS — flag HQ to realign Brain text + PDFs; do not PATCH rates unless Louis/Exec write path.

Details + known tip-out split: references/pdf-content-mismatch.md.

Reference: See wiserise-architecture/references/sops-table-and-shared-infra.md for the full sops table schema, numbering rules, and shared Python scripts.

Access control (managers · brand · channel) — HARD RULE

Managers may read SOPs, rules, and policies for their own brand + company, scoped by the store channel they ask from. They do not get other brands. They do not create/edit SOPs (Exec only).

Who is a manager?

Signal How
GM map stores.gm_slack_id = sender Slack user id
Roster workforce_employees.position in manager set for that person (when identity is known): General Manager, Assistant GM, AGM, Floor Manager, Kitchen Manager, Server Lead, Kitchen Lead, Kitchen Lead / Expo, GM
Store channel default Anyone asking inside a verified store channel may receive staff + manager audience docs for that channel’s brand + company (managers work there; channel is the main lock today)

SAFE OPEN — never silent-drop (Louis locked 2026-07-21)

Anyone who @WISE OPS in a store channel for existing SOP / form / policy / role sheet lookup → answer immediately.
No manager allowlist. No pairing. No “wait for Louis.” No empty ignore.
Brand scope still applies (company + this store only).
Hire / fire / money / create SOP still gated (identity + manager list).

Unknown / non-store channels: do not invent a store. Exec (Louis) / HQ DMs may see all brands. Cross-store “show me Masa SOP” from a Gangnam channel → hard refuse.

Brand scope (always apply when store is known)

  1. Resolve store from gateway context:
  2. Prefer stores.slack_channel_id = eq.{channel_id}
  3. Else 5-digit store number from channel name → stores.number
  4. Map stores.brand → brand_key:
  5. Gangnam* → gangnam
  6. Masa* → masa
  7. Low Country / LCB → lcb
  8. Allowed brand_keys: company + that store’s brand only.
  9. PostgREST filter (required on every search pass once store is known):
&or=(brand_key.eq.company,brand_key.eq.{store_brand})
  1. After results return, drop any row whose brand_key is not in {company, store_brand} before replying.
  2. Audience: managers and store-channel asks may see audience=staff and audience=manager. Do not hide manager SOPs from store channels.
  3. Create / edit / publish SOP or policy → only Exec (wiserise-sop / Louis). Lookup never writes.

Store → brand map (verify live stores if unsure)

Store # brand_key Channel id (verify live)
00001 gangnam C0ARAG1LKED
00002 masa C0ARAG19LRX
00003 gangnam C0ARRT1HSJU
00004 gangnam C0BCY16FKH8
00005 lcb (may be null — reconcile before posting)

Example: Levi (GM, 00003) in #store-00003-gangnam-wilmington asks “closing SOP” → return live docs with brand_key in (company, gangnam) only. Masa-only docs never appear.

When to Use

  • "What's the SOP for closing?"
  • "Send me the tip-out sheet"
  • "How do we handle a guest complaint?"
  • "Give me the interview form"
  • "What's our policy on breaks?"
  • "Where's the cash drawer count sheet?"
  • "Show me SHIFT-005"
  • "What's the pay rate for Server?"
  • "What are our pay bands?"
  • "How much does a Host make?"
  • "Company escalation policy" → TEAM-015

When NOT to Use (creation / approve / publish)

On WISE OPS, GM / manager / store / HQ OPS asks:

  • "Make an SOP for X" / "Write an SOP" / "Create a form" / "Approve this SOP" / "Publish SOP"
  • Do NOT load wiserise-sop or wiserise-form
  • Do NOT draft, reserve numbers, approve, or publish
  • HARD REFUSE with the locked professional reply (SOUL.md + store-channel-policy)
  • Then offer lookup of an existing live doc if they still need a procedure

Create / approve / publish company SOPs and forms = Louis / WISE BRAIN only (Louis locked 2026-07-13).

Key distinction: If the user wants to find an existing doc → this skill. If they want to create/approve/publish a new doc on OPS → refuse + redirect to Louis.

Supabase Access

URL: from ~/.hermes/.env → SUPABASE_URL
KEY: from ~/.hermes/.env → SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (MUST use service role — anon key = 0 rows due to RLS)

Query via REST API:

GET {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/sops?select=sop_no,title,doc_type,status,content,file_url,brand_key,audience,synonyms&...

Prefer terminal + python if execute_code is blocked in the session gateway.

Search Strategy (3 passes, stop at first hit)

Pass 0 — Resolve brand scope BEFORE search

If store channel / GM store is known → set SCOPE_BRANDS = {company, store_brand} and append the or=(brand_key.eq.company,brand_key.eq.{store_brand}) filter to every pass below. If Exec/DM with no store → no brand filter (all brands). Never invent brand.

Pass 1 — Exact number match (fastest)

If the user mentioned a number like "TEAM-004" or "SHIFT-F-002":

GET /rest/v1/sops?sop_no=eq.{NUMBER}&select=sop_no,title,doc_type,status,content,file_url,brand_key,audience

→ Apply brand scope filter when store known. If the doc is another brand → refuse:

🔒 That doc is for *{other brand}*. This channel is *{store brand}* only.
Company-wide + your brand SOPs are OK — ask for those by title.
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

Pass 2 — Title keyword search (most natural)

The user says "tip-out sheet" → search title with ilike (plus brand scope when known):

GET /rest/v1/sops?title=ilike.*{SEARCH_TERM}*&status=eq.live&or=(brand_key.eq.company,brand_key.eq.{store_brand})&select=sop_no,title,doc_type,content,file_url,brand_key,audience&order=title&limit=5
  • ilike.*{TERM}* does a case-insensitive substring match on title
  • URL-encode spaces as %20 (e.g. tip-out%20sheet)
  • Omit the or=(...) brand filter only for Exec/all-brand context

If the title search returns nothing, try synonyms (PostgREST array contains):

GET /rest/v1/sops?synonyms=cs.{{{SEARCH_TERM}}}&status=eq.live&or=(brand_key.eq.company,brand_key.eq.{store_brand})&select=sop_no,title,doc_type,content,file_url,brand_key,audience
  • cs.{value} checks if the synonyms text array contains the exact string
  • Note: this is exact match on one array element, not substring

Pass 3 — Title + content keyword search

If no synonym hit, search by title keywords (brand-scoped when store known):

GET /rest/v1/sops?title=ilike.*{KEYWORD}*&status=eq.live&or=(brand_key.eq.company,brand_key.eq.{store_brand})&select=sop_no,title,doc_type,content,file_url,brand_key,audience&order=title&limit=5

If still nothing, try content search:

GET /rest/v1/sops?content=ilike.*{KEYWORD}*&status=eq.live&or=(brand_key.eq.company,brand_key.eq.{store_brand})&select=sop_no,title,doc_type,content,file_url,brand_key,audience&limit=5

Pass 4 — Brand filter is not optional

When store context is known, brand filter is required on every query (not a “nice to have”). Map: - store-00003-gangnam-wilmington / Gangnam → gangnam - s00002-masa-greenville / Masa → masa - store-00005-lowcountryboil-… / Low Country* → lcb

Always include company with the store brand. Never return another brand’s rows.

Reply Format (Slack)

Single match found

📋 *{Title}*
DOC NO: {sop_no}
Type: SOP / FORM
Brand: {brand_key}

{content (first 500 chars, then "..." if longer)}

{If file_url exists:} 📎 PDF attached (no long link)
MEDIA:/abs/path.pdf
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

Multiple matches found

📋 *Found {N} docs for "{search_term}"*

1. {sop_no} — {title} ({doc_type})
2. {sop_no} — {title} ({doc_type})
3. {sop_no} — {title} ({doc_type})

👉 Reply with the number to see it
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

No match found

🔍 No SOP or form found for "{search_term}".

Try:
• Different words (e.g. "cash count" instead of "drawer")
• The doc number if you know it (e.g. "TEAM-004")
• If you need a *new* company SOP/form → message **Louis** (HQ). I cannot create or approve SOPs here.
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

Create / approve / publish request (GM / manager / store)

Never invent a draft. Never say approved. Reply:

📋 *SOP / form creation — HQ only*
I can find live SOPs and forms for this store.
I cannot create, approve, or publish new company SOPs or forms.

• Need an existing procedure? Tell me the topic (e.g. “closing SOP”).
• Need a new SOP or form? Please message **Louis** — HQ owns company docs.

I can still help with hiring, roster, onboarding, and daily store questions.
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

Doc conflict (money / rates) — show sources, escalate

📋 *Policy conflict — need HQ lock*
• {doc A PDF}: {rate}
• {doc B text/PDF}: {rate}
I can’t pick the floor rate. @Louis — which is live?
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

Version resolution (handbooks / training books)

Some titles had many off-Brain PDFs (UNIFIED7, COMPLETE, REBUILT, CLEAN…) while Brain only held a knowledge text dump from an old docx. Louis will say "not this version" if you serve the wrong one.

  1. Prefer status=live + file_url set over knowledge with no PDF.
  2. If only a knowledge hit: say it is legacy, attach only if file_url exists — do not rebuild a new PDF from Brain text as if it were the designed book.
  3. On "not this version" (Exec/DM only): check Drive for the designed file, then (Exec write) replace Brain content + PDF. Canonical GM Training Book:
  4. REF-008 = UNIFIED7 numbered (43-page designed PDF)
  5. Drive: WISERISE/03 – PEOPLE/gm-training-book-UNIFIED7-numbered.pdf
  6. Old COMPLETE docx dump retired (v2 live). Details: references/version-resolution.md
  7. Lookup stays read-only for managers. Version replace = Exec + wiserise-sop publish path.

Rules

  1. Always search live docs first (status=eq.live). Only show knowledge docs if no live match exists. Flag knowledge as legacy in the reply.
  2. Never show terminal output, curl, Python, or SQL in Slack. Query silently. The human only sees the result.
  3. Brand + channel lock for managers/store channels. Allowed = company + that store’s brand only. Hard refuse other brands.
  4. Company docs apply to all brands. Always include brand_key=eq.company with the store brand.
  5. Managers may see staff + manager audience for their brand scope. Do not strip audience=manager in store channels.
  6. Content is plain text. The content field is the readable answer — except when money/rate/% requires PDF verify (see PDF vs content).
  7. file_url may be a signed URL or a bare path. If it starts with http, use it (may already be signed). If it starts with playbooks/, do not assume /storage/v1/object/public/org-files/... works — often HTTP 400. Prefer signed download:
  8. POST {SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1/object/sign/org-files/{file_url} with service role body {"expiresIn": 604800}
  9. GET {SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1 + returned signedURL (usually /object/sign/org-files/...?token=...)
  10. Limit content to 500 chars in Slack. Full text on request or via PDF. Short band tables may exceed slightly if the answer is the table + PDF attached. 8b. "链接看不清楚" / "发到这里" / "send PDF here" / "only PDF" / "no link" → download signed PDF and attach with MEDIA:/absolute/path.pdf. Prefer file attach only — do not paste full long Supabase signed token URLs (Louis 2026-07-16: links too long on phone). PDF is not missing from Brain — fix files:write (rule 14). Details: references/slack-pdf-attach.md. 8d. Weekly 叫货 / order list (existing — do not reinvent): SHIFT-F-004 Gangnam Weekly Supplies Restock (main), SHIFT-F-007 Weekly Inventory, SHIFT-F-005 Inventory Supply Request, CASH-F-002 PO, SHIFT-F-001 beverage.

  17. Pay Band Policy is REF-002. Pay rate / pay band lookups → sop_no=eq.REF-002 or title=ilike.*pay%20band*. Company-level. Tip-out % is not decided by REF-002 alone — primary tip docs are PAY-002 + form PAY-F-004; always PDF-verify.

  21. Slack bot scopes for PDF attach (WISE OPS / store bots). Native attach uses files_upload_v2 → needs files:write. files:read alone is not enough. After adding scope: reinstall the Slack app. Check: auth.test response header x-oauth-scopes must include files:write. Gateway log on failure: files.getUploadURLExternal → missing_scope needed files:write.

Common Pitfalls

  1. Using anon key instead of service role. Anon key returns 0 rows on RLS-protected tables. Always use SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.
  2. Showing the whole content. Some SOPs are 2000+ chars. Truncate to 500 and offer the PDF.
  3. Forgetting company-level docs. A store channel user asking "what's the tip-out policy?" should find company PAY/REF docs even if brand is gangnam.
  4. Leaking another brand’s SOP into a store channel. Brand filter is required, not optional.
  5. Searching only live docs when knowledge docs might help. If no live match, try knowledge status as a fallback — but tell the user it's a legacy doc.
  6. URL-encoding spaces in search terms. Use %20 or + for spaces in PostgREST ilike filters. Unencoded spaces cause InvalidURL.
  7. Letting a GM edit/publish from lookup. Lookup is read-only. Create/edit/approve/publish → Louis only. Never offer “I can create one” on OPS.
  8. PDF attach fails while text succeeds. Classic: bot has files:read but missing files:write. User-visible: ⚠️ Couldn't deliver the file attachment (TEAM-014_....pdf). Do not say the PDF is missing from Brain. See references/slack-pdf-attach.md.
  9. Pasting full signed token URLs. Phone Slack shows a wall of junk (Louis 2026-07-16). Attach PDF; short text only.
  10. Bare public Storage URL returns 400. file_url like playbooks/TEAM-014_....pdf is not public. Always sign first (rule 7).
  11. Serving a knowledge text-dump as “the book”. If Louis says "not this version", stop re-serving Brain text; resolve designed PDF (see Version resolution + references/version-resolution.md).
  12. pypdf → Postgres NUL crash. Extracted PDF text often includes \x00. Strip nulls/control chars before PATCH sops.content.
  13. Trusting content over the PDF for tip-out / pay % (Kai 2026-07-27). OPS told AGM tip-out was 1% (0.5+0.5) from Brain text; PAY-002 / PAY-F-004 PDFs said 2% (1%+1%). Manager was right. Always extract PDF for money numbers; on conflict list sources and @Louis.
  14. Cross-doc tip-out drift. PAY-002 PDF 2%, Brain PAY-002 text 1%, GNG-068 0.5+0.5, REF-002 PDF 2%, GM roadmap 0.5+0.5. HQ lock — not a lookup pick.

Done Checklist

  • [ ] Searched Brain (sops table) — not Sheets, Obsidian, or Drive
  • [ ] Used SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (not anon key)
  • [ ] Live docs searched first; knowledge only as fallback
  • [ ] Brand scope resolved from channel/store when known
  • [ ] Results limited to company + store brand (no cross-brand leak)
  • [ ] Manager + staff audience allowed for managers / store channels
  • [ ] Company-level docs included in search results
  • [ ] Money/rates/%: PDF text verified when file_url exists; conflicts escalated not invented
  • [ ] Content truncated to 500 chars in Slack reply (full short tables OK + PDF)
  • [ ] PDF: MEDIA attach when file_url exists; no long signed token URLs in body
  • [ ] No terminal output, curl, Python, or SQL shown in Slack
  • [ ] Reply follows slack-message-structure format with emoji headers and divider

First principles (locked — Louis 2026-07-12)

One test:

If I ignore this for one week, does it get more expensive or more dangerous?
Yes → keep. No → drop.

4 rules (10-year-old):

  1. Email is not a to-do list — default is trash; a message must earn “important.”
  2. Important = it will hurt if ignored — hurt = lose money, get sued, card stolen, wrong bank payee, store can’t open, hard deadline.
  3. Judge by who + what — lawyer/landlord/bank + money/court/lease/payee change words. Not unread dots. Not Gmail “Important” label alone.
  4. Robot sorts; Louis presses the button — never send money; never invent status. Replies: only via skill wiserise-inbox-auto-reply (receipt auto / full draft needs explicit send).

What counts as fire (same family):

Fire Keep Drop (same sender can still be trash)
Bank risk card fraud, wire/ACH recipient changed, payment returned, unknown login (if not you) OTP, Zelle receipts, monthly statement ready, deals ads
Lawsuit judgment / settlement / pleadings / both cases lawyer firm newsletter
Landlord balance due, rent bank changed, lease entity name, TI, rent offset mall promo flyer
Invoice/job invoice needs proof before pay building material promo

Email topic search (Louis asks "search email about X")

When Louis asks to search email about a specific topic (e.g. "search my email about ABL"), use a systematic synonym ladder — don't try one query and give up.

Search ladder

  1. Exact term Louis used: subject:ABL then bare ABL (body too)
  2. Full forms / English equivalents: alcohol, liquor, beer, wine, beverage, alcoholic, on-premise, off-premise, malt, spirituous, fortified
  3. Agency / regulator names: ABC (NC ABC Board), nc.gov, beverage control, ABCC
  4. Related doc types: subject:license, subject:permit, subject:renewal, subject:application, subject:registration
  5. All folders: prefix in:anywhere to include Sent, Trash, Archive (default Gmail search = INBOX only)
  6. Cross-language: if Louis wrote in Chinese, also search the Chinese term
  7. Person name returns empty: check session_search for a name→email mapping (e.g. Kenny = D Contractors); Gmail matches email addresses, not body nicknames

When to stop

  • After 4–5 searches covering the above angles with zero hits → report "not found" and ask for context (which store, who's the contact, when)
  • Don't invent results — say what you searched and what didn't match
  • Mention the closest near-miss emails if any (e.g. insurance audit mentioning "alcohol sales" ≠ liquor license email)

Technique notes

  • gmail search default scope = INBOX only; use in:anywhere to include Sent/Trash/All Mail
  • subject:X matches subject only; bare X matches body + subject
  • Body search returns false negatives for HTML-only emails (body comes back empty); use snippet + subject
  • Batch parallel searches with different keyword angles to save round-trips
  • gmail get <id> often returns empty body for HTML/attachment-only emails; use the snippet from search results instead

See references/email-search-techniques.md for full keyword matrix and worked examples.

Pitfalls

  1. Treating 🔴 REVIEW label as truth — auto-labeler marks junk too; re-rank by counterparty
  2. Dumping every unread 7shifts logbook as “sticky”
  3. Claiming full Gmail write powers when scopes partial
  4. Guessing wife/personal life from guarantor names on leases — never
  5. Sourcing .env via bash (source) — unquoted values break; load KEY=VAL in Python
  6. Gmail search by nickname returns empty — Gmail search matches email address and subject words, not body nicknames. If Louis says "search Kenny" and from:kenny returns nothing, check session_search for prior sessions where the mapping was discovered (Kenny = D Contractors dcontractorsc@gmail.com). Then search by the real email. Keep a name→email mapping in references/sticky-threads.md.
  7. Giving up after one search — a single empty result does not mean "no emails exist." Run the full synonym ladder (see Email topic search above) before reporting nothing found. ABL / liquor license / ABC permit are the same topic under different names.

GM Roadmap Builder

Fail-stop rules (Louis 2026-07-25)

  1. POS covers = all 0 → STOP. If fetch_phase1_shift_averages returns all zeros for AM or PM, do NOT build the roadmap. Tell Louis: "POS data missing for store XXXXX. Cannot build gap. Check Chowbus API." Do not build with garbage gap data.
  2. Staff names = empty → STOP. If Brain workforce_employees returns 0 active staff for the store, do NOT build. Tell Louis: "No active staff found in Brain for store XXXXX."
  3. GM name = missing → WARN. If no GM found, build but show "GM: TBD" and flag in the message to Louis.
  4. Post-build verification → STOP. After building HTML, verify: sections 8/8, divs balanced (open = close), 19 policy cards, no placeholders left. If ANY check fails → STOP, do NOT send to Louis, report the error.
  5. Roster-dashboard staleness → WARN. If ~/.hermes/artifacts/people/roster-dashboard.json was last modified >36h ago, warn Louis: "Roster data stale — last sync was Xh ago. Rebuild may use old names." Build still proceeds, but flag the staleness in the delivery message.

Clean template (Louis 2026-07-25)

Do NOT build store 00002 by find-replace on store 00001's finished HTML. Build from a clean base template that has placeholder values. This prevents one missed replace from showing the wrong GM name in a tab.

Clean template approach: 1. Read the Fayetteville roadmap as the BASE TEMPLATE 2. Strip all store-specific data (names, covers, counts) → replace with placeholders 3. Insert the target store's live data into the clean template 4. Verify every placeholder was replaced — if any remain, STOP and report

Owner Lock (Louis 2026-07-24)

GMs CANNOT make changes to the roadmap artifact. Any change request from a GM escalates to Louis for approval. No auto-edit by managers. The artifact is read-only for GMs.

Delivery approval (Louis 2026-07-24, updated 2026-07-25)

NEVER deliver to store Slack channel without Louis reviewing first. Build → deploy to GitHub Pages → send URL to Louis → he approves → pin URL in store channel. Do not auto-pin.

New delivery model: Pin the GitHub Pages URL once. The URL is permanent. The cron auto-deploys fresh HTML behind the same URL daily. No re-uploading files. No stale artifacts.

env_load pitfall (fixed 2026-07-24)

The build script env_load() MUST use os.environ[k] = v (overwrite), NOT setdefault. Shell env can have a stale SUPABASE_URL (wrong project) that setdefault won't override — this caused empty roster + empty policy fetch. Also: fetch_policies() must use f.brain_get() (which reads env correctly), not raw urllib with os.environ.get().

p2 = f.phase2_shift_mins(p1['am_avg'], p1['pm_avg'])
paper = f.paper_grids_for_store(s, {'phase1': p1, 'phase2': p2})
grid = f.grid_for_store(s, paper)
assign = f.assign_biweekly(grid, pack['buckets'])
gaps = f.gap_rows('XXXXX', paper, pack['buckets'], pack['people'])

Build approach

  1. Build all 8 sections programmatically via build_gm_roadmap.py (static sections built in-code, dynamic sections fetch live data)
  2. Fetch live data: roster names, POS covers, gap math, policies, schedule draft
  3. Insert store-specific data into the HTML (store name, GM name, staff, covers, gaps, schedule)
  4. Rebuild policy section (fresh from Brain, 19 cards)
  5. Verify: sections 8/8, divs balanced, 19 cards, no duplicates
  6. Save HTML to ~/.hermes/artifacts/gm-roadmaps/ + copy to Desktop
  7. Deploy to GitHub Pages: python3 scripts/deploy_to_github_pages.py
  8. Notify Louis with GitHub Pages URLs (permanent links for Slack pinning)

GitHub Pages deployment

The deploy_to_github_pages.py script: 1. Clones/pulls the wiserise-gm-roadmaps GitHub repo 2. Copies fresh HTML files from ~/.hermes/artifacts/gm-roadmaps/ to the repo's roadmaps/ directory 3. Commits + pushes to main branch 4. GitHub Pages auto-serves at the permanent URL within ~30 seconds 5. If no files changed, skips commit (no noise)

Vercel project: wiserise-os/wiserise-gm-roadmaps URL base: https://wiserise-gm-roadmaps.vercel.app/

# 1. Pin the GitHub Pages URL in the store Slack channel (Louis does manually, bot cannot pin)
# 2. Post message: "🗺️ GM Roadmap — your store operating system\n👉 Bookmark this link (updates automatically): {URL}\n💻 Open on a computer — phone won't show tabs"
# 3. Post thread reply with "What's inside" (8 bullets)
# 4. URL never changes — cron auto-deploys fresh HTML behind the same link

Key change (2026-07-25): Slack file uploads are FROZEN — they don't update. GitHub Pages URLs are LIVE — cron pushes fresh HTML daily. Pin the URL once, GM always sees latest data.

Crons feeding the artifact

Cron When Type What
People-Roster-Sync daily Daily 5am Script (free, no LLM) Roster sync from 7shifts → Brain
People-Data-Health weekly Mon 5am LLM Clean bad/duplicate data in Brain
GM Roadmap Daily Refresh Daily 6am (after roster sync) LLM Rebuilds roadmaps ONLY when data changed since last build → sends to Louis for review (NOT auto-deliver to stores)

Daily rebuild is a separate skill call, not a combined cron. It calls: - people-roster-sync → Staff tab - people-min-safe-gap → Gap tab - people-scheduling → Schedule tab

Change-detection (why daily, not weekly)

Old approach: Thursday 8am rebuild → artifact 3 days stale by Monday. Covers and staff change daily.

New approach: Daily 6am (right after roster sync at 5am), but ONLY rebuild if something changed: 1. Compare today's roster counts + POS covers vs last build's snapshot (saved in ~/.hermes/artifacts/roadmaps/{storeNumber}_last_build.json) 2. If staff count, any name, or AM/PM covers differ by >5% → rebuild that store 3. If nothing changed → skip (saves LLM tokens, Louis doesn't get spammed)

This means: data changes → artifact rebuilt same morning. Data stable → no rebuild, no noise.

Auto-deploy to GitHub Pages (Louis 2026-07-25)

After building, the cron runs deploy_to_github_pages.py which pushes the fresh HTML to the wiserise-gm-roadmaps GitHub repo. GitHub Pages serves it at a permanent URL.

Flow: Cron rebuilds HTML → deploy script pushes to GitHub → GitHub Pages serves fresh HTML → GM opens same pinned link → sees latest data. No re-uploading files to Slack.

When Louis says "show me," "send me," or asks to see CASH-F-002 or any purchase form/doc:

Pitfalls

  1. Routing supply to AM — wrong; finance only
  2. Long SOP when Louis asks 怎么做 — use one paste
  3. Burying buy request inside another finance thread — always new post per store buy
  4. Auto-paying — never

  9. PDF spilling to 2 pages — CASH-F-002 has 20 table rows + header + signatures. The print CSS must compress row heights to ≤18px and font to ≤9px. CSS source-order trap: the base .inv-table td { height: 34px } rules sit AFTER the @media print block in the stylesheet, so they override print overrides of equal specificity (last-wins). Fix: add a second @media print block AFTER the base rules using !important on font-size, padding, and height. Always verify with Chrome headless --print-to-pdf + fitz.open(pdf_path).page_count == 1. See references/css-print-one-page.md for the full fix pattern. (Louis 2026-08-01)
  10. Partial updates — updating file but not content, or content but not file_url. Always update all three atomically. The bot reads content for Slack replies, NOT the HTML file. (Louis 2026-08-01)
  11. Using playbooks/ prefix in file_url. Files go in bucket root. Bare filename only. (Louis 2026-08-01)
  12. Treating Finance "购物清单" as one P1 buy post — wrong; update master catalog Sheet
  13. Creating a second shopping Sheet — reuse URL in references/shopping-catalog.md
  14. Brain content/file_url drift — when updating a form, always update file_url + content + actual file together. The bot reads content for Slack replies, NOT the file. See references/brain-integrity-check.md for the diagnostic script and fix pattern. (Louis 2026-08-01)

Pathwiserise/wiserise-secrets-sync

Wiserise secrets sync

Trigger: new API key pasted, “save to 1Password”, “sync .env”, Composio/OpenAI/etc credentials.

Source of truth (locked 2026-08-01)

1Password is the SOLE source of truth. .env files are read-only projections.

  • Vault: IT
  • Master Secure Note: Wiserise OS .env (KEY=VALUE lines in notesPlain, 143 keys)
  • Local projections (auto-synced, never manually edited):
  • ~/.hermes/.env (main Hermes)
  • ~/.hermes/profiles/wise_ops/.env (WISE OPS profile)
  • ~/Documents/WISERISE OS SYSTEM/.env.local (frontend project, if dir exists)
  • SA token: OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN in Hermes env
  • Cron: Brain-Secrets-Sync-#2 every 1h, runs ~/.hermes/scripts/op_sync_cron.sh (no_agent, deliver=local)
  • Also refreshes Supabase keys from dedicated Supabase item in IT vault
  • Health-check piggybacked: after sync, tests 4 providers (openai, zai, xai, anthropic) with 1-token API calls. Sends Slack alert to #02-executive ONLY if a key is dead. Silent when all healthy.
  • No orphaned keys: .env is fully overwritten from 1Password. Keys not in 1Password are dropped — forces all keys into 1Password.
  • wise_ops/.env is a SEPARATE file (verified 2026-08-02). The sync script does NOT write to it — only ~/.hermes/.env is synced from 1Password. wise_ops has its own OPENAI_API_KEY (Luna's key, stored as WISE_OPS_OPENAI_API_KEY in 1Password master note for backup).

How to rotate a key (the correct workflow)

  1. Update the key in the vendor console (Anthropic, xAI, etc.)
  2. Open 1Password → IT vault → Wiserise OS .env secure note
  3. Replace the key value in the note
  4. Either wait ≤1h for cron, or run bash ~/.hermes/scripts/op_sync_cron.sh manually
  5. The sync script also validates the key — if dead, you get a Slack alert in #02-executive

Never edit .env directly — the cron will overwrite it from 1Password.

When user pastes a key (or “auto safe to 1Password / .env”)

bash ~/.hermes/scripts/op-save-secret.sh "KEY=value"
# Composio bundle: COMPOSIO_API_KEY, COMPOSIO_TOOL_ROUTER_SESSION, COMPOSIO_MCP_URL

Updates 1Password master note, then syncs Hermes .env.

Optional: IT API_CREDENTIAL item (e.g. Composio - API key).

Never stop at local .env only when user asks for 1Password safety — master note + local projection.

When user says “search 1Password and update all keys”

Do not only pull the master note. Dedicated items can be newer/correct while master is stale.

Env var 1Password Field Notes
OPENAI_API_KEY IT → OpenAI - API key credential Prefer item over master if both OK
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Operations → Anthropic api_key Master can be 401-stale — always validate
NVIDIA_API_KEY + NVIDIA_NIM_API_KEY IT → NVIDIA - build.nvidia.com (AI API) API Key Also set NVIDIA_BASE_URL from item
XAI_API_KEY Master Wiserise OS .env notesPlain API only. OAuth separate: hermes auth logout xai-oauth then hermes auth add xai-oauth --type oauth --timeout 180 (agent can run). Check: hermes auth status xai-oauth
OPENROUTER_API_KEY / GLM_API_KEY Master note notesPlain Validate /v1/models
UPSTAGE_API_KEY often missing — Solar via OpenRouter until present

Workflow: candidates item→master→local → HTTP validate → backup .env → rewrite → report ✓/✗. Master write-back best-effort; if blocked, local still wins.

Full recipe: references/pull-provider-keys-from-1password.md

Bootstrap if master note missing

# SA must access IT vault
op item get "Wiserise OS .env" --vault IT
# if missing: create SECURE_NOTE from current ~/.hermes/.env via op item create --template

Then fix/use scripts: - ~/.hermes/scripts/op_sync_cron.sh — full master note → ~/.hermes/.env + project .env.local (used by cron). Also tests all 4 providers after sync and alerts Slack on dead keys. Does NOT write to wise_ops/.env — that is a separate file (see "Per-profile keys" below). - ~/.hermes/scripts/op-save-secret.sh — Python upsert + template write-back (for adding a single new key). ⚠️ Writes to 1Password master note then syncs ~/.hermes/.env ONLY — does not touch wise_ops/.env.

Pitfalls

  • If master note missing, bootstrap from ~/.hermes/.env first — op-save-secret assumes IT/Wiserise OS .env exists.
  • Live confirmed: master note + Composio - API key API_CREDENTIAL in IT; keys include COMPOSIO_API_KEY, COMPOSIO_TOOL_ROUTER_SESSION, COMPOSIO_MCP_URL.
  • Pinned skill 1password-ops may lag scripts on disk — prefer live ~/.hermes/scripts/* (op-sync = full master note pull, not Supabase-only).
  • op-save-secret.sh accepts vault as 2nd arg or --vault; always Python-upsert secrets (URLs break sed).
  • Never print full keys back in chat after save.
  • Cron op_sync_cron.sh every 1h keeps local env as a projection, not the source.
  • Script name is op_sync_cron.sh (not op-sync.sh — old name still in some references).
  • wise_ops/.env is a SEPARATE file (verified 2026-08-02 via inode check). The sync cron does NOT write to it — only ~/.hermes/.env is synced from 1Password. wise_ops can carry its own OPENAI_API_KEY (or any var) that differs from the default profile. See "Per-profile keys" below.
  • No orphaned keys (changed 2026-08-01): .env is fully overwritten from 1Password. Keys not in 1Password are dropped. If you need a key, add it to 1Password — don't add it to .env directly.
  • Health-check piggybacked (changed 2026-08-01): sync script tests all 4 providers after writing .env (openai, zai, xai, anthropic). Slack alert to #02-executive only on dead keys. Silent when healthy.
  • Anthropic ghost key (2026-08-01): Anthropic API keys are static — they do NOT expire. A 401 "invalid" means the key was deleted/rotated in the console but .env/1Password still has the old key. Fix: create new key in console → update 1Password master note → run sync → verify. See hermes-provider-management → references/api-health-check.md → "Anthropic ghost key diagnosis".
  • source ~/.hermes/.env can fail silently when values contain $ or special chars. Use grep "^KEY=" file | cut -d'=' -f2- to extract keys for testing, not shell source.
  • op item get without --vault fails with "a vault query must be provided" when using a service account. Always pass --vault IT or --vault Operations.

Per-profile keys (different key per Hermes profile)

Trigger: "give WISE OPS its own key", "Luna's key for WISE OPS", "different OpenAI key per profile".

The sync cron writes ONLY to ~/.hermes/.env (default profile). ~/.hermes/profiles/wise_ops/.env is a separate file the cron never touches. This means each profile can have its own OPENAI_API_KEY (or any var) — but you must manage wise_ops/.env manually.

The pitfall (hit 2026-08-02)

op-save-secret.sh "OPENAI_API_KEY=<new>" writes the key to the 1Password master note, then syncs ~/.hermes/.env (default profile). If the new key is meant for WISE OPS, this overwrites WISE BRAIN's key with WISE OPS's key. You must restore the original key to the default profile afterward.

Correct workflow (per-profile key for wise_ops)

  1. Save the new key to 1Password under a profile-specific var name (NOT OPENAI_API_KEY — that's shared): bash export $(grep "^OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=" ~/.hermes/.env | head -1) bash ~/.hermes/scripts/op-save-secret.sh "WISE_OPS_OPENAI_API_KEY=<new-key>" This stores it in the master note as backup and syncs to ~/.hermes/.env (harmless — it's a new var, not OPENAI_API_KEY).

  2. Restore the original OPENAI_API_KEY to the default profile if step 1's sync touched it (it won't if you used a different var name, but verify): python import re, os env_default = os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/.env") with open(env_default) as f: c = f.read() # Verify OPENAI_API_KEY still ends with the original suffix

  3. Write the new key to wise_ops/.env as OPENAI_API_KEY (the var Hermes actually reads): python import re, os env_ops = os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/profiles/wise_ops/.env") NEW_KEY = "<new-key>" with open(env_ops) as f: c = f.read() c = re.sub(r'^OPENAI_API_KEY=.*$', f'OPENAI_API_KEY={NEW_KEY}', c, flags=re.MULTILINE) with open(env_ops, 'w') as f: f.write(c)

  4. Also add WISE_OPS_OPENAI_API_KEY to wise_ops/.env (mirror of 1Password backup var, for traceability).

  5. Validate both keys with a 1-token API call — confirm WISE BRAIN keeps its original, WISE OPS uses the new one: bash curl -s https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":1}'

  6. No gateway restart needed for env var changes — the next model call picks up the new key. (If a restart IS needed, use osascript → Terminal from outside the session — see wiserise-slack-gateway-operations.)

Why this works

  • The hourly sync cron (op_sync_cron.sh) only overwrites ~/.hermes/.env. wise_ops/.env is untouched → WISE OPS's key persists.
  • The backup var (WISE_OPS_OPENAI_API_KEY) in 1Password ensures the key is recoverable if wise_ops/.env is ever rebuilt.
  • OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN must be exported from ~/.hermes/.env before running op-save-secret.sh — the script doesn't source it itself.

Permission rules (Louis locked 2026-08-01)

✅ Do WITHOUT asking Louis

When someone is out on Thu/Fri/Sat PM (or any sole-boss cell):

  • Mix Mon PM with Sat PM (or any cross-DOW / cross-daypart mix)

Example with N=4:
Mon_PM_avg = mean(last 4 Mondays’ PM covers) — not mean(all PM) and not mean(whole week)/14.

  1. 14 cells always — Mon–Sun × AM+PM; each cell is its own average.
  2. Paid POS guests only (guests_total on paid tickets).
  3. Window N = 4 or 8 (pack script default 8).
  4. Split AM/PM at 4:30 PM ET.
  5. Skip closed days for that cell only; if guests missing → sales ÷ store avg check for that same DOW×daypart.

Detail: references/covers-measurement.md
Done when: 14 independent average-cover cells filled (not one week number).

Phase 2 — Server floor MINs

Use that cell’s DOW×daypart average from Phase 1 (not a shared day/week average):

Server MIN (Mon PM) = ROUNDUP( Mon_PM_avg / 30 )
Server MIN (Sat PM) = ROUNDUP( Sat_PM_avg / 30 )
# … all 14 cells the same way

Examples: Mon PM avg 150 → 5 · Sat PM avg 240 → 8.

Done when: 14 server floor numbers (one per DOW×AM/PM cell).

Phase 3 — Server payroll T / MIN / SAFE / GAP

T_s     = sum of 14 server MINs
P_MIN_s = ROUNDUP(T_s / 4)
P_SAFE_s= ROUNDUP((T_s / 4) * 1.25)
GAP_s   = max(0, P_SAFE_s − CURRENT_servers_Brain)

CURRENT = Brain primary role count for that store (active FOH).

9+ 2–3

Or ROUNDUP(server_MIN / 3.5). Then T_b ÷4 · ×1.25 · GAP vs Brain Bussers.

4C · Boss seats (not ÷30) — management pack

Hard rule: every open hour = GM or AGM or Floor. Lead never.

4D · Management board (APPROVED pack)

  1. GM — Mon/Tue/Thu 10–9 · Fri/Sat 11–10 · Wed+Sun OFF · 55h

Pathagents/mcp-oauth-connect

MCP OAuth Server Setup

Connect remote MCP servers that use OAuth 2.0 (not static API keys) to Hermes Agent.

When to Use

  • Adding a remote MCP server that returns 401 Unauthorized with a www-authenticate: Bearer header
  • Connecting services like OpenBudget, Plaid-backed tools, or any MCP server using OAuth 2.0 + PKCE
  • User asks to "connect my bank account" / "link [service] via MCP"

The Problem

hermes mcp add NAME --url URL prompts for a static "API key / Bearer token" — it does NOT handle OAuth flows. OAuth-based servers will fail with 401 Unauthorized at add-time. You must add the config directly to config.yaml instead.

Two Methods: Native (Preferred) vs Manual (Fallback)

Hermes has native OAuth support via hermes mcp add --auth oauth + hermes mcp login. This is the preferred method for any OAuth MCP server (Higgsfield, OpenBudget, etc.). The manual 7-step flow below is a fallback for servers that don't work with the native flow.

Method A: Native OAuth (Preferred — verified with Higgsfield Aug 2026)

Step 1: Add the server with --auth oauth

hermes mcp add <name> --url <https://server.example.com/mcp> --auth oauth

This prompts "Continue without authentication? [Y/n]" and "Save config anyway? [y/N]" because it can't connect yet (401 — no token). Answer Y then y to save the config.

⚠️ KNOWN QUIRK (Aug 2026): hermes mcp add --auth oauth saves the server but does NOT persist the auth: oauth field in config.yaml. The config will show auth: None. You MUST fix this before login will work:

hermes config set mcp_servers.<name>.auth oauth

Verify with grep -A5 "<name>" ~/.hermes/config.yaml — you should see auth: oauth.

Also set timeout and enable:

hermes config set mcp_servers.<name>.enabled true
hermes config set mcp_servers.<name>.timeout 300
hermes config set mcp_servers.<name>.connect_timeout 60

Step 2: Run hermes mcp login (interactive — needs a TTY)

hermes mcp login <name>

This opens a browser for the user to sign in. On success, it prints:

✓ Authenticated — N tool(s) available

Tokens are saved to ~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/<name>.json (Hermes native store).

⚠️ Cannot run from inside the gateway. If you're in a Slack gateway session, you MUST run hermes mcp login <name> from a separate Terminal. The gateway process can't handle the interactive browser OAuth flow.

Step 3: Test the connection

hermes mcp test <name>

Should show ✓ Connected and list discovered tools.

Step 4: Restart the gateway

The gateway process loaded its MCP servers at startup. New OAuth tokens are detected by the file watcher, but the tools won't be fully registered until a restart:

hermes gateway restart

⚠️ Cannot run from inside the gateway. Run from a separate Terminal. If you try from inside a Slack session, you'll get: "Blocked: command or referenced script cannot restart or stop the gateway from inside the gateway process."

After restart, the MCP tools appear as mcp__<name>_<tool> and are available in all sessions.

Step 5: Verify tools are loaded

In a new session, call any tool from the server. If tools aren't in the search index, try tool_search with the server name. If still not found, check ~/.hermes/logs/agent.log for MCP server '<name>' warnings — failed OAuth attempts show there.

Method B: Manual OAuth (Fallback)

Use this when hermes mcp login doesn't work for a specific server (e.g., the server doesn't support standard OAuth 2.1 PKCE, or hermes mcp add fails to discover the server).

B-1. Discover if the server uses OAuth

Call the registration_endpoint discovered in step 1. Save the returned client_id and a generated PKCE code_verifier + code_challenge to /tmp/<service>_oauth.json.

⚠️ Cloudflare note: Direct Python HTTP calls to Cloudflare-protected endpoints return 403 (error 1010). Adding a User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 header bypasses this for the registration endpoint. The browser tool also works.

B-2. Register a dynamic OAuth client (via terminal)

The OAuth redirect goes to http://localhost:8383/callback. Start the callback server BEFORE giving the user the auth link:

/usr/bin/python3 ~/.hermes/skills/agents/mcp-oauth-connect/scripts/oauth_callback_server.py

Run it in the background with terminal(background=True, notify_on_complete=True).

B-3. Start a local callback server

⚠️ CRITICAL LESSON: Do NOT use the Hermes browser tool to complete OAuth flows that redirect to localhost. The browser tool blocks navigation to localhost / 127.0.0.1 ("private or internal address"). This: - Resets the browser session to about:blank - Invalidates the current verification code (if email-based) - Forces a full restart of the email + code cycle, wasting time and confusing the user

Correct approach: Build the authorization URL and give it to the user to open in their own browser (where they may already be logged in):

https://<authorization_endpoint>
  ?response_type=code
  &client_id=<client_id>
  &redirect_uri=http://localhost:8383/callback
  &scope=openid profile email offline_access
  &code_challenge=<code_challenge>
  &code_challenge_method=S256

The user opens the link → signs in (or auto-approves if already logged in) → the service redirects to localhost:8383/callback?code=... → your callback server captures the auth code and saves it to /tmp/openbudget_auth_code.txt.

Check the callback server with process(action='poll', session_id=...) to see if the code was captured.

B-4. Give the user the auth URL — do NOT use the Hermes browser

Once the callback server captures the code, exchange it at the token_endpoint using the PKCE code_verifier saved in step 3. Save the resulting access_token and refresh_token.

B-5. Exchange auth code for tokens (via terminal)

hermes mcp test <name>

Then /reset or new session for tools to appear.

Pitfalls

  • hermes mcp add --auth oauth doesn't persist auth: oauth (Aug 2026 quirk): The command saves the server config but the auth field comes through as None. hermes mcp login <name> will then fail with "Server not configured for OAuth (auth=None)". Fix: run hermes config set mcp_servers.<name>.auth oauth before hermes mcp login.
  • Cannot hermes mcp login from inside the gateway: The interactive OAuth flow needs a real TTY and browser. If running inside a Slack gateway session, you must run hermes mcp login <name> from a separate Terminal. The gateway's file watcher detects new tokens but tools won't fully register until hermes gateway restart (also can't run from inside the gateway).
  • hermes mcp add interactive prompt: Asks for Bearer token — doesn't work for OAuth servers. Add config directly to config.yaml.
  • NEVER use Hermes browser for OAuth with localhost redirect: The browser tool blocks navigation to localhost/127.0.0.1 ("private or internal address"). When the OAuth flow redirects to localhost, the browser session resets to about:blank, invalidating the verification code. This wasted 3 verification code cycles in the OpenBudget session. ALWAYS give the user the auth URL to open in their own browser instead.
  • Cloudflare blocks direct API calls: urllib/requests get HTTP 403 (error 1010) from Cloudflare-protected endpoints. Workarounds: (a) add User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 header for API calls that don't require a full browser challenge, or (b) use the Hermes browser tool for Cloudflare-protected API calls.
  • Verification codes expire quickly: Each new code request invalidates the previous one. Enter the code immediately after receiving it. If the browser session resets, the old code is dead — you need a fresh one.
  • browser_console can lock the browser: Evaluating JavaScript that triggers navigation can lock the browser to about:blank. Use browser_snapshot to check state, not browser_console with DOM-mutating expressions.
  • Hermes browser ≠ user's browser: The browser tool runs its own isolated session. If the user says "I'm in" (logged in on their personal browser), the Hermes browser is NOT logged in. Don't assume shared session state.

Token Exchange (step 6 — verified working)

After the callback server captures the auth code, exchange it at the token_endpoint:

# Load saved OAuth data
import json, urllib.request, urllib.parse
with open('/tmp/<service>_oauth.json') as f:
    oauth_data = json.load(f)
with open('/tmp/oauth_auth_code.txt') as f:
    auth_code = f.read().strip()

token_data = urllib.parse.urlencode({
    'grant_type': 'authorization_code',
    'code': auth_code,
    'redirect_uri': 'http://localhost:8383/callback',
    'client_id': oauth_data['client_id'],
    'code_verifier': oauth_data['code_verifier']
}).encode()

req = urllib.request.Request(token_url, data=token_data, headers={
    'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded',
    'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0'
})
# → returns {access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, token_type, scope, id_token}

Save the full token response to /tmp/<service>_tokens.json. Then inject the Bearer token into config:

import yaml, json
with open('/tmp/<service>_tokens.json') as f:
    tokens = json.load(f)
with open(config_path) as f:
    config = yaml.safe_load(f)
config['mcp_servers']['<name>']['headers'] = {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + tokens['access_token']
}
with open(config_path, 'w') as f:
    yaml.dump(config, f, default_flow_style=False, allow_unicode=True, sort_keys=False)

Also save the refresh token to ~/.hermes/.<service>_refresh_token for auto-renewal.

Token Refresh (step 7 — verified needed)

⚠️ Access tokens expire in ~1 hour (3600s). A refresh script is required for persistence. Use scripts/refresh_token.py which: 1. Reads the refresh token from ~/.hermes/.<service>_refresh_token and/or ~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/<service>.json 2. Reads durable client_id from ~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/<service>.client.json (Hermes native store) with fallback to /tmp/<service>_oauth.json 3. POSTs to the token_endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token 4. Updates ~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/<service>.json and the Bearer header in config.yaml when present 5. Saves the new refresh token

OpenBudget durable paths (Jul 2026): - ~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/openbudget.json — access_token, refresh_token, expires_in - ~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/openbudget.client.json — client_id - ~/.hermes/.openbudget_refresh_token — legacy refresh copy

If refresh returns 401, still try the stored access_token before forcing full re-auth — it may still be valid. Non-interactive hermes mcp test may demand browser login even when direct HTTP tools/call with the stored Bearer works.

Run refresh via cron before expiry (e.g., every 45 min). Prefer Hermes venv python for yaml:
~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python3 …/scripts/refresh_token.py --service openbudget

Direct API Calls (for testing without Hermes restart)

To call MCP tools directly (without restarting Hermes), POST to the MCP server URL with: - Content-Type: application/json - Accept: application/json, text/event-stream (BOTH required — server returns 406 otherwise) - Authorization: Bearer <token>

Body is JSON-RPC 2.0: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{}},"id":1}

Response is SSE format (data: {...}\n) — parse lines starting with data:.

Securing MCP Tools by User (pre_tool_call guard plugin)

When an OAuth MCP server is in the default profile, ANY Slack user can call its tools. To restrict to specific users, create a pre_tool_call plugin in ~/.hermes/plugins/<name>_guard/:

  1. Create plugin.yaml with kind: standalone and provides_hooks: [pre_tool_call]
  2. Create __init__.py with a pre_tool_call() function that:
  3. Checks if tool_name.startswith("mcp_<server_name>_")
  4. Reads HERMES_SESSION_USER_ID from os.environ or gateway.session_context.get_session_env()
  5. Returns {"action": "block", "message": "🔒 Access denied..."} for non-allowed users
  6. Returns None (allow) for CLI/desktop (no user ID) and allowed users
  7. Enable: hermes plugins enable <name>-guard

The HERMES_SESSION_USER_ID contextvar is set by gateway/session_context.py on every gateway message. CLI sessions have no user ID → allowed (user is at the keyboard). The check is in Python code — cannot be bypassed via prompt injection.

See finance-banking skill's references/openbudget-guard-plugin.md for a complete working example.

Slack Manager Invite (Business Plan)

Puts every manager into the company Slack workspace (wiserisehospi-evh5540.slack.com) and their own store channel. Company owns the channel. GM runs their store channel like their store.

Why managers create the wrong workspace

Regular invite links land on slack.com with a big "Create a new workspace" button next to Join. They click the wrong one.

Enterprise fix (admin.users.invite) is blocked on Business — Slack returns:

"Apps with this feature are only available to Enterprise customers."

Business fix (this skill): 1. Use one company workspace invite link (from Slack admin UI) — share that, never a free "create workspace" path 2. Cron pulls managers from 7shifts → Supabase 3. Cron finds managers already in Slack and adds them to their store channel 4. Managers not in Slack get a DM to Louis + email of the company invite link (you send or paste once)

Prerequisites

Bot scopes (WISE OPS / hermes_agent)

Bot Token Scopes must include (add if missing, then Reinstall App):

Scope Why
channels:write Invite and kick on public channels
groups:write Invite and kick on private channels (store + #02-executive)
users:read List workspace members
users:read.email Match by email (strongly recommended)
chat:write Report results
channels:read / groups:read List channels

Do NOT add admin.users:write on Business — reinstall will fail (Enterprise-only).

Live scope check (2026-07-22): Both bots can conversations.kick on private channels (probe → user_not_found, not missing_scope). Private invite still broken — needs groups:write + groups:write.invites reinstall (references/business-plan-invite.md). If kick ever returns missing_scope → one fail then Louis UI Remove. Do not thrash Cua/Slack Electron.

Dual bots — membership differs (critical)

Bot Token home Sees store channels Notes
wise_ops ~/.hermes/profiles/wise_ops/.env 00001–00004, 00003 yes Prefer for store manager invite/kick/members. Not in #08-technology. 00005 may be channel_not_found.
hermes_agent / WISE BRAIN ~/.hermes/.env 00001–00002, 00004–00005, #08-technology Not in 00003 → channel_not_found. Owner-door chats often land in #08-technology (C0ARAF90JRF) — that is not a manager target.

channel_not_found is often this bot is not a member, not “channel deleted.” Re-check with the other token before telling Louis the channel is gone.

Script default: slack_manager_invite.py load_env() only reads ~/.hermes/.env (hermes). For accurate 00003 membership, run with wise_ops SLACK_BOT_TOKEN exported (parse .env in Python — do not source wise_ops .env; unquoted values break the shell).

Env vars

# Prefer wise_ops token for store channel work
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-...
SLACK_WORKSPACE_INVITE_URL=https://join.slack.com/t/wiserisehospi-evh5540/...   # often MISSING — never invent
