Finance Banking — MCP Integration

Connect Wiserise bank accounts to Hermes so you can query balances, transactions, and spending patterns directly in chat.

Architecture (First Principles)

A bank never lets you hit its internal systems directly. There's always an aggregator in between:

Hermes → MCP Server (OpenBudget) → Plaid → Bank (Truist) → Account
  • Plaid = the aggregator. Legal agreements with 10,000+ US banks. Handles credential exchange. Same tech Venmo/Robinhood use.
  • OpenBudget = the MCP layer. Wraps Plaid's API, exposes as MCP tools (get_transactions, get_balances, etc.). Read-only.
  • Hermes = the consumer. Connects to OpenBudget's remote MCP server via Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.0 + PKCE.

Nobody can move money through this pipeline — read-only by design.

Setup Steps

1. Add the MCP server to Hermes config

OpenBudget MCP URL: https://api.openbudget.sh/mcp

Add to ~/.hermes/config.yaml under mcp_servers:

mcp_servers:
  openbudget:
    url: "https://api.openbudget.sh/mcp"
    timeout: 180
    connect_timeout: 60

⚠️ Do NOT use hermes mcp add for OAuth-based MCP servers. The CLI prompts for a static bearer token, but OpenBudget uses OAuth 2.0 with PKCE — there is no static token. The CLI will fail with 401 Unauthorized and may leave a broken config entry. Add the config manually to config.yaml instead. See references/openbudget-oauth.md for full OAuth endpoint details.

2. Create an OpenBudget account + link bank

  1. Go to openbudget.sh/sign-up
  2. Sign up with email (louis@wiserisehospitalitygroup.com)
  3. Click "Connect a bank account"
  4. Search for bank (e.g., Truist) → enter online banking credentials (Plaid handles this — OpenBudget never sees the password)
  5. Select accounts (checking, savings, credit cards)
  6. Confirm read-only access
  7. Transactions sync within ~30 seconds (up to 24 months of history)

3. Complete the OAuth flow (user's own browser — NOT Hermes browser)

OpenBudget uses OAuth 2.0 with PKCE. The flow requires a browser redirect to localhost:8383/callback, which the Hermes browser tool blocks (it treats localhost as a "private/internal address" and resets to about:blank).

Correct workflow:

  1. Register a dynamic OAuth client via terminal (add User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 header to bypass Cloudflare 403). Save client_id + PKCE code_verifier to /tmp/openbudget_oauth.json.

  2. Start a local callback server in the background (listens on localhost:8383): bash /usr/bin/python3 /tmp/openbudget_oauth_server.py

  3. Give the user the auth URL to open in their own browser (where they're already logged in to OpenBudget): https://api.openbudget.sh/api/openbudget/auth/mcp/authorize ?response_type=code &client_id=<client_id> &redirect_uri=http://localhost:8383/callback &scope=openid profile email offline_access &code_challenge=<code_challenge> &code_challenge_method=S256

  4. User signs in (or auto-approves if already logged in) → redirect captured by callback server → auth code saved to /tmp/openbudget_auth_code.txt

  5. Exchange auth code for tokens at the token endpoint using the saved PKCE code_verifier

See mcp-oauth-connect skill for the reusable callback server script and detailed OAuth flow.

⚠️ NEVER use the Hermes browser tool for this OAuth flow. It cannot navigate to localhost redirect URIs. Using it wastes verification codes (each attempt invalidates the previous code) and frustrates the user. This was learned the hard way — 3 code cycles were burned before switching to the user's own browser.

4. Restart Hermes

Config changes require a new session (/reset or relaunch) for the MCP server connection to initialize.

What You Can Ask After Setup

  • "What's my Truist balance?"
  • "Show last week's transactions"
  • "How much did I spend on restaurants last month?"
  • "What recurring subscriptions am I paying for?"
  • "Compare grocery spending this month vs last"
  • "Analyze all my bank data" / "top skills for business + personal finance"

Direct MCP call when Hermes tools not loaded (verified Jul 2026)

hermes mcp test openbudget may fail in non-interactive Slack/background with: "MCP OAuth requires browser authorization… Run hermes mcp login". Native mcp_openbudget_* tools may also be missing from the session tool list even when config has the server.

Do not stop. Call OpenBudget over HTTP yourself:

  1. Token files (source of truth):
  2. Access + refresh: ~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/openbudget.json
  3. Client registration: ~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/openbudget.client.json (client_id)
  4. Legacy refresh copy: ~/.hermes/.openbudget_refresh_token

  5. Do not rely only on /tmp/openbudget_oauth.json (often missing after reboot)

  6. Try stored access token first (even if refresh just 401'd). Session Jul 13 2026: refresh 401 but access still worked for full tools/list + tools/call.

  7. JSON-RPC + SSE to https://api.openbudget.sh/mcp:

  8. Headers: Content-Type: application/json, Accept: application/json, text/event-stream (both required or 406), Authorization: Bearer <access>, User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0
  9. Body: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{...}},"id":1}

  10. Response is SSE: parse lines starting with data:, JSON-parse last payload, unwrap result.content[].text (often nested JSON string)

  11. Useful tools: list_accounts, search_transactions, get_liabilities, update_liability, list_available_categories, categorization rules tools.

  12. Amount sign (Plaid/OpenBudget): positive = spent/outflow, negative = received/inflow.

  13. Refresh script note: mcp-oauth-connect/scripts/refresh_token.py must read client_id from ~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/openbudget.client.json (not only /tmp/...). Prefer venv python that has yaml: ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python3.

Full portfolio analysis playbook (business + personal)

When Louis asks to analyze bank data / run finance / top skills for money:

  1. Balances — list_accounts + get_liabilities (use userBalanceCurrent when balanceCurrent null). Merge with ~/.hermes/wiserise/bank_balance_truth.json if still gappy. Split business cash vs personal (mask 8517 TRUIST ONE CHECKING) vs cards.
  2. Category rollups — for YTD / 90d / 30d, call search_transactions per primary category with pagination (limit 100, offset, totalCount). Sum spend vs inflow. Do not dump thousands of rows into chat.
  3. Merchant truth — top merchants inside FOOD_AND_DRINK, GENERAL_SERVICES, RENT_AND_UTILITIES, GOVERNMENT_AND_NON_PROFIT, TRANSFER_OUT, INCOME. Restaurant Plaid labels lie (see references/restaurant-bank-categories.md).
  4. Monthly trend — income (Chowbus/DoorDash), Gusto labor, PFG/COGS, tax. Flag spikes and one-off bank fees (e.g. return deposit items).
  5. Owner / personal split — transfers to 8517, wires, LIU/HEFENG-named ACH, lifestyle on business cards. Call out mix without moralizing.
  6. Answer shape for Louis — short bullets first (3–6), high-school words, lead with the answer. If he asks "top 3 skills", give operator skills grounded in HIS numbers (cash control, true P&L categories, tax/fixed calendar + personal split) — not a generic finance textbook list. Optional second block: Hermes skills to use weekly (finance-banking, pos-chowbus/pos-fraud, people payroll/roster).

See references/restaurant-bank-categories.md for Wiserise-specific category → real P&L mapping and known merchant patterns.

Balance truth when Plaid is partial (locked Jul 2026)

Plaid/OpenBudget often syncs transactions for all Truist accounts but returns null balances on many (not an offline connection — hasError false). App totals ≠ OpenBudget totalNetWorth in that state.

Source of truth order for "what's my balance": 1. If OpenBudget has complete cash balances (all main operating accounts non-null) → use OpenBudget. 2. Else use snapshot file: ~/.hermes/wiserise/bank_balance_truth.json (from Truist app / Louis photo) and say stale-as-of date. 3. Never present partial OpenBudget net worth as full company cash without flagging gap.

Automation limits: - Hermes cannot complete Plaid bank login (password / 2FA) — that is the only human step, and only when reconnect is required. - Daily "open OpenBudget and re-link" is NOT the ops model. - Card balances can be forced via update_liability(balance=...). Checking balances cannot — no depository override tool.

When Louis sends a Truist balances screenshot: update bank_balance_truth.json immediately; set card update_liability overrides; answer from snapshot.

Pitfalls

  • hermes mcp add doesn't work for OAuth servers — expects a static bearer token. Add config manually to config.yaml.
  • NEVER use Hermes browser for OAuth with localhost redirect — the browser tool blocks localhost/127.0.0.1 navigation ("private/internal address"), resets to about:blank, and invalidates the current verification code. Give the user the auth URL to open in their own browser instead. See mcp-oauth-connect skill for the full workflow.
  • Cloudflare blocks direct API calls — Python requests/urllib to OpenBudget API endpoints return 403 (error code 1010). Workaround: add User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 header for API calls, or use the Hermes browser tool.
  • Hermes browser ≠ user's browser — the browser tool runs its own isolated session. If the user says "I'm in" (logged in on their personal browser), the Hermes browser is NOT logged in.
  • Verification codes expire quickly — each new code request invalidates the previous one. If a code fails, get a fresh one.
  • OpenBudget free tier is 7 days — then paid plan required. Check pricing.
  • Token expires in 1 hour — access tokens expire in 3600s. Prefer ~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/openbudget.json (+ .client.json for client_id). Legacy: ~/.hermes/.openbudget_refresh_token. Refresh script must use durable client path; system python may lack yaml — use Hermes venv. If refresh 401s, still try current access token before forcing full re-login.
  • Hermes MCP tools absent ≠ no bank access — use direct HTTP tools/call (see Direct MCP section). Do not tell Louis "bank tools are broken" until token + HTTP path both fail.
  • Never trust raw Plaid categories for restaurant P&L — FOOD_AND_DRINK is mostly vendor COGS; GENERAL_SERVICES includes Gusto + some rent; TRANSFER_OUT mixes internal moves and vendors. Always merchant-rollup before conclusions.
  • Partial card null balances — get_liabilities.userBalanceCurrent and bank_balance_truth.json beat inventing net worth from partial balanceCurrent.

Security — Owner-Only Access (Louis + Luna; verified Jul 2026)

By default, any MCP server in the default profile is accessible from Slack. Bank data is restricted to owners via openbudget_guard.

Allowed Slack IDs (same set as WISE BRAIN owner door): - Louis U08TW3FEDNE - Luna U0AP162P3KM (wife — same owner perms, locked 2026-07-13)

  1. Plugin at ~/.hermes/plugins/openbudget_guard/ — pre_tool_call checks HERMES_SESSION_USER_ID against LOUIS_SLACK_IDS (name is historical; set = all owners).
  2. If ID not in set:
  3. Silent block — {"action": "block", "message": "No bank account data is available."} (no hint bank data exists).
  4. DM alert to Louis — chat.postMessage to D0BGEEPQ141 with who/where/tool/args/when.
  5. CLI/desktop (no user ID) → allow (owner at keyboard).
  6. Enable: hermes plugins enable openbudget-guard.

⚠️ Preference: non-owners get silence + Louis is DM-alerted. Luna is not “non-owner” — keep her in LOUIS_SLACK_IDS and the full 4-place owner list (owner-gate, openbudget_guard, config.yaml slack.allow_from, .env SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS). See wiserise-architecture → access-control.

See references/openbudget-guard-plugin.md for plugin shape.

Key details: - Owner IDs: Louis U08TW3FEDNE, Luna U0AP162P3KM - Alert DM: D0BGEEPQ141 (Louis home) - Blocks all mcp_openbudget_* for non-owners - Code check, not prompt — not bypassable by prompt injection

Makes an HTML SOP — short, plain, easy to follow. HTML only, no Word docs. The HTML is the master. For the Playbook page it is turned into a PDF (Chrome).

sop_builder.py stays on disk as a shared library (voice-check words, brand colors). We no longer build .docx files. Do not call sop_builder to make a doc.

Architecture (3 core — the rest are push destinations)

Load wiserise-architecture for the full framework. Key rules for SOPs:

Core SOP Role Rule
🧠 Brain (Supabase) Source of truth for SOP numbers, content, status, PDF link sops table = one ledger. Never read SOP data from Sheets or Obsidian as truth.
⚡ Hermes Sole worker — builds HTML, runs voice check, publishes This skill tells Hermes how. No sub-agents.
💬 Slack Where Louis or Luna approves publishing Human gate: never publish without explicit owner yes in Slack.

Push destinations (automatic, not human steps): Drive (PDF upload via sop_publish), Sheets (index auto-refresh). Obsidian wiki push = future, not built yet.

Key rule: The Brain (sops table) is the one truth. Drive = legal original push destination. Never read from Drive/Sheets/Obsidian as source.

The 5-step workflow (Elon algorithm — simplified v3.0)

1. RESERVE     → number from Brain (sop_registry → sops table)
2. BUILD       → HTML with voice check inline (add form/example if needed)
3. SHOW        → .html file in Slack — "SOP NO · title · Approve publish?"
4. APPROVE     → Louis or Luna says yes (HARD GATE — no auto-publish)
5. PUBLISH     → HTML→PDF→Storage→Brain row (status=live)

No separate form-test step. No separate example-test step. No separate voice-check step. Those are decisions made during BUILD, not checkpoints after.

SOP NUMBER (step 1 — Supabase sops table is the source of truth)

Every SOP gets a number from sop_registry.py, never a made-up one. It computes the next free number live from the Supabase sops table.

Pick the SERIES (aligned with the 7 Playbooks shelves), then call reserve:

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/louisliu/.hermes/skills/wiserise/wiserise-sop")
import sop_registry as reg

sop_no = reg.reserve("TEAM", "Onboarding Buddy SOP")   # -> e.g. "TEAM-018"
  • Series: SAF (safety/inspections), GST (guests), SHIFT (running the shift), TEAM (hiring/training/write-ups), PAY (pay/tips/breaks), CASH (cash/purchasing), REF (look-up docs), GNG / MAS / LCB (brand role + task docs).
  • reserve(series, title) returns the number. Peek without logging: reg.next_free("TEAM").
  • Old prefixes (OPS/HR/FIN/SYS/GM) are rejected with a hint to the new series.

The look (Wiserise brand template — Brand Guidelines v1.0 §05)

build_html() lays it out top to bottom, always this order: 1. Header band — navy #152035. White text wordmark "WISERISE / HOSPITALITY GROUP" on the left, "STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE" label on the right. No logo image. 2. Title — Unna Bold, navy, with a gold #C4A55A accent rule under it. 3. Info chips — SOP NO | WRITTEN BY | DATE. 4. Body rows — navy-deep #1E3152 label (white caps) on left, body text on right. 5. PROCEDURE — gold-numbered step cards. Add "checkbox": True for check boxes + progress bar. 6. No sign-off block. 7. Footer — "WISERISE HOSPITALITY GROUP · CONFIDENTIAL · FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY".

Required rows + optional rows (simplified — first principles)

Two rows are REQUIRED on every SOP:

  • WHO — the role this is for. "Closing staff."
  • WHAT IF — the escape hatch when it goes wrong. "Drawer is short? Call the manager."

Add these ONLY if they apply:

  • WHEN — when they do it and how often. Skip for reference docs (wage bands, tip rules).
  • WHAT YOU NEED — the stuff to grab first. Skip if no tools/items needed.
  • PROCEDURE — the steps. Most SOPs have this. Pure reference docs may not.
  • PURPOSE — one line on why. Add if the title isn't self-explanatory.

Do NOT use: SCOPE (always duplicates WHO), RESPONSIBILITY (usually same as WHO).

Row options

  • Text row: {"label": "WHO", "text": "Closing staff."}
  • Steps row: {"label": "PROCEDURE", "steps": ["Count the drawer.", "Lock up."]}
  • Sub-numbers: add "prefix": "1" → steps number as 1.1, 1.2, 1.3
  • Keyword styling (automatic): step written as Keyword — detail → KEYWORD — detail
  • Checklist: add "checkbox": True for tap-to-check boxes + progress bar
  • Filled example: gold-pill header over gold-edged card of label → value rows: python {"label": "FILLED EXAMPLE", "sub": "One shift, done right — copy the style, not the words.", "foot": "Before you leave: every Required field green.", "example": [ {"k": "TODAY'S GOAL", "v": "Goal: $5,500. Last Tuesday: $5,000. Beat it by 10%."}, {"k": "SHIFT RECAP", "v": "Busy dinner rush, 7 to 9. Steady after."}, ]}
  • Flow banner: pass flow=[{"num":1,"label":"DOCUMENT","sub":"Write it down"}, ...]

Voice rules (MANDATORY — runs inline during BUILD)

  • Max 15 words per line. Count them.
  • One idea per line. No jargon. Active voice. Be blunt.
  • Swap fancy words: optimize→make better, utilize→use, implement→build/do, facilitate→help, ensure→make sure, prior to→before, escalate→tell the boss.
  • check_voice() runs inside build_html(). Fix warnings before showing.

Companion form + filled example (decide during BUILD, not after)

Companion form: Does following this SOP require writing, signing, counting, or logging? - Yes → build with wiserise-form skill alongside the SOP. - No → skip. Most "just do it" SOPs need none.

Filled example: Would a new person do better if they SAW one finished sample? - Yes → add ONE example row to the end of rows. - No → skip.

These are build-time decisions, not separate checkpoint steps.

How to make one (steps 1–3: reserve, build, show)

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/louisliu/.hermes/skills/wiserise/wiserise-sop")
import sop_html_builder as h
import sop_registry as reg

title = "Opening the Store"
sop_no = reg.reserve("SHIFT", title)          # step 1: reserve

rows = [
    {"label": "WHO", "text": "Opening manager. First person in the building."},
    {"label": "WHEN", "text": "Every morning. 30 minutes before doors open."},
    {"label": "WHAT YOU NEED", "text": "Keys. Alarm code. Opening checklist. Cash bag."},
    {"label": "PROCEDURE", "steps": [
        "Unlock the front door. Turn off the alarm right away.",
        "Walk the dining room. Check for leaks, breaks, or mess.",
        "Turn on lights, music, and AC.",
        "Count the cash drawer. Set it to the starting amount.",
        "Open the POS. Log in. Test one order.",
        "Unlock the front door for guests at opening time.",
    ]},
    {"label": "WHAT IF", "steps": [
        "Alarm does not turn off? Call Louis right now. Do not leave.",
        "Cash drawer is short? Count again. If still short, call Louis.",
        "POS will not boot? Restart once. If still down, call Louis.",
    ]},
]

html = h.build_html(title, sop_no, "Louis Liu", "August 1, 2026", rows)  # step 2: build (voice check inline)

out_path = f"/tmp/{sop_no}_Opening-the-Store_SOP.html"
h.save_html(html, out_path)                   # step 3: show in Slack via MEDIA:
print("done", sop_no)

Show in Slack (Louis locked 2026-07-23): - Attach the .html file itself via MEDIA:/abs/path/Name.html - Short clean filename: {SOP_NO}_{Short-Title}.html - Short text above media: SOP NO · title · Approve publish? - Do NOT dump PNGs as the default review format unless Louis asks "screenshot"

⭐ Step 4–5: Approve + Publish (HUMAN GATE — always get approval)

HARD RULE: never publish without Louis or Luna's explicit approval. 1. Build the HTML and show it (steps 1–3 above). 2. ASK: "Approve publishing this to the Playbook page (text + PDF)?" 3. Only on a clear yes from Louis or Luna, run publish:

import sop_html_builder as h
import sop_publish as pub

rows = [ ... ]
html = h.build_html("Closing the Store", "SHIFT-099", "Louis Liu", "June 30, 2026", rows)
html_path = "/tmp/SHIFT-099_Closing_SOP.html"
h.save_html(html, html_path)

sop_id, file_url = pub.publish_sop(
    html_path, title="Closing the Store", sop_no="SHIFT-099",
    rows=rows, brand_key="company", audience="staff",
    synonyms="closing, lock up, end of night",
)
print(sop_id, file_url)
  • ALWAYS set audience. manager for sensitive SOPs, staff for everyone.
  • Re-publishing same title+brand updates the row.
  • After publish, set registry status 🔨 building → ✅ live.
  • Either owner may approve; do not wait for the other owner unless they ask.

Do NOT auto-publish. No exceptions. GM/store "yes" never counts.

Slack Notification Format

When posting SOP status to Slack (approval request, publish confirmation), follow slack-message-structure:

📋 *SOP — {Title} / {Brand}*
SOP NO: {sop_no}
Status: 🔨 Building / ✅ Live
Type: SOP (or FORM)
Audience: Staff / Manager
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

⛔ Never show terminal output, Python scripts, or curl commands in Slack. The human only sees the result — SOP number, status, and next step. Use execute_code silently.

Brain → Push destinations

Action Brain (sops table) Drive (org-files bucket) Sheets
Reserve number status='building' row inserted — —
Build HTML — — —
Publish (approved ⭐) status='live', file_url set, content set PDF uploaded Index auto-refreshed
Rebuild Same row updated Old PDF removed, new uploaded —

All data flows Brain → outward. Never read from Drive/Sheets as source for SOP operations.

Shared Python Scripts

All under ~/.hermes/skills/wiserise/wiserise-sop/:

Script Purpose
sop_builder.py Voice rules (JARGON dict, MAX_WORDS=15), brand colors. Shared library — do NOT use for .docx (legacy, dead path).
sop_html_builder.py Clickable HTML SOP builder. build_html(), save_html(), check_voice().
sop_registry.py Numbering from Supabase. next_free(), reserve(), next_free_form(), reserve_form().
sop_publish.py HTML→PDF (headless Chrome), PDF→Storage upload, row→sops table. publish_sop().

The Form skill (form_html_builder.py) depends on sop_builder.py for voice rules.

Atomic update rule (Louis locked 2026-08-01)

When updating ANY SOP or form, you MUST update all three in one operation: 1. File — upload to org-files/ bucket root (bare filename, no playbooks/ prefix) 2. content — the plain-text field in sops table (what the bot reads for Slack replies) 3. file_url — must be the bare filename (e.g. CASH-009_Weekly_Purchase_Order_SOP.html)

Why: The bot reads content for its Slack reply text — NOT the HTML file. If you update the file but not content, the bot shows old text. If you update content but not file_url, the download link breaks. All three must move together.

Never set file_url to org-files/filename (includes bucket name) — use bare filename. Never set file_url to playbooks/filename (old subfolder) — use bucket root.

Common Pitfalls

  1. Publishing without approval. Always ask Louis first. No exceptions.
  2. Skipping the voice check. If check_voice() reports problems, fix them before showing the SOP.
  3. Making .docx files. HTML only. The .docx builder is legacy — do not use.
  4. Inventing SOP numbers. Always use sop_registry.reserve(). Never make up a number.
  5. Using old series prefixes. OPS/HR/FIN/SYS/GM are retired. Use the new series.
  6. Terminal output in Slack. Never show curl, Python, or shell commands. Only the result.
  7. Missing companion form. If the SOP requires writing, signing, counting, or logging → build the form too.
  8. Partial updates — updating file but not content, or content but not file_url. Always update all three atomically. (Louis 2026-08-01)
  9. Using playbooks/ prefix in file_url. Files go in bucket root. Bare filename only. (Louis 2026-08-01)
  10. Missing companion form. If the SOP requires writing, signing, counting, or logging → build the form too.

Done checklist (5 items)

  • [ ] Voice check passed (inline — every line ≤15 words, no jargon)
  • [ ] WHO + WHAT IF present (other rows only if they apply)
  • [ ] Shown in Slack as .html file attachment (MEDIA:)
  • [ ] Louis or Luna approved BEFORE publishing
  • [ ] Brain sops table = status live, file_url set

People Job Ads & Flyers

Class skill for external recruiting creative: Indeed copy, Facebook/IG ads, and 1-page flyers (PDF + PNG).
Store gap-check / Gate 1 pipeline stays in people-recruiting.

When to use

  • "create Facebook / Indeed ads"
  • "make a flyer" / "hiring poster"
  • "redesign the ad" / "5 different designs"
  • "rate this ad/design on first principles"
  • "post online" / "post to Facebook" for a job ad
  • Recruit non-floor roles (trainer, area coach) or any public job creative
  • "offer letter" for HQ/corporate or salaried store leadership (Regional People Coach, HR Manager, GM, Trainer, etc.)
  • "add offer letter tab" / lock pack from attached letter / "approved and update people department"

When NOT to use

  • GM says "need 1 server" in store channel → people-recruiting
  • Onboarding / training days → people-recruiting / people-gm-train
  • Internal SOP/forms → wiserise-sop / wiserise-form

First principles (score every draft)

Principle Pass looks like
One job Single role title
One promise One plain sentence (what they do)
One pay Band from REF-002 or Louis-set; big on flyer
One apply path Per channel: FB = DM this post; Indeed = Apply on Indeed — never DM+email+QR together
Few teaches Max 4 bullets/boxes
Fast scan Title → pay → apply readable on phone in ~2s
No new system Teach existing Wiserise system only (don't invent frameworks in the ad)

Rate on request: give X/10 + 3 bullets strong + gaps + one fix. Don't rebuild unless asked.

Louis style (hard lessons)

  1. Confused / 看不下去 → halve copy. One short ad block only. No multi-section essays. (clear-simple-bullets)
  2. Don't stack options → decide defaults (pay band, CTA, cities).
  3. Template attach → match layout once; if he says "don't like it / redesign your way" → full original, not another template clone.
  4. Show N designs → N visually different systems (not recolors). Deliver all PNG+PDF; table of vibe + best channel; ask A/B/C pick.
  5. Final lock → one CTA version for FB, separate twin for Indeed if both channels.
  6. Post online → try Composio Facebook publish before saying blocked (he will ask why Composio/1P were not used).

Default content spine (trainer example → generalize)

Title: {Role}
Pay: ${low}–${high}/hr (or salary) · Full-time
Promise: one line, floor-real
Teach: ≤4 plain items
Need: 3 bullets max (years / drive / teach clear)
Apply: ONE path + one proof ask (e.g. week-1 server plan)
Geo: NC cities when multi-unit (or named store)
Brand: Wiserise Hospitality Group

Pay: query live sops REF-002. Trainer = HQ band $18–$22/hr (locked 2026-07-18). If any other role missing, state DOE in nearest band and note Louis must lock. Don't invent salary without him.

Workflow

  1. Confirm role + channel (FB / Indeed / both / flyer only). Store geo when he names a store (e.g. Gangnam Wilmington).
  2. Pull pay band REF-002 if management/hourly known.
  3. Draft short text ad first (Indeed full + FB primary/headline).
  4. If flyer / feed creative: HTML → headless Chrome PDF + PNG (square 1080 for FB feed).
  5. Attach with MEDIA: paths (PDF + PNG). Also save Desktop copies.
  6. If he says post online / post to Facebook / boost: do not stop at copy. Follow Facebook publish path below before saying blocked.
  7. On "rate first principles" → score only unless "update".
  8. On "update base on recommendation" → apply only the listed fixes; keep the same visual system unless he asked redesign.
  9. On "redesign completely" → new art direction; new photo OK via image_generate.

Facebook publish path (Louis: "why block — Composio / 1P?")

Order — always try before "can't post":

  1. Composio Facebook (preferred) — COMPOSIO_API_KEY + connected account toolkit=facebook status=ACTIVE.
  2. List pages: POST /api/v3/tools/execute/FACEBOOK_GET_USER_PAGES (user_id=hermes-louis + active connected_account_id).
  3. Map store → page name; re-list if ids drift (do not hardcode forever).
  4. Photo: FACEBOOK_CREATE_PHOTO_POST (page_id, message, url = https image, published=true).
  5. Text fallback: FACEBOOK_CREATE_POST.
  6. Image host: upload PNG → Brain org-files/marketing/fb-ads/… → signed URL Meta can fetch.
  7. If 403 / missing pages_manage_posts: list ≠ publish. Immediately:
  8. POST /api/v3/connected_accounts/link with Facebook auth_config + user_id=hermes-louis
  9. Open redirect_url; Louis approves as Page admin
  10. On “done”, retry post. Do not blame “no Composio.”
  11. 1Password — which login owns the page only. Meta Ads env rows are often REPLACE-WITH-… placeholders — ignore. Never type FB passwords into browser (password ≠ Graph publish).
  12. Browser GUI — only after Composio tried, and only if already logged in as page admin.

Pitfall (2026-07-18): Declaring blocked because Chrome shows public Log in while Composio Facebook is ACTIVE is wrong. Execute Composio + read error body first; then re-auth link; only then ask manual paste.

Details: references/facebook-composio-publish.md

Flyer production (known-good)

# HTML at /tmp/wiserise-job-ads/{slug}.html
# local images as relative files next to HTML
CHROME="/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"
"$CHROME" --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-pdf-header-footer \
  --print-to-pdf="$OUT.pdf" "file://$HTML"
"$CHROME" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars \
  --window-size=816,1056 --force-device-scale-factor=2 \
  --screenshot="$OUT.png" "file://$HTML"
# Verify exactly 1 PDF page before sending
python3 -c "from pypdf import PdfReader; assert len(PdfReader('$OUT.pdf').pages)==1"

Pitfalls: - 2-page PDF = tighten spacing; re-render before Slack. - Chrome screenshot black bars = use 816×1056 + device scale 2, or rasterize PDF page. - AVIF template refs: convert with sips -s format png before vision. - Photo paths must be relative to the HTML file for file:// print.

Design directions (when user wants variety)

Ship distinct systems, not theme tweaks:

Code System
Swiss Hard red/black grid poster
Editorial Cream paper / serif magazine

Premium dark Charcoal + gold cards (good default HQ after template rejection)

If he attaches a template, match it first. If he says he doesn’t like it / “redesign your way” → do not ship another template clone; switch to premium dark or a fresh system.

Channel twins: when both FB and Indeed matter, export two files (CTA text only differs: “DM this post” vs “Apply on Indeed”). Never mix three apply doors on one asset.

Channel copy rules

Facebook primary: ≤ short paragraph + pay + one CTA line.
Indeed: title, location, bullets, must-haves, apply proof ask.
Boost/short: one block under 500 chars.

Never put long Supabase links on flyers. No internal jargon (Brain, Gate 2, WISE BRAIN).

HQ Offer Letters (Regional People Coach, Trainer, multi-unit roles)

Trigger: Louis asks for an offer letter for a corporate/HQ role.

Not store hire pipeline. No store channel, no Gate 1, no auto Landing Page. Direct owner → candidate offer.

Structure (one page, scannable)

Wiserise Hospitality Group — Offer Letter
{Role Title}
Date / To / From (owner)

The Role (2–3 lines)
Pay & Terms (salary, hours, mileage, hotel, office, review, start)
Weekly Schedule (Mon–Fri)
What You Do (HR lifecycle order, numbered)
What You Don't (authority split, numbered)
Acceptance (sign + return by deadline, contingency)

HR lifecycle order for "What You Do"

  1. Coach managers (main job — fixes root cause)
  2. Recruiting — phone-screen, hire store team members
  3. Onboarding — Day 1 paperwork, audit
  4. Schedule — audit GM schedules (labor %, posted on time) ← NOT "build schedules"
  5. Develop — 1:1s, performance check-ins, promotions ← missing stage = B-grade, add it
  6. Payroll — check timesheets
  7. Exit — write-ups, fire store team members

Why this order: hire → onboard → schedule → develop → pay → exit. The "develop" stage is the one most offer letters skip — it's the biggest HR job between onboarding and exit.

Authority split ("What You Don't")

  1. Hire or fire managers (owner approves)
  2. Approve payroll (owner + payroll do)
  3. Touch the bank
  4. Keep separate spreadsheets (system integrity)

"Update based on recommendation" workflow

When Louis says "update based on recommendation" / "update base on recommendation": 1. Find the prior session via session_search (session may have been reset by daily schedule) 2. Find the last rating/recommendation message (e.g. "B+ — two leaks") 3. Apply ONLY the listed fixes — do not redesign 4. Rebuild the PDF 5. Show the full text in Slack + attach PDF via MEDIA: 6. Do NOT ask "可以?" again if he already said "update" — just do it

FPDF2 production

  • Build script: /tmp/{slug}_offer_v{N}.py using fpdf2 library
  • Output: ~/Desktop/Wiserise_Offer_{Candidate}_{Role}.pdf
  • Preview: pdftoppm -png -r 150 "{pdf}" /tmp/{slug}_offer_v{N}
  • Verify text: pdftotext "{pdf}" - — confirms all items present (vision model may miscount items in image renders)
  • Python env: /Users/louisliu/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python3 (has fpdf2 installed)

1-page fit (when content overflows)

If the last item gets cut off at the page bottom: - Reduce numbered() lh from 0.17 → 0.16 and space_after from 0.02 → 0.01 - Reduce hr() space_before from 0.05 → 0.03 and space_after from 0.08 → 0.05 - Reduce role description space_after from 0.06 → 0.04 and lh from 0.17 → 0.16 - Always verify with pdftotext after rebuild — vision model can miscount items in image render

Pitfall: vision_analyze on a PDF page PNG may report items as "missing" when they are actually present in the PDF. Always cross-check with pdftotext "{pdf}" - before re-rendering.

JS required

function showPage(id,btn){
  document.querySelectorAll('.page').forEach(p=>p.classList.remove('active'));
  document.querySelectorAll('.tab').forEach(t=>t.classList.remove('active'));
  document.getElementById(id).classList.add('active');
  btn.classList.add('active');
  window.scrollTo({top:0,behavior:'smooth'});
}
function goTab(i){document.querySelectorAll('.tab')[i].click()}
function setLang(lang,btn){
  document.body.className='lang-'+lang;
  document.querySelectorAll('.lang-btn').forEach(b=>b.classList.remove('active'));
  btn.classList.add('active');
}
// arrow keys switch tabs

First tab label must match first .page.active.

Pathproductivity/google-workspace

Google Workspace

Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Contacts, Sheets, and Docs — through Hermes-managed OAuth and a thin CLI wrapper. When gws is installed, the skill uses it as the execution backend for broader Google Workspace coverage; otherwise it falls back to the bundled Python client implementation.

References

  • references/gmail-search-syntax.md — Gmail search operators (is:unread, from:, newer_than:, etc.)

Scripts

  • scripts/setup.py — OAuth2 setup (run once to authorize)
  • scripts/google_api.py — compatibility wrapper CLI. It prefers gws for operations when available, while preserving Hermes' existing JSON output contract.

First-Time Setup

The setup is fully non-interactive — you drive it step by step so it works on CLI, Telegram, Discord, or any platform.

Define a shorthand first:

GSETUP="python ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/productivity/google-workspace/scripts/setup.py"

Step 0: Check if already set up

$GSETUP --check

If it prints AUTHENTICATED, skip to Usage — setup is already done.

Step 1: Triage — ask the user what they need

Before starting OAuth setup, ask the user TWO questions:

Question 1: "What Google services do you need? Just email, or also Calendar/Drive/Sheets/Docs?"

  • Email only → They don't need this skill at all. Use the himalaya skill instead — it works with a Gmail App Password (Settings → Security → App Passwords) and takes 2 minutes to set up. No Google Cloud project needed. Load the himalaya skill and follow its setup instructions.

  • Email + Calendar → Continue with this skill, but use --services email,calendar during auth so the consent screen only asks for the scopes they actually need.

  • Calendar/Drive/Sheets/Docs only → Continue with this skill and use a narrower --services set like calendar,drive,sheets,docs.

  • Full Workspace access → Continue with this skill and use the default all service set.

Question 2: "Does your Google account use Advanced Protection (hardware security keys required to sign in)? If you're not sure, you probably don't — it's something you would have explicitly enrolled in."

  • No / Not sure → Normal setup. Continue below.
  • Yes → Their Workspace admin must add the OAuth client ID to the org's allowed apps list before Step 4 will work. Let them know upfront.

Step 2: Create OAuth credentials (one-time, ~5 minutes)

Tell the user:

You need a Google Cloud OAuth client. This is a one-time setup:

  1. Create or select a project: https://console.cloud.google.com/projectselector2/home/dashboard
  2. Enable the required APIs from the API Library: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library Enable: Gmail API, Google Calendar API, Google Drive API, Google Sheets API, Google Docs API, People API
  3. Create the OAuth client here: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth 2.0 Client ID
  4. Application type: "Desktop app" → Create
  5. If the app is still in Testing, add the user's Google account as a test user here: https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/audience Audience → Test users → Add users
  6. Download the JSON file and tell me the file path

Important Hermes CLI note: if the file path starts with /, do NOT send only the bare path as its own message in the CLI, because it can be mistaken for a slash command. Send it in a sentence instead, like: The JSON file path is: /home/user/Downloads/client_secret_....json

Once they provide the path:

$GSETUP --client-secret /path/to/client_secret.json

If they paste the raw client ID / client secret values instead of a file path, write a valid Desktop OAuth JSON file for them yourself, save it somewhere explicit (for example ~/Downloads/hermes-google-client-secret.json), then run --client-secret against that file.

Step 3: Get authorization URL

Use the service set chosen in Step 1. Examples:

$GSETUP --auth-url --services email,calendar --format json
$GSETUP --auth-url --services calendar,drive,sheets,docs --format json
$GSETUP --auth-url --services all --format json

This returns JSON with an auth_url field and also saves the exact URL to ~/.hermes/google_oauth_last_url.txt.

Agent rules for this step: - Extract the auth_url field and send that exact URL to the user as a single line. - Tell the user that the browser will likely fail on http://localhost:1 after approval, and that this is expected. - Tell them to copy the ENTIRE redirected URL from the browser address bar. - If the user gets Error 403: access_denied, send them directly to https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/audience to add themselves as a test user.

Step 4: Exchange the code

The user will paste back either a URL like http://localhost:1/?code=4/0A...&scope=... or just the code string. Either works. The --auth-url step stores a temporary pending OAuth session locally so --auth-code can complete the PKCE exchange later, even on headless systems:

$GSETUP --auth-code "THE_URL_OR_CODE_THE_USER_PASTED" --format json

If --auth-code fails because the code expired, was already used, or came from an older browser tab, it now returns a fresh fresh_auth_url. In that case, immediately send the new URL to the user and have them retry with the newest browser redirect only.

Step 5: Verify

$GSETUP --check

Should print AUTHENTICATED. Setup is complete — token refreshes automatically from now on.

Notes

  • Token is stored at ~/.hermes/google_token.json and auto-refreshes.
  • Pending OAuth session state/verifier are stored temporarily at ~/.hermes/google_oauth_pending.json until exchange completes.
  • If gws is installed, google_api.py points it at the same ~/.hermes/google_token.json credentials file. Users do not need to run a separate gws auth login flow.
  • To revoke: $GSETUP --revoke

Usage

All commands go through the API script. Set GAPI as a shorthand:

GAPI="python ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/productivity/google-workspace/scripts/google_api.py"

Gmail

# Search (returns JSON array with id, from, subject, date, snippet)
$GAPI gmail search "is:unread" --max 10
$GAPI gmail search "from:boss@company.com newer_than:1d"
$GAPI gmail search "has:attachment filename:pdf newer_than:7d"

# Read full message (returns JSON with body text)
$GAPI gmail get MESSAGE_ID

# Send
$GAPI gmail send --to user@example.com --subject "Hello" --body "Message text"
$GAPI gmail send --to user@example.com --subject "Report" --body "<h1>Q4</h1><p>Details...</p>" --html
$GAPI gmail send --to user@example.com --subject "Hello" --from '"Research Agent" <user@example.com>' --body "Message text"

# Reply (automatically threads and sets In-Reply-To)
$GAPI gmail reply MESSAGE_ID --body "Thanks, that works for me."
$GAPI gmail reply MESSAGE_ID --from '"Support Bot" <user@example.com>' --body "Thanks"

# Labels
$GAPI gmail labels
$GAPI gmail modify MESSAGE_ID --add-labels LABEL_ID
$GAPI gmail modify MESSAGE_ID --remove-labels UNREAD

Calendar

# List events (defaults to next 7 days)
$GAPI calendar list
$GAPI calendar list --start 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z --end 2026-03-07T23:59:59Z

# Create event (ISO 8601 with timezone required)
$GAPI calendar create --summary "Team Standup" --start 2026-03-01T10:00:00-06:00 --end 2026-03-01T10:30:00-06:00
$GAPI calendar create --summary "Lunch" --start 2026-03-01T12:00:00Z --end 2026-03-01T13:00:00Z --location "Cafe"
$GAPI calendar create --summary "Review" --start 2026-03-01T14:00:00Z --end 2026-03-01T15:00:00Z --attendees "alice@co.com,bob@co.com"

# Delete event
$GAPI calendar delete EVENT_ID

Drive

# Search existing files
$GAPI drive search "quarterly report" --max 10
$GAPI drive search "mimeType='application/pdf'" --raw-query --max 5

# Get metadata for a single file
$GAPI drive get FILE_ID

# Upload a local file (auto-detects MIME type)
$GAPI drive upload /path/to/report.pdf
$GAPI drive upload /path/to/image.png --name "Logo.png" --parent FOLDER_ID

# Download (binary files download as-is; Google-native files export to a
# sensible default — Docs→pdf, Sheets→csv, Slides→pdf, Drawings→png)
$GAPI drive download FILE_ID
$GAPI drive download DOC_ID --output ~/doc.pdf
$GAPI drive download DOC_ID --export-mime text/plain --output ~/doc.txt

# Create a folder
$GAPI drive create-folder "Reports"
$GAPI drive create-folder "Q4" --parent FOLDER_ID

# Share
$GAPI drive share FILE_ID --email alice@example.com --role reader
$GAPI drive share FILE_ID --email alice@example.com --role writer --notify
$GAPI drive share FILE_ID --type anyone --role reader        # anyone with link
$GAPI drive share FILE_ID --type domain --domain example.com --role reader

# Delete — defaults to trash (reversible). Use --permanent to skip the trash.
$GAPI drive delete FILE_ID
$GAPI drive delete FILE_ID --permanent

Contacts

$GAPI contacts list --max 20

Sheets

# Create a new spreadsheet
$GAPI sheets create --title "Q4 Budget"
$GAPI sheets create --title "Inventory" --sheet-name "Stock"

# Read
$GAPI sheets get SHEET_ID "Sheet1!A1:D10"

# Write
$GAPI sheets update SHEET_ID "Sheet1!A1:B2" --values '[["Name","Score"],["Alice","95"]]'

# Append rows
$GAPI sheets append SHEET_ID "Sheet1!A:C" --values '[["new","row","data"]]'

Docs

# Read
$GAPI docs get DOC_ID

# Create a new Doc (optionally seeded with body text)
$GAPI docs create --title "Meeting Notes"
$GAPI docs create --title "Draft" --body "First paragraph..."

# Append text to the end of an existing Doc
$GAPI docs append DOC_ID --text "Additional content to append"

Output Format

All commands return JSON. Parse with jq or read directly. Key fields:

  • Gmail search: [{id, threadId, from, to, subject, date, snippet, labels}]
  • Gmail get: {id, threadId, from, to, subject, date, labels, body}
  • Gmail send/reply: {status: "sent", id, threadId}
  • Calendar list: [{id, summary, start, end, location, description, htmlLink}]
  • Calendar create: {status: "created", id, summary, htmlLink}
  • Drive search: [{id, name, mimeType, modifiedTime, webViewLink}]
  • Drive get: {id, name, mimeType, modifiedTime, size, webViewLink, parents, owners}
  • Drive upload: {status: "uploaded", id, name, mimeType, webViewLink}
  • Drive download: {status: "downloaded", id, name, path, mimeType}
  • Drive create-folder: {status: "created", id, name, webViewLink}
  • Drive share: {status: "shared", permissionId, fileId, role, type}
  • Drive delete: {status: "trashed" | "deleted", fileId, permanent}
  • Contacts list: [{name, emails: [...], phones: [...]}]
  • Sheets get: [[cell, cell, ...], ...]
  • Sheets create: {status: "created", spreadsheetId, title, spreadsheetUrl}
  • Docs create: {status: "created", documentId, title, url}
  • Docs append: {status: "appended", documentId, inserted_at, characters}

Rules

  1. Never send email, create/delete calendar events, delete Drive files, share files, or modify Docs/Sheets without confirming with the user first. Show what will be done (recipients, file IDs, content, share role) and ask for approval. For drive delete, prefer the default trash (reversible) over --permanent.
  2. Check auth before first use — run setup.py --check. If it fails, guide the user through setup.
  3. Use the Gmail search syntax reference for complex queries — load it with skill_view("google-workspace", file_path="references/gmail-search-syntax.md").
  4. Calendar times must include timezone — always use ISO 8601 with offset (e.g., 2026-03-01T10:00:00-06:00) or UTC (Z).
  5. Respect rate limits — avoid rapid-fire sequential API calls. Batch reads when possible.

Troubleshooting

Problem Fix
NOT_AUTHENTICATED Run setup Steps 2-5 above
REFRESH_FAILED Token revoked or expired — redo Steps 3-5
HttpError 403: Insufficient Permission Missing API scope — $GSETUP --revoke then redo Steps 3-5
AUTHENTICATED (partial) or "Token missing scopes" New write capabilities (Drive write/delete, Docs create/edit) require re-authorization. $GSETUP --revoke then redo Steps 3-5 to grant the upgraded scopes.
HttpError 403: Access Not Configured API not enabled — user needs to enable it in Google Cloud Console
ModuleNotFoundError Run $GSETUP --install-deps
Advanced Protection blocks auth Workspace admin must allowlist the OAuth client ID

Revoking Access

$GSETUP --revoke

Naming skills + crons

Formula (Louis approved)

Dept-Stage-# short title
  • Dept = People | POS | Money | Ops | Brain
  • Stage = one word (Onboard, Sales, Fraud, Staffing, Health…)
  • # = step number in that dept/stage
  • short title = what it does (plain English)
  • Max ~15 words, a 10-year-old can understand
  • No emoji · no P1–P4 · no “v2”

Example

People-Onboard-#2 Create 7shift logins
= People dept · Onboard stage · step 2 · make 7shifts logins

Skills (tools) stay separate

area-job only: pos-chowbus, people-shifts-accounts, people-recruiting, brain-data-health
(Crons call skills; skill names are not the cron list names.)

Wiserise Form Maker

⛔ Owner gate (Louis locked 2026-07-29; OPS confirm 2026-07-28 — Luna form rights)

Who may run this skill: Louis (U08TW3FEDNE) or Luna (U0AP162P3KM) on WISE OPS or WISE BRAIN.

Can do Louis Luna GM / store / HQ OPS floor
Draft / revise company form ✅ ✅ ❌
Approve publish (“yes / approve / 改一下表格 / publish”) ✅ ✅ ❌
Publish live PDF + Brain ✅ ✅ ❌
Hermes settings / code / plugins ✅ ❌ ❌

If GM / AGM / manager / HQ OPS / any store asker (not Louis, not Luna) requests create, write, approve, or publish a form:

  • Stop. Do not build HTML, reserve numbers, or publish.
  • Do not treat their “yes / approve” as publish approval.
  • Reply with the professional HQ-only refuse script in wiserise-store-channel-policy / wise_ops SOUL.md.
  • Offer playbook lookup only.
  • New form need → redirect to Louis or Luna.

Makes an HTML form that people fill in and sign by hand. Print-first. Same navy+gold brand as the SOP maker, but instead of step cards you get FORM FIELDS: blank lines, checkboxes, tables, and a signature block. HTML only.

This skill reuses the SOP skill's engine — one source of truth: sop_registry.py, sop_publish.py, sop_builder.py. Only form_html_builder.py is new.

Architecture (3 Pillars + 4 Utilities)

Load wiserise-architecture for the full framework. Key rules for Forms:

Pillar/Utility Form Role Rule
🧠 Brain (Supabase) Source of truth for form numbers, content, status, PDF link sops table = one ledger. Never read form data from Sheets or Obsidian as truth.
⚡ Hermes Sole worker — builds HTML, runs voice check, publishes This skill tells Hermes how. No sub-agents.
💬 Slack Where Louis or Luna approves publishing Human gate: never publish without explicit owner yes in Slack.
📊 Sheets View only — form index can show as a dashboard Never enter form data into Sheets directly. Brain → Sheet auto-refresh.
📓 Obsidian Knowledge wiki — forms referenced here as living docs Push from Brain. If Obsidian dies, Brain still has the data.
📁 Drive Original PDFs — the signed/legal copy Push from Brain (sop_publish uploads to org-files bucket). If Drive dies, annoying, not fatal.
🔬 NotebookLM Research reader — can ingest forms for training Consumes from other pillars. Never a source of truth.

The loop for Forms:

Louis or Luna says "make a form" / "改一下表格" (Slack · WISE BRAIN)
→ Hermes reserves form number from Brain (sop_registry → sops table)
→ Hermes builds HTML (form_html_builder)
→ Hermes shows HTML to the requesting owner for review
→ Louis or Luna approves (Slack human gate ⭐)
→ Hermes publishes (HTML→PDF→Storage→sops row with doc_type='form')
→ Brain updated → Sheet refreshed → Drive PDF saved

Key rule: The Brain (sops table) is the one truth. Drive = legal original. Obsidian = living wiki. Both are push destinations from Brain, never read as source.

First principles — what a form is

A form's only job is to capture information from a person, cleanly, so it can be filed and acted on. Four parts — nothing else:

  1. Identity — what form, its number, who fills it.
  2. How to use — one line: when to fill it, what to do after.
  3. The fields — blanks, boxes, tables to write in.
  4. Proof — signature + date (for any HR / legal / consent form).

No PROCEDURE. No WHAT IF. No checklist JavaScript.

FORM NUMBER (Supabase sops table is the source of truth)

Forms use a SEPARATE number pool from SOPs, with a -F- infix: SERIES-F-### (e.g. TEAM-F-011, SHIFT-F-008). Numbers come live from the Supabase sops table.

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/louisliu/.hermes/skills/wiserise/wiserise-sop")
import sop_registry as reg

form_no = reg.reserve_form("TEAM", "Buddy Check Form", used_at="store")
  • If the form is already live (a rebuild), reuse its existing SERIES-F-###.
  • Brand series (GNG/MAS/LCB) have no form variant — use the shelf series instead (e.g. SHIFT-F-###).

The look (Wiserise brand template)

  1. Header band — navy #152035, white wordmark + "FORM" label. No logo image.
  2. Title — Unna Bold, navy, gold rule.
  3. Info chips — FORM NO | FOR | DATE (DATE is blank).
  4. HOW TO USE — one gold-edge line.
  5. Sections — navy pill headers + fields.
  6. Footer — "WISERISE HOSPITALITY GROUP · CONFIDENTIAL · FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY".

The four field blocks

  • Blank line: {"line": "Full name"} — add "full": True for full width.
  • Checkboxes: {"boxes": "Shirt size:", "options": ["S","M","L","XL"]}
  • Table: {"table": [("Name","32%"), ("Phone","22%")], "rows": 2}
  • Signature block: {"sign": ["Signature", "Print name", "Date"]}

Advanced blocks

  • Grouped table: multi-column groups with color cycling.
  • Panels: color-coded boxes for multi-stage hand-offs.
  • Reason box: {"reason": "Reason for any over / short", "lines": 2}
  • Footer note: {"note": "Only night close checks against POS sales."}

Voice rules (MANDATORY — same as SOPs)

  • Max 15 words per line. build_html() runs the voice check.
  • One idea per line. No jargon. Active voice. Be blunt.
  • Keep field labels short: "CELL PHONE", not "Your cellular telephone number".

How to make one

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/louisliu/.hermes/skills/wiserise/wiserise-form")
sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/louisliu/.hermes/skills/wiserise/wiserise-sop")
import form_html_builder as fb
import sop_registry as reg

title = "Tip Pool Agreement"
form_no = reg.reserve_form("PAY", title, used_at="hq")

sections = [
    {"label": "YOUR INFO", "fields": [
        {"line": "Full name", "full": True},
        {"line": "Store"},
        {"line": "Role"},
    ]},
    {"label": "How tips are split", "fields": [
        {"table": [("Role", "40%"), ("Share %", "30%"), ("Notes", "30%")], "rows": 3},
    ]},
    {"label": "Agree", "fields": [
        {"boxes": "I understand the tip pool:", "options": ["Yes"]},
    ]},
    {"label": "Sign here", "fields": [
        {"sign": ["Signature", "Print name", "Date"]},
    ]},
]
howto = "Read it. Sign it. Give it to your manager."

html = fb.build_html(title, form_no, "All tipped staff", "", sections, howto)
path = f"/Users/louisliu/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/INBOX/{form_no}_Tip-Pool_FORM.html"
fb.save_html(html, path)
print("done", form_no, path)
# Slack review (Louis locked 2026-07-23): always attach .html via MEDIA:
# MEDIA:/abs/path/{form_no}_Short-Name.html
# Same orange HTML card style as Growth-Department.html — all channels.

Slack delivery default (all channels)

After build, always post the .html file with MEDIA: in the review message.
Never “open outside only.” PDF only if Louis asks print.

⭐ Publish to the Playbook page (HUMAN GATE — always get approval)

HARD RULE: never publish without Louis or Luna’s explicit approval.

Valid owner yes phrases (examples): yes · approve · publish · 改一下表格 · 发版 · 上线.

import sop_publish as pub
import form_html_builder as fb

content = fb.sections_to_text(title, howto, sections)
form_id, file_url = pub.publish_sop(
    html_path, title=title, sop_no=form_no, rows=[],
    content=content, brand_key="company", doc_type="form",
    audience="staff", synonyms="tip pool, tips, gratuity",
)
  • ALWAYS set audience. staff = everyone fills it. manager = manager-only.
  • After publish, set registry status 🔨 building → ✅ live.
  • Either owner may approve; do not wait for the other owner unless they ask.

Do NOT auto-publish. No exceptions. GM/store “yes” never counts.

Slack Notification Format

When posting form status to Slack (approval request, publish confirmation), follow slack-message-structure:

📋 *FORM — {Title} / {Brand}*
FORM NO: {form_no}
Status: 🔨 Building / ✅ Live
Type: FORM
Audience: Staff / Manager
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

⛔ Never show terminal output, Python scripts, or curl commands in Slack. The human only sees the result — form number, status, and next step. Use execute_code silently.

Brain → Utility Push Map

Action Brain (sops table) Drive (org-files bucket) Obsidian Sheets
Reserve number status='building', doc_type='form' row — — —
Build HTML — — — —
Publish (approved ⭐) status='live', file_url set, content set PDF uploaded Wiki push (future) Index refreshed
Rebuild Same row updated Old PDF removed, new uploaded Wiki updated —

All data flows Brain → outward. Never read from Drive/Obsidian/Sheets as source for form operations.

Shared Python Scripts

SOP scripts (under ~/.hermes/skills/wiserise/wiserise-sop/):

Script Purpose Lines
sop_builder.py Voice rules (JARGON dict, MAX_WORDS=15), brand colors. Shared by both SOP and Form skills. 455
sop_registry.py Numbering from Supabase. next_free_form(), reserve_form(). 128
sop_publish.py HTML→PDF→Storage→sops row. publish_sop(). Works for forms too. 171

Form scripts (under ~/.hermes/skills/wiserise/wiserise-form/):

Script Purpose Lines
form_html_builder.py Print-and-write HTML form builder. Imports JARGON + MAX_WORDS from sop_builder. build_html(), sections_to_text(), save_html(). 474

Cross-skill dependency: form_html_builder.py imports from sop_builder.py via sys.path pointing at the sibling wiserise-sop directory.

Common Pitfalls

  1. Publishing without approval. Always ask Louis first. No exceptions.
  2. Skipping the voice check. If check_voice() reports problems, fix them.
  3. Making forms more than 1 page. The PDF must fit on one page. Compact the sections.
  4. Inventing form numbers. Always use sop_registry.reserve_form(). Never make up a number.
  5. Using brand series for forms. GNG/MAS/LCB have no -F- variant. Use shelf series (SHIFT-F, TEAM-F, etc.).
  6. Terminal output in Slack. Never show curl, Python, or shell commands. Only the result.
  7. Missing signature block. If the form is HR/legal/consent → must have a signature block.

Done checklist

  • [ ] Voice check passed — every label/line ≤15 words, no jargon
  • [ ] HTML only — no .docx made
  • [ ] Brand template: navy band + white wordmark + FORM tag
  • [ ] Four parts: identity, how-to-use, fields, signature (if needed)
  • [ ] Clean on phone AND paper; PDF is 1 page
  • [ ] Shown IN Slack as .html file attachment (MEDIA:) — all channels default
  • [ ] Asked Louis for approval BEFORE publishing
  • [ ] Brain (sops table) is the one truth — no data read from Sheets/Obsidian/Drive
  • [ ] No terminal output shown in Slack replies

Skills Organization & Permissions

Organize ~/.hermes/skills/ by domain, tag each skill with a permission level, and configure per-platform access so the team only sees safe skills.

When to Use

  • User asks to reorganize or clean up their skills folder
  • User asks to control which skills the team can access on Slack/other platforms
  • User asks to pin skills so they aren't archived
  • User asks to create sidebar project shortcuts for skill domains
  • After large reorg/installs: rebuild Skill Dojo browse map (skill-library-navigation + references/skill-dojo.md)

First-Principles Folder Structure

Skills have 3 natural dimensions:

  1. Domain (WHAT) — coding, finance, people, security, etc.
  2. Permission (WHO) — louis-only vs team-safe
  3. Maturity (HOW RELIABLE) — pinned/production vs experimental vs archived

Rule: Domain = folders (how you browse). Permission = metadata (how you filter).

Current Domain Layout

~/.hermes/skills/
├── wiserise/       Core Wiserise system (wise-brain, wiserise-os, loi-agent, slack-msg)
├── finance/        Finance dept (wiserise-form, polymarket)
├── people/         People/HR dept (wiserise-sop)
├── coding/         Dev tools (plan, spike, TDD, debugging, ponytail)
├── agents/         AI delegation (claude-code, codex, hermes-agent, opencode)
├── github/         GitHub workflows (auth, PRs, issues, review)
├── security/       1Password, secrets
├── research/       Papers, feeds, wikis
├── productivity/   Docs, decks, maps, OCR
├── comms/          Messaging, notes, email
├── apple/          macOS system tools (findmy, computer-use)
└── _archive/       Inactive/experimental (curator-managed)

Version + Updated Frontmatter (required on all skills)

Every active SKILL.md MUST have version: and updated: in frontmatter. This was batch-added to all 118 active skills on 2026-08-01.

---
name: my-skill
version: 1.0.0
updated: 2026-08-01 22:10
---

Rules: - updated: = date of last edit (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format) - version: = semantic version; bump minor on meaningful changes, patch on small fixes - Bump updated: on EVERY edit — this is how stale skills are detected - The Skill Health Report (weekly cron) flags any skill not updated in 90+ days as stale - When you create a new skill, set version: 1.0.0 + updated: to today

Batch-add to missing skills (shell one-liner):

cd ~/.hermes/skills
find . -name "SKILL.md" -not -path "*/.archive/*" | while read f; do
  fm=$(awk '/^---$/{p++; next} p==1{print}' "$f")
  ver=$(echo "$fm" | grep -iE '^version:' | head -1)
  upd=$(echo "$fm" | grep -iE '^updated:' | head -1)
  [ -n "$upd" ] && continue  # already has updated
  mtime=$(stat -f "%Sm" -t "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M" "$f")
  if [ -z "$ver" ]; then
    closing=$(awk '/^---$/{c++; if(c==2){print NR; exit}}' "$f")
    sed -i '' "${closing}i\\\version: 1.0.0\\\nupdated: ${mtime}\n" "$f"
  else
    ver_line=$(awk '/^---$/{p++; next} p==1 && /^[Vv]ersion:/{print NR; exit}' "$f")
    sed -i '' "${ver_line}a\\\updated: ${mtime}\n" "$f"
  fi
done

Permissions — Binary, No Per-Department

First principle (Louis confirmed 2026-08-01): Hermes only supports louis-only vs team-safe. Building per-department permissions adds complexity for no real payoff — your team is small. Don't over-engineer.

The rule: - Store-facing skills (recruiting, playbook, purchase, my-job, ops-issue-intake, roster-sync, scheduling) → team-safe - Everything else → louis-only - If a GM shouldn't see it, it's louis-only. Done.

Do NOT create per-department permission tiers. Do NOT add finance-only or people-only — there's no mechanism for it and no need.

Permission Metadata

Step 1: Add permission: to SKILL.md frontmatter

---
name: my-skill
permission: louis-only    # or: team-safe
---

Insert before the closing --- of frontmatter. Use a Python script to batch-add:

# Find second ---, insert permission line before it
first_end = content.find("---")
second_start = content.find("---", first_end + 3)
frontmatter_body = content[first_end + 3:second_start]
new_frontmatter = frontmatter_body.rstrip("\n") + f"\npermission: {perm}\n"
new_content = content[:first_end + 3] + new_frontmatter + content[second_start:]

Step 2: Configure platform blocklist in config.yaml

skills:
  platform_disabled:
    slack:
      - agents/claude-code
      - security/1password
      # ... all louis-only skills

How it works: - CLI (Louis) sees ALL skills - Slack (team) sees only skills NOT in the platform_disabled.slack list - The agent's skill loader unions global disabled + platform-specific platform_disabled.<platform> at session start

To edit: hermes config edit → add skills.platform_disabled.slack list. Cannot use hermes skills config from non-interactive terminals.

Curator Pinning

Only agent-created (local) skills can be pinned. Bundled/hub-installed skills are already protected from archival.

hermes curator pin <skill-name>    # protect from auto-archive
hermes curator unpin <skill-name>  # allow curator to manage again
hermes curator status              # see what's active/stale

What pinning does

  • ✅ Prevents curator from auto-archiving after 90 days idle
  • ✅ Protects from consolidation (LLM merge pass)
  • ❌ Does NOT sort to top of sidebar
  • ❌ Does NOT affect load order

What pinning does NOT do

  • Does not work on bundled/hub skills (they're already safe)
  • Does not make skills load faster or appear first

Sidebar Projects

Create Hermes desktop projects to pin skill domains in the sidebar:

# In Hermes chat (or use project_create tool):
project_create(name="🏢 Wiserise", path="~/.hermes/skills/wiserise")
project_create(name="💰 Finance", path="~/.hermes/skills/finance")
# ... etc

Pitfall: Creating too many projects clutters the sidebar. Keep it to domains you actively work in. For reference-only domains, skip the project — use open ~/.hermes/skills/<domain>/ in Finder instead.

Pitfall: Do NOT create projects for skill folders (~/.hermes/skills/*). Skills are accessible from the Skills sidebar. A project per skill domain = 12+ extra sidebar items that are just folders, not real workspaces. Only create projects for real working directories (e.g. ~/Dev/Wiserise_OS, ~/Dev/Agents/4-PEOPLE).

Adding a New Skill

  1. Create in the right domain folder: ~/.hermes/skills/<domain>/<name>/SKILL.md
  2. Add permission: louis-only or permission: team-safe to frontmatter
  3. Add version: 1.0.0 and updated: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM to frontmatter
  4. If louis-only → add to Slack blocklist in config.yaml under skills.platform_disabled.slack
  5. If agent-created and critical → hermes curator pin <name>
  6. Restart gateway (/restart or hermes gateway restart) for config changes to reach team

Hub installs → domain folders (required)

hermes skills install often creates ~/.hermes/skills/<skill-name>/ at skills root. Move immediately:

mv ~/.hermes/skills/grill-me ~/.hermes/skills/productivity/
mv ~/.hermes/skills/grilling ~/.hermes/skills/productivity/
mv ~/.hermes/skills/grill-with-docs ~/.hermes/skills/coding/
# add permission: louis-only on each SKILL.md
python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/wiserise/skill_dojo_rebuild.py

Permission pass (batch unset)

When tagging unset: most tool domains → louis-only; wiserise store-facing → team-safe; owner-sensitive wiserise (SOP/form/LOI/bank/inbox/termination/architecture) → louis-only. Frontmatter ≠ Slack hide — still update platform_disabled.slack.

Sync louis-only → Slack blocklist

  1. Backup config.yaml
  2. Rescan active (non-_archive) skills with permission: louis-only
  3. Rewrite skills.platform_disabled.slack as relative paths (domain/name)
  4. Keep legacy aliases if needed: wiserise/wise-brain, wiserise/wiserise-os, people/wiserise-sop, finance/wiserise-form
  5. Match YAML indent (platform_disabled: → 4-space slack: → 6-space list items)
  6. /restart or hermes gateway restart

Cold archive (only with Louis yes / “do all recommendations”)

Move 0-use, non-core, unpinned → ~/.hermes/skills/_archive/<domain>/<name>/. Keep company core, grill pack, any-use tools, invest routers Louis still wants. Dojo Archive tier still lists them.

Skill Dojo rebuild

python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/wiserise/skill_dojo_rebuild.py
bash ~/.hermes/scripts/wiserise/skills_install_and_rebuild.sh <id> -y   # prefer after hub install

v3.2 (Elon 5-step 2026-08-01): Earn rent first; Top 20 ranked by actual usage (not locked — dead skills removed); Catalog = professional table; disk truth not Brain/GitHub skills; outputs artifacts+Desktop+Pages. Spec: references/skill-dojo.md.

Common Pitfalls

  1. Moving skills within the same category folder. Same-dir mv fails. Already-correct domain → only add metadata.
  2. Pinning bundled skills. Cannot pin hub/bundled — already curator-safe.
  3. Non-interactive hermes skills config. Edit config.yaml directly from agent.
  4. Sidebar clutter from too many projects. Real workspaces only — not skill folders.
  5. Forgetting to restart gateway after config changes.
  6. Duplicate project names. Use emoji prefixes.
  7. Hub skill left at skills root. Always mv + permission + rebuild Dojo.
  8. Equal weight to 170+ skills. Top 20 should reflect actual usage — don't lock dead skills in Earn Rent. Elon step 1 (2026-08-01): removed grill-me/grilling (0 uses), replaced with clear-simple-bullets + wiserise-people.
  9. louis-only without Slack blocklist. Does not hide from team Slack.
  10. Earn Rent locked order. ~~Lock company core order.~~ WRONG — locked order protects dead skills. Rank by actual usage. If a Top 20 skill hits 0 uses, replace it.
  11. Stale Dojo after hub install. Use skills_install_and_rebuild.sh or rebuild immediately.
  12. Ghost skills in .usage.json. Archived skills remain state: active in .usage.json even after moving to .archive/. Any script reading usage data MUST filter by disk reality (rglob('SKILL.md') excluding .archive/), not trust the state field. 68 of 181 entries were ghosts on 2026-08-01.
  13. Missing desktop copy. Nightly Dojo cron must cp HTML to ~/Desktop/Skill-Dojo.html after build. Without it, the desktop deliverable is stale/missing.

Verification Checklist

  • [ ] Every active SKILL.md has permission: louis-only or team-safe
  • [ ] Every active SKILL.md has version: and updated: in frontmatter
  • [ ] platform_disabled.slack covers louis-only skills
  • [ ] No hub packs at ~/.hermes/skills/<name>/ root
  • [ ] Skill Dojo rebuilt (Desktop + Pages); Earn rent tab reflects actual usage
  • [ ] Config backup before blocklist edits
  • [ ] Scripts reading .usage.json filter by disk reality (ghost skills pitfall)
  • [ ] Nightly Dojo cron copies HTML to ~/Desktop/Skill-Dojo.html

Browse UI (not a second org system)

Skill Dojo = HTML map (earn-rent + search + domain + permission + cold debt). Layout truth = folders + frontmatter here. Rebuild via script; don’t hand-edit skill rows. See skill-library-navigation.

Cleaning Up Cluttered Projects (projects.db)

When the sidebar gets too many projects (from accidental skill-folder projects, auto-discovered repos, or duplicates), edit projects.db directly.

Location & Schema

~/.hermes/projects.db  (SQLite)

Tables: - projects — id (p_), name, slug, primary_path, archived, created_at - project_folders — project_id (FK CASCADE), path, is_primary - project_meta — key-value; active_id points to the current active project - discovered_repos — root (path), label, last_seen (auto-discovered git repos)

Safe to Delete Projects

Sessions (state.db → sessions table) do NOT store project_id. They are grouped by cwd path matching. So deleting a project does NOT orphan sessions — they re-associate with remaining or auto-discovered projects.

Kanban tasks (kanban.db → tasks table) DO have an optional project_id column. Check before deleting: SELECT project_id, COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY project_id;

Cleanup Procedure

  1. Backup: cp ~/.hermes/projects.db ~/.hermes/projects.db.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
  2. Check kanban references: sqlite3 ~/.hermes/kanban.db "SELECT project_id, COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY project_id;"
  3. Delete projects (CASCADE removes project_folders rows): sql BEGIN; DELETE FROM projects WHERE id IN ('p_xxx', 'p_yyy'); UPDATE project_meta SET value = 'p_zzz' WHERE key = 'active_id'; -- if active project was deleted COMMIT;
  4. Clean discovered_repos of any parent folders that spawned bad auto-projects
  5. Disable repo discovery (prevent the gray book-icon list from regrowing): sql UPDATE project_meta SET value = '{"enabled":false,"exclude_paths":[],"roots":[]}' WHERE key = 'repo_discovery_policy';
  6. Verify: sqlite3 ~/.hermes/projects.db "SELECT id, name, primary_path FROM projects ORDER BY name;"
  7. Verify via API: project_list tool should show the clean list
  8. Restart Hermes desktop for sidebar to refresh

Reference: references/projects-db-cleanup.md — full schema, safety checks, SQL, and repo-discovery disable from two real cleanup sessions (2026-07-10 22→9, 2026-07-29 9→2).

Step 4 — Script / no_agent jobs

  • Fix print/post text inside the script to v3 parent (English). jobs.json prompt alone is not enough when no_agent=true — the script owns the Slack body.
  • Prefer post_parent_thread from slack_channel_format.py (parent short; names/rules/examples → thread with SEP).

  • Examples: token_spend_watch_cron.py, fraud/reviews/HR poll, people_wages_nudge_00003.py (People-Wages-#1).

Step 4b — Louis points at one bad live message

Treat as a format lock, not a one-off rewrite of the sample text:

  1. Identify profile (wise_ops vs default) + job name + script path
  2. Rewrite script Slack strings → English + v3 (3-line parent + thread)
  3. Confirm shape in cron-notification-pack.md (add if missing)
  4. Grep that script for remaining user-facing Chinese in posted strings
  5. Never leave Chinese titles like 每日提醒 / 时薪未填完 on cron channel parents

Step 4c — Strip competing legacy FORMAT blocks from agent prompts

Critical. WISE OPS agent cron prompts still hid legacy blocks that the model treated as the message format:

FORMAT (Louis locked 2026-07-21 — ALL channels — match HR screenshot):
- Final Slack message = SHORT parent only:
  TITLE line
  • one bullet per item (max ~6)
  optional last line: ⏰ N more → thread  OR  details in thread
- No Cronjob Response / job_id / terminal / long From-Subject-Summary walls.
- If already inside a home thread: short title + ≤6 bullets + ▬ divider.
- High-school English. Silent/[SILENT] when nothing new.

Also watch for:

MESSAGE:
MESSAGE SHAPE:
{3-line bullet + ▬ divider block}

These blocks competed against the v3 footer and won because the model saw them as an explicit format directive, not as a "competing" block.

Fix: For every agent Slack-facing job's .prompt, grep for these patterns and delete the entire block. No partial fix — the whole thing must go. Also strip any ▬▬▬ divider characters that survived (v3 separator is -------------------------------------).

After stripping, inject a per-job LOCKED SLACK PARENT block at the end (before footer). See references/locked-parent-shapes.md for canonical shapes per job name.

Step 4d — Remove clear-simple-bullets from cron skill lists

This skill contains Chinese example text (e.g. 私下谈一次, 小孩都能懂, 太复杂, 链接看不清楚) that bleeds into cron Slack output when the model reads the loaded skill text looking for "how to write." Every Slack-facing agent cron must remove clear-simple-bullets from its skills array. The v3 footer + per-job locked shape already enforce English + concise output — no extra style skill needed.

Also audit for other skills that contain Chinese keywords that could leak: people-recruiting, brain-slack-chat, pos-fraud, wiserise-exec-inbox (already cleaned). Only keep them on a cron if the cron's business logic requires loading them (e.g. pos-fraud needs data queries). If a cron only uses a skill for style/formatting → strip it.

Step 5 — Verify before claiming saved

For each agent Slack job: skill=True and footer=True. Report counts (default N + wise_ops N).
For script jobs: open the .py and confirm parent is WHAT/WHO/WHEN + 👉 + English only.

Pitfalls

  1. Dual-profile clones — wise_ops still has Brain-Chat-#4 (and other clones). Updating only default leaves old digests posting. Always batch both jobs.json.
  2. Wrong day — store chat is today ET, not yesterday (Louis 2026-07-18).
  3. Hermes wrapper — agent deliver=slack: may still prefix Cronjob Response:. Body must still be pure v3; for clean production digests prefer script self-post + deliver=local + empty stdout.
  4. Meta / Chinese in parent — never “拉取完成 / 已存入 Brain / 每日提醒 / 时薪未填完” as the channel message. Louis 2026-07-26 + 2026-07-27: English only, always, including wise_ops people/store scripts.
  5. Missing owner — never post without 👉 @person. Defaults: Louis exec/bank/legal · Sally people/HR · Yumi money/ops · store GM day-to-day · Anson marketing.
    #06-people (Louis 2026-08-01): owners = Sally + Louis only. AIlin/Allin = assistant, never owner line. Green roster / no-action People noise = silent.
  6. Pinned skill — slack-message-structure is curator-pinned; autonomous background curator cannot patch its SKILL.md — put new shapes/pitfalls in references/cron-notification-pack.md or this lock skill.
  7. Marketing crons live on wise_ops (#1–#4) — include them in any “all cron” lock.
  8. format_parent_v3 + Slack IDs — helper does owner if startswith("@") else f"@{owner}". Passing "<@U…>" yields broken @<@U…>. Build 👉 <@UID> action yourself, or pass a name already starting with @. Reference: people_wages_nudge_00003.py local parent_v3().
  9. Long parent — sample name lists, completion rules, “OPS does not change rates” go in thread, not channel parent (Louis: “need slack message structure format”).
  10. Script body divergence across profiles — wise_ops may have the v3 rewrite while the default ~/.hermes/scripts/ copy still has the old long-form post. The cron runner may execute either copy depending on profile/workdir. When Louis flags a bad live message, always md5 both copies and sync the fixed one to both paths. Don't assume one profile is the live one — the bad post может come from the other. Example (2026-07-27): shifts_accounts_2h.py wise_ops had _post_7shifts_digest v3 but default still posted ✅ 7shifts Account Created — … 8-line block; bad Slack came from default. Fix: cp wise_ops/scripts/X.py ~/.hermes/scripts/X.py after verifying syntax + --format-preview.
  11. v3 function defined but not called — a script can have _post_digest() v3 code but still post old format because main() was never wired to call it. When locking a script, grep for _post_ and confirm main() actually calls it. Don't just check that the function exists — check the call site.

Digest pitfalls (from 2026-08-01 build)

  1. Cron script field with args — Hermes cron script= may not pass CLI args. Use a thin wrapper: os.environ["DEPT_DIGEST_CYCLE"] = "afternoon" + runpy.run_path().

When to Use

  • "train GM" / "start GM train" / "GM training"

First principles (always)

A restaurant dies from only 3 floor jobs. The store also needs 1 OS job (how managers talk to the company system). Train only these — do not invent a fourth “framework.”
